Company: Lawrence Harvey | Part of LHi Group
Industry: Emerging Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data, Cybersecurity & Business Transformation
Position: Entry-Level Sales Development Representative (SDR) / Recruitment Consultant
Base Salary: $50,000 + $10,000 Guaranteed Commission + Uncapped Commission
Average First-Year Earnings (OTE): $70,000–$80,000+
Experience: Entry-Level | No Previous Sales or Recruitment Experience Required
Training: 12-Week Structured Sales & Recruitment Training Program

Launch Your Sales Career in Los Angeles

Looking for an entry-level SDR job in Los Angeles where your ambition, communication skills, and sales performance can directly influence your earnings and career progression?

Lawrence Harvey, part of LHi Group, is hiring an Entry-Level Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our team in Santa Monica, Los Angeles.

This opportunity is ideal for recent college graduates, aspiring sales professionals, career changers, and individuals with experience in customer service, hospitality, retail, or other customer-facing roles who want to transition into a professional sales career.

You'll develop valuable skills in B2B sales, business development, lead generation, cold calling, client acquisition, negotiation, and consultative selling, while building relationships with companies and professionals across emerging technology and business transformation markets.

Unlike a traditional SDR position focused exclusively on qualifying leads, this role provides the opportunity to develop into a full-cycle sales and recruitment consultant, managing client relationships, negotiating deals, and earning commission through successful placements.

No previous sales, recruitment, or technology industry experience is required.

We provide comprehensive training, ongoing mentorship, and a clear pathway for career progression.

If you're competitive, motivated by financial rewards, enjoy connecting with people, and want to build a long-term career in sales, we'd love to hear from you.

What Does an Entry-Level SDR Do at Lawrence Harvey?

As an Entry-Level Sales Development Representative, you'll learn how to generate new business opportunities and develop relationships with organizations hiring specialist technology professionals.

Your role combines B2B sales, business development, talent acquisition, and relationship management.

You'll identify prospective clients, conduct outbound sales outreach, build professional relationships, and connect businesses with specialist talent across technology and business transformation.

As your experience develops, you'll gradually take ownership of the complete recruitment sales cycle, from initial prospecting and lead generation through to client management, candidate placement, and successful deal completion.

This is a sales-driven, revenue-generating position with uncapped commission potential, rather than an internal HR or administrative recruiting role.

From day one, you'll receive structured training and coaching to develop your sales confidence, commercial awareness, and specialist industry knowledge.

Why Lawrence Harvey? Sales Careers in Emerging Technology

Lawrence Harvey specializes in recruitment across Emerging Technology, Technology and Business Transformation, connecting organizations with professionals who help them innovate, grow, and navigate change.

We work with businesses seeking specialist talent across some of the most commercially important and evolving areas of technology.

Our specialist recruitment markets include:

• Artificial Intelligence (AI): AI technologies, machine learning, and intelligent automation.
• Data & Analytics: Data engineering, data science, business intelligence, and data-driven transformation.
• Cybersecurity: Information security, cloud security, and cyber risk.
• Cloud Computing: Cloud infrastructure, cloud engineering, and digital modernization.
• Technology & Engineering: Specialist engineering, software, and technical transformation.
• Business Transformation: Technology-enabled change, digital transformation, and business improvement.

As an SDR specializing in emerging technology recruitment, you'll develop commercial expertise while building relationships with organizations investing in technology, innovation, and business transformation.

You'll learn how businesses identify and hire specialist professionals, understand emerging industry trends, and develop a network of clients and candidates.

This is an opportunity to combine a career in sales and business development with exposure to technology markets that are shaping how businesses operate.

You don't need a technology background to succeed. We'll provide the specialist market training and support you need to develop your industry knowledge and commercial skills.

Why Join LHi Group?

Lawrence Harvey is part of LHi Group, a global, 100% employee-owned specialist talent solutions business.

Joining our Los Angeles team means becoming part of an ambitious, collaborative environment where performance, professional development, and long-term career progression are encouraged.

Here's what makes LHi Group different:

• Employee Ownership: Join a 100% employee-owned business where employees have a stake in the company's long-term success.
• Sales Training & Development: Benefit from structured sales and recruitment training, ongoing mentorship, and practical coaching.
• Merit-Based Career Progression: Build your career through performance, professional development, and ambition.
• International Opportunities: With offices across the US, UK, and Europe, international career development opportunities may be available.
• Specialist Industry Expertise: Develop valuable commercial knowledge and professional networks within emerging technology and business transformation.
• Collaborative Sales Culture: Work alongside motivated colleagues in an environment that recognizes achievement, encourages teamwork, and celebrates success.

Salary, Commission & Benefits – Los Angeles SDR Jobs

We offer a competitive compensation package designed to reward ambition, performance, and professional growth.

Competitive Compensation & Uncapped Commission

• $50,000 annual base salary
• $10,000 guaranteed commission during training, paid biweekly
• Uncapped performance-based commission
• Average first-year total earnings of $70,000–$80,000+, including base salary and commission
• Opportunities to increase earnings as your sales performance and experience develop

Generous Paid Time Off

• 20+ days of paid time off
• 13 company holidays including your birthday off
• 5 sick days
• 2 Mind & Body Days
• 1 volunteering day
• Summer Fridays

Comprehensive Employee Benefits

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) retirement plan with company match
• Commuter benefits
• Employee Assistance Program
• Employee ownership opportunities, including eligibility for shareholder equity after 12 months

Sales Training & Career Development

• Structured 12-week sales and recruitment training program
• Ongoing one-on-one coaching from your manager
• Hands-on B2B sales and business development training
• Cold calling, prospecting, and lead generation development
• Negotiation and closing training

Key Responsibilities – Entry-Level Sales Development Representative

As an Entry-Level SDR at Lawrence Harvey, you'll learn how to identify new business opportunities, develop client relationships, and generate revenue through specialist technology recruitment solutions.

Your responsibilities will include:

Outbound Sales & Lead Generation

• Identify prospective clients and generate new business opportunities within emerging technology and business transformation markets.
• Conduct outbound prospecting through cold calls, emails, LinkedIn, networking, and other outreach strategies.
• Build and manage a pipeline of prospective clients and business opportunities.
• Research target companies, decision-makers, technology hiring trends, and emerging market opportunities.

Business Development & Client Acquisition

• Develop relationships with prospective clients and understand their specialist technology recruitment needs.
• Introduce Lawrence Harvey's recruitment services to new businesses.
• Learn consultative selling techniques to identify client challenges and provide tailored recruitment solutions.
• Support new business development and contribute to the growth of your specialist technology market.

Candidate Sourcing & Talent Acquisition

• Research emerging technology trends, specialist hiring needs, and industry developments.
• Develop commercial knowledge and build your professional reputation within your specialist market.

You'll receive ongoing support as you learn, with increasing responsibility as your confidence, skills, and sales performance develop.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for ambitious, motivated, and commercially minded individuals who want to build a successful career in sales, business development, and technology recruitment consulting.

You don't need previous SDR, BDR, sales, recruitment, or technology industry experience to apply.

You could be a great fit if you're:

• Relationship-Focused: Enjoy connecting with people and building long-term professional relationships.
• Coachable: Open to feedback, ongoing training, and continuous improvement.
• Goal-Oriented: Energized by targets and motivated to achieve individual and team-based objectives.
• Team-Oriented: Embody LHi Group's Good Human ethos by contributing to a positive, supportive, and collaborative environment.
• Interested in Technology: Excited by the opportunity to develop knowledge of AI, Data, Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, and emerging technologies.

Previous Experience That Could Be Relevant

Experience in any of the following areas may be beneficial, but is not required:

• Sales or business development
• Customer service
• Hospitality or retail
• Account management
• Marketing or lead generation
• Recruiting or talent acquisition
• Other customer-facing or target-driven positions

Recent graduates, career changers, and candidates without a university degree are encouraged to apply.

We hire for attitude, ambition, communication skills, and willingness to learn.

SDR Training & Sales Career Progression

We don't expect you to know everything about sales, recruitment, or technology when you join Lawrence Harvey.

Our 12-week structured sales and recruitment training program is designed to help you develop the commercial skills needed to succeed.

Your training will cover:

• B2B sales fundamentals
• Outbound prospecting and cold calling
• Lead generation and pipeline development
• Business development and client acquisition
• Consultative selling and relationship building
• Candidate sourcing, screening, and interviewing
• Client relationship and account management
• Objection handling and negotiation
• Sales closing techniques
• Market mapping and industry research
• Professional networking and personal branding
• Emerging technology and business transformation market knowledge

You'll receive hands-on coaching, regular feedback, and ongoing support from experienced recruitment consultants and sales leaders.

Sales & Recruitment Career Path

Unlike traditional SDR positions where responsibilities are often focused primarily on lead generation, this opportunity provides a pathway into full-cycle sales, client management, and specialist recruitment consulting.

A potential career path includes:

Entry-Level SDR / Recruitment Consultant → Recruitment Consultant → Senior Recruitment Consultant → Principal Consultant or Team Leader

Further progression opportunities may include senior individual contributor positions, team management, and leadership roles, depending on your performance, development, and ambitions.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I Need Previous SDR or Sales Experience?

No. This is an entry-level sales and recruitment opportunity.

You'll receive structured training and ongoing coaching to develop your sales, business development, and recruitment skills.

Is This a Traditional SDR Position?

Not exactly.

While you'll develop core SDR skills such as cold calling, lead generation, prospecting, and client acquisition, this position also provides the opportunity to manage the full recruitment sales cycle.

You'll learn how to develop client relationships, source candidates, negotiate offers, and earn commission through successful placements.

Is Technology Recruitment a Sales Career?

Yes. Technology recruitment consulting is a commercially focused career involving B2B sales, business development, relationship management, and revenue generation.

You'll work with clients and candidates, build your professional network, and earn commission through successful recruitment placements.

Do I Need a College Degree?

No. A university degree is not required.

We welcome recent graduates, career changers, and individuals who have developed relevant skills through previous employment or other experiences.

How Much Can an Entry-Level SDR Earn in Los Angeles?

This position offers a $50,000 annual base salary plus $10,000 in guaranteed commission during training, paid biweekly.

You'll also have the opportunity to earn uncapped performance-based commission.

Average first-year total earnings are $70,000–$80,000+, including base salary and commission. Actual earnings depend on individual performance.

Do I Need a Technology Background?

No. Previous experience in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data, cloud computing, or technology recruitment is not required.

You'll receive specialist market training to help you understand the industry, develop professional relationships, and identify commercial opportunities.

Where Is This SDR Position Located?

This position is based in Santa Monica, Los Angeles, California, within Lawrence Harvey's Los Angeles team.

Location: Chicago, IL

About the team

SumUp’s Field Sales team is on the ground, expanding into new markets across the country and building real relationships with the small and medium-sized businesses that power local communities.

Every day, our team meets merchants face-to-face, helping them discover payment and loyalty solutions that can make running and growing their businesses easier.

As an Outside Sales Senior Account Executive, you’ll take ownership of your territory, manage the full sales cycle, and become a trusted face of SumUp for the merchants you serve. With the support of your Team Lead and Regional Manager, you’ll have the autonomy to build your pipeline, close new business, and grow your earnings.

What you'll do

• Own your territory by building and managing a strong sales pipeline through prospecting, canvassing, referrals, and relationships with local businesses.

• Manage the full sales cycle from cold outreach and door-to-door prospecting through discovery, product demonstrations, negotiation, and close.

• Build meaningful merchant relationships by understanding each business, identifying its needs, and recommending the right SumUp solutions.

• Work strategically by researching your territory, identifying high-potential opportunities, and prioritizing your time effectively.

• Stay on top of your pipeline using Salesforce to track activity, manage opportunities, and maintain clear and consistent follow-up.

• Be a local ambassador for SumUp by confidently representing our payment and loyalty solutions and showing merchants how SumUp can help their businesses thrive.

You'll be great if the following describes you…

• Candidates must have prior sales experience in fintech, payment processing, or point-of-sale (POS) solutions. This is a required qualification, not a preferred one.

• Are comfortable working independently in a field-based, territory-driven sales environment.

• Can connect with people quickly, ask the right questions, listen carefully, and adapt your approach to each merchant.

• Are comfortable with cold outreach and face-to-face prospecting, including visiting local businesses within your territory.

• Have a valid driver’s license and reliable transportation to travel throughout your assigned territory.

• Are self-motivated, resilient, and results-driven, with the ambition to grow your skills, your career, and your earning potential.

Why you should join SumUp

🌍 Make an impact at a global fintech Collaborate with SumUppers around the world on large scale fintech products that help millions of businesses succeed.

💼 US based Customer Experience team in Texas that can support both English and Spanish speaking merchants

📚 Invest in your growth Receive a $2,000 annual learning and development budget to build new skills and support your career development.

💰 Build your financial future Participate in our 401(k) retirement plan with SumUp matching

Compensation

📈 Grow your career and your earnings Take advantage of clear opportunities for career advancement and increased compensation, with growth directly tied to your performance and impact.

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower merchants across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 38 countries rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Our commitment to small businesses is reflected in our diverse team of over 4,000 SumUppers from over 90 nationalities, united by global collaboration and an innovative mindset. Our core values lay the foundation for who we are and what we stand for, shaping our work culture and driving our success. We foster inclusivity and a continuous learning culture, providing a safe space for personal and professional growth. Our differences make us unique and strong as we strive to create an environment where everyone belongs and feels supported, no matter how they identify.

SumUp is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, actively seeking and embracing diversity in our workforce. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by company policy. Our commitment extends beyond recruitment to creating a safe and respectful workplace where harassment of any form is strictly prohibited. Discover more about our culture and opportunities on our careers website, and follow our journey on LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok.

jobs.title: Principal Specialist, HR Change Management
jobs.description:
The Principal Specialist, HR Change Management is Renesas’ principal advisor for enterprise HR transformation and adoption. The role translates complex people, organization, process, policy, and technology priorities into coordinated change programs spanning governance, stakeholder alignment, communications, readiness, enablement, and adoption. Working globally across functions and regions, the role resolves ambiguous change challenges and influences senior stakeholders through expertise rather than direct authority.

Key Responsibilities

• Enterprise change strategy: Define and lead integrated strategies for Renesas-wide HR and organization priorities, covering the case for change, sponsorship, stakeholder analysis, readiness, communications, learning, resistance, reinforcement, and benefits realization.
• Immediate transformation portfolio: Lead change across evolving priorities such as organization simplification, job re-leveling and title cleanup, technical ladder program, rewards and benefits harmonization, HR process standardization, and digital, automation, or AI-enabled ways of working.
• Portfolio governance and delivery: Establish integrated roadmaps, milestones, interdependencies, decision forums, ownership, resource needs, risk escalation, and accountability from design through stabilization.
• Communications and enablement: Translate complex priorities into executive briefings, leader narratives, manager toolkits, presentations, FAQs, digital content, cascade plans, training, and practical support for employee conversations.
• Stakeholder and sponsor alignment: Build coalitions across HR, Legal, Communications, Finance, business functions, and regions; align outcomes, sequencing, and employee impacts while surfacing competing needs early.
• Employee experience and digital engagement: Create accessible channels and self-service resources that provide employees and managers with reliable information, tools, updates, and support throughout the change journey.
• Insights and adoption: Use readiness, adoption, sentiment, service, process, and channel data to remove barriers, refine interventions, demonstrate value, and sustain new behaviors.
• Capability and innovation: Build change capability through coaching, reusable methods, communities of practice, and mentoring, while applying external practices in workforce transformation, digital enablement, and responsible AI.

Scope and Accountability:

• Serves as Renesas’ principal advisor and thought leader for complex, enterprise-scale HR change.
• Partners with senior business and HR leaders to establish strategy, principles, and priorities across functions and geographies.
• Resolves significant and unique issues requiring conceptual thinking, independent judgment, and a long-term view.
• Develops enterprise methods and standards where established approaches are insufficient.
• Owns outcomes affecting the HR function and multiple business areas through expertise, influence, and cross-functional leadership.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent advanced knowledge in Human Resources, Organizational Psychology, Business, Communications, Technology, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
• Typically 12+ years of progressive experience in change management, HR transformation, organization effectiveness, HR technology, or a related discipline, including complex global initiatives.
• Expertise in change strategy, organization transformation, sponsor and stakeholder management, executive communications, enablement, and adoption measurement.
• Experience across people and organization change, including organization redesign, job architecture, career frameworks, rewards or benefits harmonization, HR process transformation, and digital or AI-enabled adoption.
• Proven ability to advise executives and influence outcomes in a global, matrixed, multicultural environment.
• Strong analytical judgment and working knowledge of responsible AI, data privacy, employee relations, and regional consultation requirements.
• Change management certification such as Prosci, CCMP, or equivalent preferred.

Core Capabilities

Enterprise Change Strategy | Portfolio Delivery | Organization and Workforce Transformation | Job Architecture and Career Programs | Rewards and Benefits Change | HR Process and Digital Transformation |  Communications and Manager Enablement | Governance and Risk | Adoption Analytics | Global Collaboration

The expected annual pay range for this position is $200K - $250. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Research Scientist, Visual Reasoning
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The mission of the Waymo AI Foundations team is to develop machine learning solutions addressing open problems in autonomous driving, towards the goal of safely operating Waymo vehicles in dozens of cities and under all driving conditions. As part of our work, we also initiate and foster collaborations with other research teams in Alphabet. AI Foundations areas that we are currently focusing on include reinforcement learning, learning from demonstration, generative modeling, Bayesian inference, hierarchical learning, and robust evaluation.

Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

You will:

• Research and develop novel visual and spatio-temporal reasoning methods for multimodal Perception Foundation Models using AV sensor data

• Design and implement post-training recipes—including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL)—to improve perception generalization in long-tail autonomous driving scenarios

• Conduct large-scale experiments and ablation studies on autonomous driving benchmarks, with the opportunity to publish findings at top-tier AI/CV conferences (e.g., CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML)

You have:

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field

• Hands-on experience & strong publications in perception, and/or LLM/VLM

• Knowledge of pre-training and post-training of the large foundation models

• Strong Python coding skills with expertise in modern deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)

We prefer:

• Experience with visual reasoning for LLM/VLM/robotics/driving

• Experience with RL training in LLM/VLM/robotics

• Experience with open-vocabulary perception

Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in.

The expected hourly rate for this full-time position is listed below. Interns are also eligible to participate in the Company’s generous benefits programs, subject to eligibility requirements.

$85—$85 USD

Job Description

Position: Operations Engineer/ Sr. Operations Engineer (dependent upon experience)

Location: Remote

Overview:

The Operations Engineer provides engineering support across the operating fleet, with a focus on resolving key technical issues, improving plant reliability, and optimizing performance. This role serves as a plant generalist—bridging field execution, engineering analysis, and vendor engagement across the full plant, from the PV array to the point of interconnection. Working alongside the Power Conversion and Substation Engineers, the position drives resolution of both systemic and site-specific issues and provides operational insight that informs the design, equipment selection, and turnover of new projects.

Main Responsibilities:

• Serve as a primary engineering resource for the Asset Operations team, providing troubleshooting support and coordinating corrective action implementation across the plant.

• Drive the resolution of key technical issues across the fleet, including serial defects, major equipment failures, and sustained underperformance.

• Translate field observations, inspection results, and performance data into clear problem statements and actionable solutions.

• Support O&M teams with structured troubleshooting and escalation.

• Own technical issues related to the PV array and DC balance of plant, including modules, trackers, DC collection, and grounding systems.

• Support technical issues on the AC balance of plant, from the padmount transformers to the point of interconnection, including MV collection systems.

• Support performance optimization for operating projects with recurring performance issues and for new projects with latent construction issues.

• Lead the identification and implementation of reliability best practices, including PM optimization, failure and root cause analyses, spare parts strategies, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Lead the review of engineering-related PM activities (such as thermal imaging and transformer DGA testing) to identify and correct deficiencies.

• Serve as a technical interface with OEMs, EPCs, contractors, and service providers, supporting issue escalation, warranty claims, and oversight of vendor performance.

• Support the engineering-related turnover of new projects from construction to operations, including commissioning review and resolution of technical gaps.

• Provide operational insight to Engineering and Delivery teams through design reviews and new equipment and vendor evaluations.

• Identify and communicate design or operational deficiencies.

• Develop processes, procedures, and tools that help the team manage technical issues efficiently, and support the training and mentoring of team members.

• Collaborate closely with Asset Management, O&M, Performance Engineering, ROC, Compliance, Engineering, and Delivery teams to improve fleet performance.

Qualifications:

Education

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical Engineering strongly preferred)

Experience

• Operations Engineer: 0–5 years of relevant experience. Senior Operations Engineer: 6+ years of relevant experience.

• Utility-scale solar operations experience required for Senior Operations Engineer and preferred for Operations Engineer.

• Field experience troubleshooting utility-scale solar plant equipment, such as PV array and DC systems, inverters, and MV equipment.

• Experience working with OEMs, EPCs, contractors, and cross-functional teams to resolve technical issues.

• Experience with project turnover, commissioning, or design review is a plus.

Skills

• Broad understanding of utility-scale PV plant systems, including modules, trackers, DC collection, inverters, MV collection, and substations.

• Familiarity with electrical testing and inspection methods, such as insulation resistance, VLF, transformer electrical testing, thermography, and transformer DGA.

• Ability to read and review electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, and equipment specifications.

• Working knowledge of plant SCADA, communications networks, and monitoring systems sufficient to troubleshoot data and communication issues.

• Working knowledge of applicable NEC, NESC, IEEE, IEC, and NETA requirements.

• Proven ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues.

• Experience with root cause analysis and reliability practices.

• Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Strong communication skills and ability to influence outcomes across teams.

What We’re Looking For

• A field-proven engineer and plant generalist who is comfortable across the entire PV plant.

• Someone who can connect on-site issues to broader system and fleet impacts.

• Organized and proactive; comfortable managing multiple priorities.

• Comfortable owning technical problems and driving them to resolution.

Our interview process:

A typical interview process at Silicon Ranch might include the below stages. Please note that we may make changes to these steps as needed, and details will be provided to you early on in the process.

• Introductory Interview with our recruiter

• Hiring Manager Interview to dive into technical skills and behavioral questions

• Panel Interview to assess cross-functional skills and dive deeper into technical skills

• Executive Interview to answer high-level questions about SRC and the team

Schedule: This is a 0.9 FTE position, three 12-hour shifts per week, 7:00pm-7:30am, rotating days of the week.

The Feinberg Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU) is a multifaceted, high-acuity PACU that works in conjunction with the main Feinberg Operating Room (OR) and off-site interventional areas that focus on providing world-class care to patients recovering from anesthesia. Our nurses provide care to some of the most complex surgical patients in the State of Illinois. The PACU is designated for patients who require close monitoring after complex surgical interventions, and to administer pre-operative care from the inpatient areas. This unit allows nurses to advance their skillset by combining cutting-edge technology and critical care thinking to provide evidence-based comprehensive nursing care to our highly complex patient population.

Specialty care and devices include:

• Shock-Cardiogenic, Distributive, Hypovolemic, Obstructive
• Pre-operative care to CABG, transplants, valve surgeries, general surgery, trauma
• Urology
• Interventional Radiology cases
• Post-ablations
• Organ transplants/donors
• Abdominal Surgeries
• Gastric Bypass
• Neurosurgical procedures
• Spinal procedures
• ENT
• Plastics

• Wedge resections
• Bronchoscopy
• Vascular procedures

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

Territory Account Managers will be responsible for expanding our existing customer base by building relationships with contractors and construction company principals. Primary Responsibilities

• Assists with Equipment rental, sales, and service when needed by customers on-site.

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive compensation: Base salary plus uncapped commission

• Commission guarantee period while building book of business

• Company provided truck or Vehicle allowance ($800/mo)

• Company provided cell phone or phone stipend

• Relocation assistance (discretionary)

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• 401(k) and company match

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events and quarterly team activities

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

• You’re competitive, self-motivated and results driven, but thrive in a team-oriented environment

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, PhD, Research, Behavior Post-training

jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The mission of the Waymo AI Foundations team is to develop machine learning solutions addressing open problems in autonomous driving, towards the goal of safely operating Waymo vehicles in dozens of cities and under all driving conditions. As part of our work, we also initiate and foster collaborations with other research teams in Alphabet. AI Foundations areas that we are currently focusing on include reinforcement learning, learning from demonstration, generative modeling, Bayesian inference, hierarchical learning, and robust evaluation.

Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

You will:

• Build tools for sampling, selecting, and discarding synthetic driving data with testable hypotheses of how that data will lead to improvement

• Train and evaluate models with mixtures of synthetic and logged data

• Present and write about methods for synthetic data generation and training

You have:

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field

• Familiarity with methods of sampling from large models

• Experience with post-training methods such as SFT, RL, and preferences

• Modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and Jax

We prefer:

• Experience working with open and closed loop decision making models in robotics

• Experience with synthetic data generation and evaluation

• Prior projects using LLM-as-a-judge

jobs.title: Activation Engineer
jobs.description:
WE'RE BUILDING A NEW HEALTHCARE CLEARINGHOUSE

Stedi is the only headless clearinghouse and RCM engine. Headless means every part of our product is accessible via API. Developers and AI agents build their own interface on top of it. By offering modern, AI-ready APIs alongside traditional real-time and batch EDI processes, we enable both healthcare technology businesses and established players to exchange mission-critical transactions. Our clearinghouse product and customer-first approach have set us apart. Stedi was ranked by Ramp https://ramp.com/data/top-saas-vendors-on-ramp-march-2026 as one of the fastest-growing SaaS vendors.



Stedi has lightning in a bottle: engineers and designers shipping products week in and week out; a lean business team supporting the company's infrastructure; a passion for automation and eliminating toil; and $142 million in funding from top investors like Stripe, Addition, USV, Bloomberg Beta, First Round Capital, and more.



To see what we ship, watch the 2026 Stedi Keynote https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MxyCUNAr9Y8. To learn more about how we work, watch our founder Zack's interview with First Round Capital https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IO6sR-i5rSs.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We’re growing our Activation team. Our customers are building on a clearinghouse, which means their first months with Stedi are a technical project: mapping their use case to our APIs, testing submissions and reading what comes back, and getting to production volume without surprises. How well that goes decides whether a customer ever realizes the value they bought.

As an Activation Engineer, you will be the technical counterpart to our sales and account management teams, ensuring that they have everything they need to make customers successful with Stedi. Activation Engineers work with customers from their first integration call through to running full production volume. You’ll also build the demos, guides and internal documentation that empowers the rest of customer-facing team to answer technical questions without you, and you’ll be the conduit back to Product when the answer is “we don’t do that yet”. The work moves fast, spans a lot of surface area, and has a real impact - on our customers, our revenue, and our roadmap.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You are technical. You understand and have experience using and integrating APIs, and have a familiarity with data formats and standards such as JSON, X12, and other flat file formats.

 - You are proactive by default. You don't wait for a ticket. You decide which customers need attention and when, usually before they ask, based on what you can see in their data and where they are in their ramp.

 - You have a product mindset. You go beyond helping customers with the task at hand. You are able to intuitively understand product gaps and are able to articulate those to the engineering and product teams, and ensure those requirements satisfy the customer's needs.

 - You have deep customer empathy and have experience in customer-facing roles. You can understand a customer’s needs and quickly establish credibility by getting into the weeds on technical areas of a product to ensure they’re getting the most value. You keep customers at the center of your work and always prioritize customer relationships.

 - You have subject matter expertise in revenue cycle management or are excited to learn. Bonus points if you have experience working at an RCM company and understand the full cycle of how healthcare technology companies run eligibility checks, submit claims, check claim status, and reconcile ERAs.

 - You do what it takes to get the job done. You are resourceful, self-motivating, self-disciplined, and don’t wait to be told what to do. You put in the hours.

 - You are exceptional at staying on top of many open threads simultaneously. You are hyper-responsive, organized, and thorough.

 - You move fast. We move fast as an organization. Our median response time to customers during business hours is 3.4 minutes. This requires an ability to match our pace and not get lost by responding with urgency (both externally to customers and internally to stakeholders), communicating what you are working on, and proactively asking for help or feedback when you need it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Serve as the technical counterpart on pre-sale deals. Ask the questions that qualify the opportunity, determine what the use case actually requires, explain to the customer what kind of integration this will be, and which product gaps have to be closed before we can deliver.

 - Own technical design during the proof-of-concept phase. Establish use cases and requirements, clear blockers, and make sure customers have what they need to test their integration and interpret the results.

 - Coordinate payer list matching and run insurance discovery batch tests, then share and interpret the results so customers can see what good looks like.

 - Drive ramping customers to expected transaction volume on the expected timeline. Build the migration plan, track actual volume against what was sold, and identify and clear the root causes of processing errors.

 - Build the internal material that makes new functionality sellable: feature overviews, positioning and talk tracks, demos, best-practice writeups, and qualification criteria. Answer functionality questions for the customer-facing team, or track down the person who can.

 - Represent customers to Product. Write the one-pagers that define customer problems, shape requirements, and co-own a customer-driven feature backlog, including how much customer weight sits behind each request.



We’ve been made aware of individuals impersonating the Stedi recruiting team. Please note:

 - All official communication about roles at Stedi will only come from an @stedi.com http://stedi.com email address, or from our official identification verification partner, Persona, @frompersona.com http://frompersona.com.

 - If you’re unsure whether a message is legitimate or have any concerns, feel free to contact us directly at careers@stedi.com.

We appreciate your attention to this and your interest in joining Stedi.



At Stedi, we're looking for people who are deeply curious and aligned to our ways of working. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description.

jobs.title: Director of Commercial and Ancillary
jobs.description:
What You Will Do

AIR Communities is seeking a strategic, analytically driven Senior Director, Commercial & Ancillary Services to lead financial management, commercial leasing, lease administration, and ancillary revenue performance across the portfolio. Reporting to the Vice President, Commercial & Ancillary Services, this role will maximize revenue, improve operational performance, strengthen commercial tenant relationships, and support long-term asset strategy through financial analysis, forecasting, revenue optimization, and disciplined execution.

This leader will partner with Accounting, Property Operations, Asset Management, and other business partners to translate financial and operational data into actionable insights, identify revenue opportunities, and ensure commercial and ancillary programs are administered accurately and effectively.

The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking, financial expertise, operational discipline, and collaborative leadership while partnering closely with the Vice President, mentoring at least one direct report, and advancing departmental and portfolio-wide objectives.

Commercial Leasing, Revenue Growth & Asset Strategy

Develop and execute commercial leasing strategies that support asset objectives, resident needs, tenant quality, and long-term revenue goals while maintaining a high-quality commercial and retail tenant mix aligned with property-level and portfolio-wide strategies.

Evaluate prospective tenants and commercial opportunities based on financial performance, tenant suitability, market considerations, and alignment with asset strategy.

Lead or oversee the negotiation of commercial leases, renewals, extensions, amendments, and other agreements in coordination with the Vice President and appropriate internal partners.

Identify opportunities to increase commercial rent, commercial parking income, and other ancillary revenues through improved leasing, pricing, contract terms, and program performance.

Build and maintain strong relationships with commercial tenants, brokers, and other external partners to support leasing activity, tenant retention, and revenue growth.

Monitor commercial and ancillary performance, identify trends and opportunities, and recommend initiatives that improve financial results and operational effectiveness.

Lease Administration, Contract Management & Compliance

Oversee the accuracy and completeness of the commercial lease database, ensuring lease terms, financial obligations, and related documentation are properly maintained.

Ensure commercial lease setup, recurring rent charges, monthly billings, and applicable expense estimates are accurate and timely.

Monitor critical lease dates, renewal and expiration schedules, contractual obligations, and compliance requirements to minimize financial and operational risk.

Maintain complete tenant files and current Certificates of Insurance in accordance with established requirements.

Maintain accurate ancillary services contract records, including key terms, expiration dates, renewal schedules, and applicable financial obligations.

Establish effective processes, documentation, and controls for lease and contract administration, billing, reporting, data integrity, and coordination among Commercial & Ancillary Services, Accounting, and Property Operations.

Financial Management, Planning & Reporting

Lead annual budgets, monthly forecasts, variance analyses, and long-range financial plans for commercial and ancillary revenue programs, supported by financial models, scenario analyses, and performance forecasts that inform strategic planning, revenue optimization, and business decisions.

Prepare timely, accurate executive reporting and presentations on commercial rent, parking, ancillary revenues, operating performance, key trends, risks, and opportunities to support leadership decisions, asset strategy, and portfolio performance.

Analyze actual results against budget and forecast, identify performance drivers and emerging risks, and recommend corrective actions and opportunities for improvement.

Monitor Accounts Receivable, delinquency trends, collections, and outstanding balances, partnering with appropriate teams to address issues and improve collection performance.

Partner with Accounting to ensure annual Common Area Maintenance (CAM) reconciliations and estimates of future-year expenses are completed accurately and on time.

Ancillary Services & Property Operations

Oversee the financial performance and administration of parking and other ancillary revenue programs, identifying opportunities to improve revenue, service delivery, contract management, and the resident and tenant experience while ensuring alignment with portfolio objectives and property needs.

Serve as a key point of contact for property teams regarding commercial tenants, lease-related matters, and ancillary service programs.

Collaborate with Property Operations and other internal partners to resolve tenant concerns, address operational challenges, and support effective property-level execution.

Support consistent program administration, clear accountability, and effective communication across corporate and property teams.

Develop reporting and analytical tools that help stakeholders monitor performance, identify trends, and make informed operational decisions.

Strategic Partnership, Process Improvement & Leadership

Work closely with the Vice President, Commercial & Ancillary Services, in a collaborative, shared-responsibility environment to establish priorities and advance departmental goals.

Provide guidance, coaching, and mentorship to at least one direct report, supporting individual development, accountability, and strong team performance.

Partner with Accounting, Property Operations, Asset Management, and other stakeholders to align financial objectives, leasing strategy, operational execution, and reporting, translating complex information into clear recommendations for business partners and senior leadership.

Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, reporting capabilities, data quality, and operational efficiency.

Document policies, procedures, and process flows to promote consistency, accuracy, and effective internal controls.

Participate in special projects, cross-functional initiatives, and strategic planning efforts that support revenue growth and overall business performance.

Foster a collaborative, accountable, and team-oriented culture consistent with AIR Communities' values.

A Bit More About Who You Are

You're Financially and Analytically Driven. You apply expertise in budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial modeling to evaluate performance, identify trends, and recommend practical actions that support business objectives.

You're an Excel Expert. You use advanced formulas, PivotTables, financial models, and complex datasets to build efficient analytical tools and interpret large volumes of financial and operational data.

You're a Strategic, Results-Oriented Thinker. You connect financial performance, leasing decisions, tenant mix, contract terms, and ancillary services to broader asset and portfolio objectives; balance near-term results with long-term value creation; and turn analysis into measurable revenue and operational improvements.

You're Detail-Oriented and Process-Minded. You understand the importance of accurate lease data, timely billing, reliable financial reporting, contract compliance, and consistent processes. You anticipate risks and work proactively to resolve issues.

You're a Collaborative Leader and Clear Communicator. You build strong relationships across corporate and property teams, mentor others, share responsibility effectively, and translate complex financial information into concise recommendations that help stakeholders and senior leaders make informed decisions.

You're Motivated by AIR Communities' Values and Culture. You demonstrate integrity, respect, collaboration, customer focus, and performance in your work. You are adaptable, self-motivated, and committed to continuous improvement.

Keys to Success

Strategic Financial Management: Produces sound budgets, forecasts, financial models, and performance analyses that guide decisions and improve commercial and ancillary results.

Revenue Optimization: Identifies opportunities to improve commercial and ancillary revenue, tenant mix, and overall portfolio performance.

Operational Excellence: Ensures accurate lease and financial data, timely billing and reporting, contract compliance, and consistent administration across the portfolio.

Analytical Problem-Solving: Uses financial and operational data to identify root causes, assess opportunities, and recommend practical solutions.

Leadership and Accountability: Develops direct reports, establishes clear ownership, delivers results, and advances departmental priorities in partnership with senior leadership.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Builds productive partnerships with Accounting, Property Operations, Asset Management, and other stakeholders.

Communication and Influence: Clearly presents financial results, explains business implications, and develops support for recommended actions.

Adaptability and Continuous Improvement: Navigates changing priorities while identifying ways to improve systems, processes, and business outcomes.

What You Have

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Real Estate, or a related field.

Significant experience in financial planning and analysis, commercial real estate, property operations, commercial leasing, ancillary revenue management, or a related discipline, including developing budgets, forecasts, financial models, variance analyses, and executive-level reporting.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, PivotTables, financial modeling, and data analysis, with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and Power BI.

Experience analyzing financial performance, identifying revenue opportunities, and translating complex data into actionable recommendations.

Experience managing or overseeing commercial leases, contract administration, tenant relationships, accounts receivable, billing, or related financial and operational processes.

Demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments and influence stakeholders without relying solely on direct authority.

Experience providing leadership, guidance, or mentorship to team members.

Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, communication abilities, and sound business judgment.

Ability to balance strategic priorities with operational execution in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Highly Desirable Skills and Experience

Experience in multifamily real estate, commercial real estate, retail leasing, or real estate investment trust (REIT) operations.

Experience overseeing parking revenue, ancillary services, or other property-related revenue programs.

Proficiency in SQL, VBA, and/or other tools used to automate reporting, improve data analysis, and streamline processes.

Experience with financial planning, reporting, and property management systems, including Hyperion or comparable platforms.

Experience preparing executive presentations and communicating financial performance, risks, and opportunities to senior leadership.

AIR offers attractive total compensation packages designed to recognize and reward performance at the individual, team and company levels. We start with a competitive base salary and add bonus opportunities and benefit choices topped off with:

• Expected base salary of $150,000-$170,000. You will be provided a pay rate that is in line with your skills and experience as they relate to the requirements of the job.
• Base salary plus annual bonus.
• 25% Rent Discount available
• Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance options available. HSA with company sponsored contributions, FSA (traditional and dependent care FSA).

Whether it’s the talent within our communities or the expertise across our property operations teams, we work together to make extraordinary happen for our clients, residents and fellow team members.

Our people are dedicated to delivering exceptional experiences to everyone we serve including each other. This shared purpose drives us to excel in every role and fosters a welcoming, inclusive workplace where teamwork thrives. Guided by our core values of concern, creativity, passion and the pursuit of perfection, we are inspired and empowered to reach higher, unlock our full potential and be truly extraordinary.

Primary Responsibilities

As a Multi-Site Maintenance Manager, your primary responsibilities include:

• Leading by example and being a role model for the standards and behaviors consistent with the core values and culture of Bozzuto

• Dedicating time to hiring, developing and providing on-the-job and classroom education opportunities to techs and community care associates

• Showing care and concern for our residents through timely follow up and meticulous completion of their apartment service tickets

• Preserving the beauty of the building and the safety of the community through general upkeep and cleanliness, snow removal and grounds maintenance

• Sustaining peak efficiency operation levels for all property components

• Adhering to applicable building, county and safety codes/standards, while running an accident-free operation

• Ensuring completion of annual building systems inspections required by the jurisdiction

• Leading cost-effective capital improvement and special projects

• Establishing and managing vendor relationships and projects within budget parameters

• Reinforcing monthly staffing schedules, ensuring 24/7 emergency coverage

What You Bring to Us:

• 3+ years of supervisory experience and a track record of hiring, developing and retaining high performing teams

jobs.title: Commercial HVAC Estimator with Morgan Mechanical Inc
jobs.description:
Title: Remote Commercial HVAC Estimator
Schedule: Remote/Full-Time - Pacific Time (PT)

Location: Latin America
Compensation: $2,000–$2,500/month, depending on experience




ABOUT THE COMPANY

Our client is an owner-operated commercial HVAC and mechanical contracting business based in Kirkland, Washington, serving commercial construction projects in the Seattle area. The company operates with a lean team and values accuracy, accountability, and practical collaboration.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an experienced Senior Commercial HVAC Estimator to take ownership of estimating for commercial HVAC projects. This individual will be responsible for reviewing construction drawings and specifications, performing detailed material takeoffs, developing accurate cost estimates, and supporting bid preparation.

The ideal candidate has extensive hands-on experience estimating commercial HVAC systems, understands U.S. construction standards, and can work independently in a remote environment while collaborating directly with the business owner.

This role requires dedicated commercial HVAC estimating experience. Residential estimating or general mechanical estimating experience alone will not meet the requirements.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Perform detailed material takeoffs for commercial HVAC projects using blueprints, construction drawings, and technical specifications.

 - Read, interpret, and analyze mechanical plans, equipment schedules, and project documentation.

 - Estimate quantities for HVAC ductwork, equipment, piping, fittings, insulation, accessories, and other applicable system components.

 - Prepare detailed and accurate cost estimates for commercial bid submissions.

 - Calculate material quantities, labor requirements, equipment costs, and other relevant project expenses.

 - Review project specifications and applicable U.S. construction standards to ensure estimates reflect the required scope.

 - Identify scope gaps, conflicting information, missing details, and potential cost risks.

 - Document estimating assumptions, exclusions, and items requiring clarification.

 - Coordinate with the business owner and other relevant stakeholders regarding project scope, pricing, and bid strategy.

 - Review estimates for accuracy, completeness, and consistency before submission.

 - Work within the company's existing estimating systems, tools, and workflows.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 10+ years of estimating experience, with substantial hands-on experience specifically in commercial HVAC estimating.

 - Proven experience estimating commercial HVAC projects for contractors or commercial mechanical firms.

 - Strong ability to interpret commercial construction drawings, mechanical plans, equipment schedules, and technical specifications.

 - Demonstrated experience performing HVAC material takeoffs and preparing cost estimates independently.

 - Working knowledge of U.S. commercial construction standards, applicable mechanical codes, and project specifications.

 - Understanding of HVAC materials, installation methods, labor estimating, and commercial bid preparation.

 - Proficiency with relevant estimating and takeoff software, such as Bluebeam, PlanSwift, Trimble, or comparable tools.

 - Strong English communication skills, including the ability to explain estimating methodology and technical decisions clearly.

 - Ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and maintain accuracy in a remote environment.

 - Availability to work full-time during Pacific Time business hours.

 - Willingness to complete a practical technical assessment as part of the interview process.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Previous experience working with U.S.-based commercial HVAC contractors or mechanical subcontractors.

 - Experience with commercial construction projects such as offices, retail facilities, warehouses, or other commercial buildings.

 - Experience with firms such as WSP or similar commercial mechanical or engineering organizations, provided the candidate has direct HVAC estimating experience.

 - Familiarity with HVAC estimating workflows, vendor quotations, labor units, and bid documentation.

 - Ability to provide redacted samples of previous HVAC takeoffs or estimates demonstrating a clear and systematic methodology.





WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

The successful candidate will produce accurate, complete, and well-documented commercial HVAC estimates, proactively identify scope gaps and pricing risks, and work independently while maintaining clear communication with the business owner.

Reports to: Vice President of National Accounts

Position Summary

The National Accounts Coordinator coordinates the launch and ongoing administrative support of National Accounts.

This role owns the account launch process from signed agreement through go-live, ensuring customer requirements, documentation, approved pricing, service coverage, account setup, and billing procedures are complete and communicated. Working closely with National Accounts, Operations, franchisees or service providers, and Accounts Receivable (AR), this role tracks readiness, follows up on outstanding items, and escalates barriers to a successful launch.

After launch, the National Accounts Coordinator supports a consistent customer experience through proactive communication, billing coordination, issue follow-through, and account health tracking. This is a hands-on position requiring organization, initiative, attention to detail, and a willingness to assist without waiting to be asked.

Key Responsibilities

Account Launch Ownership

• Own and maintain the account launch checklist, timeline, assigned responsibilities, and readiness status from signed agreement through go-live.

• Review customer requirements with National Accounts and Operations and translate them into actionable setup tasks.

• Coordinate required documentation, including signed agreements, service requirements, certificates of insurance (COIs), customer contacts, and billing instructions.

• Confirm approved pricing is documented and accurately reflected in the appropriate systems and customer portals.

• Verify service coverage and responsible service providers with Operations, documenting gaps and escalation contacts before launch.

• Coordinate customer account, location, portal, and work order setup with the appropriate teams.

• Confirm invoice requirements, purchase order procedures, supporting documentation, submission methods, and payment terms with Accounts Receivable.

• Communicate launch requirements and responsibilities to internal teams and participating service providers.

• Track outstanding items, escalate launch risks, and obtain readiness confirmation from responsible teams before go-live.

• Monitor initial work orders and billing activity to identify and resolve early account issues.

Customer Experience & Communication

• Serve as a central contact for customer updates, administrative questions, service concerns, and billing inquiries.

• Track customer concerns with a clear owner, next action, and expected resolution date.

• Coordinate responses with the appropriate team and follow through until issues are resolved.

• Maintain accurate records of customer communication, commitments, and account requirements.

• Escalate concerns that could affect service delivery, customer satisfaction, or the overall account relationship.

Operations & Billing Coordination

• Facilitate communication between National Accounts, Operations, franchisees or service providers, and Accounts Receivable.

• Monitor open work orders and follow up on missing updates, overdue activity, and incomplete documentation.

• Confirm completed work includes the information required for billing.

• Coordinate resolution of invoice discrepancies, rejected invoices, missing purchase orders, and customer billing questions.

• Track outstanding billing issues and support Accounts Receivable with customer communication and documentation.

• Identify recurring administrative or service gaps and recommend practical process improvements.

Account Health & Performance Tracking

• Maintain an account health tracker showing open work orders, response times, completion status, documentation compliance, unresolved customer issues, and billing exceptions.

• Monitor performance against each account's agreed service requirements and flag exceptions promptly.

• Provide regular account status reports to National Accounts and Operations, highlighting overdue items, recurring issues, and actions needed.

• Keep reporting accurate and current so teams can act on account risks.

• Track corrective actions through completion and identify patterns that could affect customer retention or account growth.

Required Qualifications

• 2+ years of experience in project coordination, account management, or a related role.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple accounts, tasks, and deadlines simultaneously.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a professional, customer-focused approach.

• Ability to take ownership of follow-up and coordinate work across cross-functional teams without direct supervisory authority.

• Strong attention to detail when handling pricing, documentation, account records, and billing requirements.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM systems, customer portals, and work order platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting multi-location customers, franchise organizations, or field service businesses.

• Familiarity with certificates of insurance (COIs), invoicing, and Accounts Receivable processes.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

We are looking for a highly organized, execution-focused Supplier Operations Manager to serve as the primary program owner for one or more assigned hardware component suppliers. This role is accountable for end-to-end execution at the supplier level, spanning forecast management, capacity planning, data quality, and cross-functional coordination across all parts and commodities sourced from the account.

The SOM is the key liaison between Form's Global Supply Management team and assigned suppliers, partnering closely with Global Supply Managers (commodity owners), Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Logistics, and Finance. The SOM is the active operations resource ensuring supplier readiness, compliance, and performance as Form scales from NPI into volume production.


Relocation assistance is available. This role requires travel up to 50% of the time. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own end-to-end program execution for assigned supplier account(s), covering both new product introduction (NPI) and sustaining phases.

 - Serve as Form's primary operational point of contact for assigned suppliers; coordinate across all parts and commodities sourced from the account.

 - Partner with Global Supply Managers to align commodity sourcing strategies with supplier-level execution plans and capacity commitments.

 - Manage supplier forecast submissions, order status, and capacity reviews; drive adherence to forecast and commitment cadences.

 - Own supplier-level data quality and process compliance, including lead times, order status, forecast accuracy, and standardized, high-quality reporting, including regularly refreshed Clear-To-Build (CTB) reports.

 - Lead regular supplier program forums, status reviews, and executive summaries with internal stakeholders and supplier leadership.

 - Coordinate supplier business reviews (SBRs) and periodic performance assessments; track and escalate supplier-specific risks, shortages, and recovery plans.

 - Partner with Engineering and Quality to support first article, change management (ECOs), and supplier corrective actions.

 - Coordinate inbound logistics, expedites, and delivery performance with suppliers and internal planning/receiving teams.

 - Onboard and train suppliers on Form's data systems, quality reporting, forecast processes, and program requirements.

 - Drive resolution of cross-commodity supplier issues that span multiple internal owners.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field, with 1–3 years of experience in supply chain operations, supplier management, or manufacturing; or a recent college graduate with internship experience in a manufacturing environment.

 - Demonstrated actions toward becoming a supply chain professional (e.g., coursework, APICS/ASCM or similar certification, relevant projects, or hands-on supply chain experience).

 - Demonstrated ability to manage complex, cross-functional programs with multiple internal and external stakeholders.

 - Ability to travel up to 50% to supplier sites.

 - Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills; ability to translate between internal teams and supplier planning organizations.

 - Experience with hardware supply chain operations, including forecast management, capacity planning, and supplier performance tracking.

 - Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems and Excel or equivalent data tools.
   




PREFERRED:

 - Master's degree

 - Exposure to supplier operations, material planning, or manufacturing of mechanical, plastic, metal, or electromechanical components.

 - Familiarity with capacity planning and forecast / response-to-forecast processes.

 - Experience coordinating across commodity managers and engineering in a matrixed organization.

 - Comfort working with overseas suppliers across time zones; additional languages a plus.

A Manager, Paid Search is responsible for the end-to-end execution, performance, and day-to-day management of paid search campaigns across assigned accounts. This individual translates client objectives into tactical campaign strategies, owns campaign optimization and budget management, identifies opportunities for account growth, and communicates performance insights and recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders. What You'll Do

• Own the day-to-day execution and performance of paid search campaigns across Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and supporting search technologies, from planning and setup through launch, optimization, and reporting.

• Develop tactical paid search strategies aligned with client objectives, audience strategies, KPIs, and broader integrated media plans. Contribute to campaign forecasts, planning inputs, and supporting data analysis.

• Troubleshoot platform, tracking, attribution, trafficking, and reporting issues using strong platform expertise and analytical problem-solving skills.

• Mentor and train junior team members on platform execution, campaign processes, and best practices while continuing to develop people leadership capabilities.

• Contribute to process improvements, documentation, training materials, automation initiatives, and emerging platform capabilities that strengthen team efficiency and performance.

This Position Is a Perfect Fit for You If

• You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.

• You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.

• You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.

• You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What You Should Have

• 3+ years of professional experience managing digital media campaigns, with significant hands-on experience in paid search.

• Strong expertise in Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and paid search campaign management.

• Experience managing campaigns end to end, including planning, setup, launch, optimization, reporting, and performance analysis.

• Strong understanding of bidding strategies, keyword management, audience targeting, attribution, conversion optimization, and campaign measurement.

• Demonstrated ability to monitor campaign performance, manage budgets and pacing, and optimize toward established KPIs.

• Experience developing forecasts, tracking spend, and maintaining accurate monthly budget actualization.

• Ability to troubleshoot platform, tracking, tagging, attribution, and reporting issues.
