jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are seeking candidates in US and Canada.

The Opportunity

Application Core Services (AppCore) is a group within Platform, in the Foundations department. We build and operate systems that support Grafana’s business operations and customer experience, working closely with product teams and internal business partners.

The Usage squad works on billing, rates, usage calculations, usage visibility and cloud marketplace integrations. Our software helps customers understand their consumption and costs, and helps internal teams operate accurate, reliable billing processes.

We are looking for a Staff Fullstack Engineer with strong backend experience who enjoys making complex business systems reliable, understandable and easier to operate. You will help deliver new capabilities while improving existing services, reducing repetitive manual work and addressing edge cases that affect customers and internal stakeholders.

This is a hands-on Staff engineering role within the AppCore Usage squad. You will lead complex technical work, contribute directly to implementation and share ownership with the squad’s other Staff and Senior engineers. Your primary focus will be Usage’s systems and outcomes, collaborating with adjacent teams when the work requires it.

Our ownership includes application code, data stores, deployment configuration and the cloud infrastructure supporting our services. You should be comfortable following a problem across those boundaries and making improvements with the appropriate platform teams.

We are remote-first and global. For this role, we prefer candidates in NASA’s Eastern Time zone to provide more overlap with our EMEA colleagues.

What You’ll Be Doing

Your initial focus will be approximately 75% backend and 25% frontend. This balance will evolve with the squad’s priorities. You should be comfortable delivering across the stack, from business logic and APIs through to the interfaces customers and internal teams use.

• Design, build and operate backend services and APIs supporting billing, rates, usage calculations, usage visibility and marketplace workflows.

• Build and maintain backend services primarily in Go, with Node.js also present in our stack, and contribute to TypeScript/React applications to deliver complete features.

• Improve the correctness and reliability of billing and usage workflows, including validation, reconciliation, error handling and recovery.

• Identify recurring manual tasks and replace them with maintainable automation, clear operational workflows and appropriate controls.

• Maintain and evolve the infrastructure supporting our services, including Kubernetes workloads, scheduled jobs, cloud resources and deployment configuration.

• Use infrastructure as code and automated delivery pipelines to make changes repeatable, reviewable and safe across environments.

• Investigate production issues across application code, databases and infrastructure, including resource exhaustion, failed jobs, slow queries and replication delays.

• Plan and execute service deployments, database changes and infrastructure migrations, including validation, monitoring and recovery plans.

• Build and maintain integrations with cloud marketplaces and external business systems where required by the squad’s work.

• Deliver projects from understanding requirements and proposing an approach through implementation, testing, rollout and production support.

• Make changes traceable and testable, supporting audit requirements and clear explanations of system behaviour.

• Collaborate with product management, Support, DealOps, GTM, infrastructure teams and adjacent AppCore squads to clarify requirements and resolve dependencies.

• Share technical leadership through design discussions, code reviews, mentoring and practical improvements.

• Participate in the squad’s on-call rotation after onboarding. Improve dashboards, alert quality, runbooks and recovery procedures, and follow through on incident findings.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You enjoy engineering work where correctness, reliability and business impact matter. You find value in improving an established system, removing a recurring operational problem or making a billing workflow easier to understand and support.

You take ownership from understanding the problem through delivery and production support. You can turn an ambiguous request into manageable increments, make sound trade-offs and follow through without needing each step prescribed. You ask useful questions, seek feedback and raise uncertainty or blockers early.

You adapt as priorities change, learn unfamiliar systems and technologies, and contribute where the squad needs you. You bring a strong backend specialty while remaining willing and able to work on frontend features and supporting infrastructure.

You reason about how a service behaves in production: how it is deployed, where its data lives, what happens when dependencies fail, and how the team detects and recovers from problems.

You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation. In a distributed team, you make decisions, progress and risks visible so colleagues can contribute across time zones. You work independently while staying connected to the squad.

As a Staff engineer, you bring technical depth and sound judgment while remaining close to implementation. You collaborate constructively with other experienced engineers, welcome different perspectives and help the squad reach decisions and move forward.

We embrace thoughtful use of AI-assisted development. We value engineers who use these tools to support exploration, implementation, testing and documentation while taking responsibility for the quality and correctness of the result.

Requirements

• Substantial experience designing, delivering and operating production backend systems, with the depth and judgment to lead complex work hands-on.

• Strong experience building and operating production backend systems in Go, our primary backend language.

• Professional experience contributing to frontend applications using TypeScript and React, or comparable technologies, and willingness to work across the stack as priorities change.

• Experience reasoning about distributed systems, including partial failures, retries, consistency and interactions between services.

• Experience with relational databases, including data modelling, schema migrations, query performance and safe production changes.

• Practical experience deploying and troubleshooting containerised services and jobs in Kubernetes.

• Experience managing cloud infrastructure through code and working with CI/CD pipelines, environment configuration and controlled rollouts.

• Ability to investigate production problems using logs, metrics and traces, and turn findings into lasting improvements.

• A record of delivering projects end to end, clarifying requirements, making trade-offs and following through after release.

• Experience working remotely, with clear asynchronous communication and dependable collaboration across time zones.

• Ability to learn unfamiliar domains and technologies, adjust your approach as new information emerges, and take ownership beyond your main area of expertise.

• Experience writing readable, well-tested software that other engineers can understand, maintain and operate.

• Willingness to participate in on-call and take responsibility for the production behaviour of the systems you build.

• Experience supporting colleagues through code reviews, mentoring and constructive technical discussions.

Bonus Points For

• Usage metering, billing engines, pricing and rates, financial reconciliation or customer-facing cost management applications.

• Reducing operational toil and automating workflows with recurring exceptions or manual interventions.

• Systems with auditability, traceability or financial-control requirements.

• MySQL operations, replication, database upgrades and performance tuning.

• Terraform, Jsonnet and Kubernetes deployment configuration.

• Argo Workflows or comparable deployment and job-orchestration tooling.

• Cloud infrastructure involving managed databases, object storage, service accounts and access controls, particularly on GCP.

• Data synchronisation pipelines and BigQuery integrations.

• Cloud marketplace integrations across AWS, Azure or GCP.

• Integrations with business platforms such as NetSuite or Salesforce.

• Observability tools such as Grafana, Prometheus, Loki or OpenTelemetry.

jobs.title: Partner, Corporate & Investment Banking / Capital Markets
jobs.description:
Be the leader behind the transformation of tomorrow’s financial institutions.

Join a fast-growing global consulting firm that’s rewriting the rules for how strategy and execution intersect. At Sia, we empower senior leaders to drive complex transformations, shape industry trends, and grow thriving practices. As a Partner in our Financial Services Business Unit, you’ll play a critical role in expanding our footprint in North America while delivering next-generation solutions to financial institutions reshaping the industry.

Backed by a global footprint and consulting capabilities across all major industry sectors, our teams guide C-suite leaders across banking, wealth management, capital markets, and fintech. We combine deep domain expertise with digital and tech-forward approaches that make a lasting impact.

Capital markets and corporate & investment banking are at a significant inflection point. Evolving market structures, extended trading hours, accelerated and continuous settlement, and technology modernization are reshaping how financial institutions trade, finance, clear, settle, and service assets. Sia helps global banks, institutional broker-dealers, custodians, clearing houses, depositories, and market infrastructure providers turn that change into strategic opportunity.

As a Partner, you will accelerate the buildout of Sia's U.S. capital markets and corporate & investment banking practice. You will shape our point of view and offerings, originate and lead high-value engagements, recruit and grow the team, and build lasting relationships with senior executives across institutional financial services. You will bring Sia's global capabilities to bear on the most important questions facing the industry.

Your Role as a Partner

You'll be a recognized leader inside and outside the firm, responsible for business development, delivery excellence, and leadership across accounts and teams. You will:

Drive Client Growth

• Lead and grow strategic client accounts in financial services, serving as their trusted advisor on capital markets and corporate & investment banking transformation, front-to-back operating model design, technology modernization, and regulatory change.

• Own and lead at least two key client accounts, serving as the primary relationship lead and strategic advisor.

Deliver Consulting Excellence

• Oversee complex strategy and transformation programs end-to-end, ensuring high-impact delivery that exceeds client expectations.

• Leverage global expertise and cross-functional teams to solve our clients’ toughest challenges.

Lead People & Culture

• Inspire and coach a high-performing team of Managers and above.

• Champion Sia’s inclusive, collaborative, and entrepreneurial culture, mentoring the next generation of leadership.

Shape the Future of the Firm

• Grow Sia's capital markets and corporate & investment banking practice across the U.S.

• Define and enhance Sia’s offerings, thought leadership, client pipeline, and grow the team.

• Contribute to our go-to-market strategy, client success, practice development, and firm governance at the BU and Hub level.

• Actively collaborate across international hubs and service lines to deliver integrated, cross-border value.

What you will bring:

• Based in Charlotte, with an active, senior-level financial services network across the U.S., spanning global corporate and investment banks, institutional broker-dealers, custodians, clearing houses, depositories, and other market infrastructure providers.

• 15+ years in consulting, including leadership roles in capital markets or corporate & investment banking transformation, operating model design, technology enablement, or regulatory advisory.

• A proven track record of winning and delivering multimillion-dollar consulting engagements.

• Executive presence and the ability to influence and engage C-level clients including demonstrable experience in US and Global GSIBs

• A passion for team development, coaching, and fostering a high-performance culture.

• Deep, demonstrable expertise in capital markets and corporate & investment banking, including institutional sales and trading, equities, fixed income, the front-to-back trade lifecycle, middle- and post-trade operations, securities financing, collateral management, clearing and settlement, custody, or asset servicing, with a track record of leading strategy, transformation, or regulatory-driven programs in these areas.

• Established relationships with senior executives who lead corporate & investment banking, capital markets, sales and trading, institutional operations, technology, or transformation at global banks, broker-dealers, custodians, and market infrastructure providers, including P&L owners and senior business sponsors.

• Working command of the regulatory, risk, control, and market-structure landscape shaping capital markets, including clearing and settlement, custody, recordkeeping, operational resilience, and governance, as well as the implications of extended trading hours, accelerated settlement, and technology-driven post-trade modernization.

• A recognized voice in the market, with a record of thought leadership, speaking, or industry engagement.

• A proven ability to build a practice from a small base, developing offerings, viewpoints, and a pipeline of clients and talent without an inherited book of business.

• Bachelor's required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree strongly preferred.

Compensation & Benefits

Sia invests in total rewards that support how our people work, live, and grow.

Compensation

• Base Salary: $300,000–$350,000. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by applicable law.

• Personal Sales Bonus (uncapped)

• Annual Performance Bonus (appraisal)

Benefits

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Company-paid life and AD&D insurance; voluntary supplemental insurance and EAP at no cost

• 401(k) with company match and immediate vesting; HSA and FSA

• College savings and student loan repayment programs

• Paid parental leave

• Generous PTO, nine company holidays, and one floating holiday

• Monthly cell phone stipend

• Well-being and professional development programs

Benefits are subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements.

Workplace

Sia embraces a flexible workplace model that balances autonomy with in-person connection. Management is expected to be in the office at least three days per week, serving as culture carriers who mentor teams, strengthen client relationships, and lead by example.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout their employment. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Our Commitment

At Sia, we believe in fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture where our employees and partners are valued and thrive in a sense of belonging.

Sia is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment, including hiring, promotion, remuneration, or discipline, are based solely on performance, competence, conduct, or business needs.

jobs.title: Configuration & BOM Engineer
jobs.description:
Who we are

Helsing develops artificial intelligence-enabled capabilities to protect and defend democracies. We are growing our US operations, cultivating an ambitious and committed team of mission-driven professionals to apply their skills to solve challenging problems.

The role

You will be the single owner of the Bill of Materials across our products — the person who can answer, at any moment and with confidence, what the product is made of, what it weighs, what it costs, where it comes from, and whether we can build it.

This is not a data-entry role. You will sit at the intersection of design engineering, procurement, quality and manufacturing, and you will be the one who turns a set of CAD assemblies and engineering intentions into an executable, auditable, buildable structure. You will decide how we represent our products as data, and you will hold the rest of the organization to that standard.

The day-to-day

• Maintain a single, trusted source of truth for product structure across all programs, revisions and configurations.

• Track as-designed and as-built mass at line, assembly and system level. Surface variance against allocation early, and make it visible to the people who can act on it.

• Maintain target, quoted and actual cost per line; roll up to assembly and unit cost; track cost at volume and flag drift against program targets.

• Record and verify country of origin and manufacturer for every part. Flag sourcing, export-control, ITAR/EAR and supply-chain-resilience risks to the relevant teams before they become schedule risks.

• Define and maintain the status model that the whole company runs on, including:

• Engineering released — the line is cleared by design and approved to purchase

• Sourced — a qualified supplier and part number are identified

• On order — a purchase order is placed

• EDD — a current, credible estimated delivery date is held against every open line

• Determine when an assembly's inputs are sufficiently cleared, ordered and inbound to trigger manufacturing to prepare for receiving and production. Manufacturing should be able to act on your signal without checking it.

• Run the ECO/ECN process: assess change impact on mass, cost, schedule and inventory; manage effectivity and obsolescence; ensure nothing changes in CAD without changing in the BOM.

• Define and improve our PLM/ERP data model, tooling and automation so that BOM health is continuously visible rather than periodically assembled by hand.

• Give engineering leadership and program management a clear, current view of build readiness, long-lead exposure, cost and mass position — and the specific blockers behind each.

You should apply if you

• Significant experience owning BOMs for complex electromechanical hardware in a fast-moving environment — aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, space or consumer hardware at scale.

• Deep practical fluency with PLM and ERP systems (e.g. ION, Windchill, Teamcenter, Arena, Duro, Odoo, SAP, NetSuite) and a clear view of how product data should be structured.

• Strong working knowledge of engineering change management, revision and configuration control, and effectivity.

• Comfortable reading mechanical drawings, electrical schematics and CAD assemblies, and able to challenge an engineer on what they have actually released.

• Experience working directly with procurement and suppliers on lead times, quotes, origin and qualification.

• Highly numerate and systematic. You instinctively automate repeated work — scripting, SQL or Python is a strong advantage.

• Exceptionally organized and direct. You chase the missing line. You escalate without drama. You are comfortable being the person who says "we are not OK to build."

• Able to work with ambiguity and set the standard where none exists yet.

• US Citizenship

Note: We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarized in a few bullet points.

Nice to Have

• Experience taking a product from prototype through NPI into serial production.

• Familiarity with export control (ITAR/EAR) and defense supply chain requirements.

• Experience with mass budgeting on weight-critical platforms (airborne, maritime or space).

• Background in a company that scaled its hardware function quickly.

Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields

• Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, External
jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You’ll Do

As a Senior Backend Engineer on the External Attack team, you'll contribute to the full set of backend services that power NodeZero's external pentesting capabilities, from architecture and development through deployment and production operations. You'll own parts of our core API, data processing and ETL pipelines, datalake, graph, along with the container orchestration and cloud infrastructure beneath it all. You'll be accountable for the performance, scalability, and uptime of several of these services, and you'll be a key contributor to user-facing product launches and platform stability.



Responsibilities

 - Design, build, and maintain features in our core Python API, with a focus on performance, correctness, and maintainability.

 - Design, build, and operate workflow orchestration for large-scale, long-running workloads using tools such as Prefect or Temporal, including scheduling, retries, idempotency, state management, and failure recovery.

 - Build orchestration that scales reliably across many concurrent workflows, with clear visibility into progress, failures, and throughput.

 - Comfort reading and untangling unfamiliar, complex SQL, and the judgment to optimize or refactor it safely in production.

 - Build and operate high-throughput data processing and ETL pipelines that turn large volumes of raw assessment data into reliable, queryable datasets.

 - Contribute to datalake architecture on AWS, including storage layout, partitioning, schema evolution, and query performance.

 - Deploy and manage services on Kubernetes, and take part in cluster operations, release management, and capacity planning.

 - Develop and extend GraphQL and graph-based APIs that let product components and customers explore complex relationships in their data.

 - Own the observability, uptime, and scalability of the services you build, including metrics, tracing, alerting, and on-call participation.

 - Partner with frontend engineers, product managers, and designers to turn backend capabilities into a clear, responsive user experience.

 - Contribute to systems architecture decisions and write design docs that help the team move quickly with shared understanding.

 - Collaborate with frontend team members to present data in a clear and user-friendly format, enhancing the product's user experience.



What You’ll Bring

 - The ability to own and manage concurrent initiatives, with sound judgment in prioritization and time management.

 - A self-driven approach: you can conceive and implement solutions on your own and with a team.

 - A reliability mindset for distributed work: you design for retries, partial failure, and recovery, and you debug asynchronous systems methodically.

 - A strong desire to keep learning new technologies in a fast-paced Agile environment.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, clear communication, and attention to detail.

 - A bias toward operational ownership: you care how your code behaves in production

 - Strong technical writing for design docs, runbooks, and API documentation.

 - Effective collaboration with designers, developers, and product managers.



Required Education / Experience

 - Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or related field.

 - 7+ yrs professional software engineering experience using modern object-oriented or functional languages (Python, Java, Go, Scala, C++, TypeScript, etc).

 - Experience building and running workflow orchestration or distributed task-processing systems in production (for example Prefect, Temporal, Airflow, Celery, or similar).

 - Hands-on experience designing and building high-throughput data processing systems and ETL pipelines.

 - Experience building applications on cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, GCP, using container technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.



What Sets You Apart

 - Deep Kubernetes experience, including managing deployments and clusters and troubleshooting production workloads.

 - Experience with durable-execution or workflow engines such as Temporal or Prefect, including designing workflows that are resilient, observable, and easy to evolve.

 - Experience building GraphQL backends and working with graph databases

 - A track record of owning observability, uptime, and scalability for production systems (for example Datadog, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry).

 - Systems engineering and architecture experience with datalakes and the cloud services around them.

 - Experience building platform capabilities or internal tooling that other engineering teams rely on.

 - Experience in cybersecurity or with attack surface and vulnerability data.



Only US persons can interview for this role due to security clearance requirements by our customer(s) and/or vendor(s). Employee must be eligible for and successfully secure a US Federal Security Clearance as a condition of employment.



Travel Required

We are a fully remote company, and this job may require up to 5% of travel to be successful.

 

Perks of Horizon3

 - Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

 - Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

 - Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

 - Hybrid & Remote Work: We embrace a mix of remote and hybrid work models depending on role and location, including our Chicago office, where some roles require regular in-office presence.

 - Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.



Compensation and Values

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State’s transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

 - Base salary range: $199,750 - $235,000 annually. The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.

 - Additional compensation: All full-time roles are eligible for an equity package in the form of stock options.



You Belong Here

Horizon3 is not just an equal opportunity employer - we are a community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental principles of our culture and success. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status by law.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion means we strive to attract, develop, and retain a workforce that reflects the varied communities we serve. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our ability to create cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions. At Horizon3, every team member is valued and supported in an environment that encourages personal and professional growth.

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we encourage all qualified individuals to apply. Come be a part of Horizon3, where your unique contributions are recognized, and your potential is limitless.



Other Duties

jobs.title: Principal Full-Stack Data Scientist  - Foundational Models
jobs.description:
About Stitch Fix, Inc.

Stitch Fix (NASDAQ: SFIX) Stitch Fix is redefining retail by combining human creativity with advanced data science and Generative AI. As we build the future of personalized shopping, we’re equally committed to building yours.  We believe in investing in our team as much as our technology. Join us to be a trendsetter in the industry and help us redefine what’s possible for our clients, while we help you reach your full potential.

About the Role

Stitch Fix is redefining retail by blending the art of fashion with the science of machine learning. The Foundational Models team builds and evolves the machine learning systems that power personalization and recommendations across Stitch Fix. The team owns foundational capabilities—including client and item representations, recommendation and retrieval systems, and core models such as the Client Time Series Model (CTSM)—that are leveraged across multiple client experiences and downstream applications. We foster a culture of ownership where Data Scientists manage the full lifecycle of their work. As a Senior Full-Stack Data Scientist, you will work across the full machine learning lifecycle: identifying opportunities, developing and evaluating new modeling approaches, running large-scale experiments, and deploying and operating models in production. You will tackle technically challenging problems in personalization and recommendation systems, working with large-scale behavioral, transactional, textual, and visual data.

This is a highly collaborative and hands-on role. You will partner with Data Scientists, ML Engineers, Product, and other technical teams to translate research and emerging ML techniques into reliable systems that create measurable client and business impact.

Responsibilities:

• Design, develop, evaluate, and productionize machine learning models that improve Stitch Fix's personalization and recommendation systems.

• Advance foundational modeling capabilities, including client and item representations, embeddings, retrieval, ranking, recommendation models, and assortment generation.

• Explore and apply LLMs and machine learning techniques—including deep learning, representation learning, multimodal modeling, and generative approaches—where they can meaningfully improve our systems.

• Own work across the full ML lifecycle, from problem formulation and data exploration through modeling, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

• Design rigorous offline evaluations and online experiments to understand model performance, measure client and business impact, and communicate results to stakeholders and leadership.

• Work with large-scale behavioral and product datasets using Python, SQL, and distributed data-processing tools.

• Build production-quality ML solutions with attention to scalability, reliability, latency, observability, and cost.

• Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and other Data Science teams to understand downstream needs and translate them into reusable foundational ML capabilities.

• Contribute to the technical direction of the Foundational Models team through design discussions, code reviews, research, prototyping, and development of engineering and modeling best practices.

• Communicate complex technical concepts, modeling approaches, and tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical partners.

• Mentor and collaborate with other Data Scientists and engineers, helping raise the technical bar across the team.

About You

This is what you’ll need to succeed in this role from day 1.

Requirements:

• Bachelor’s Degree in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field required. Master’s Degree or PhD preferred.

• 8+ years of experience in design and deployment of machine learning solutions, ideally in personalization, such as recommendation systems, representation learning, or search.

• Strong ability to architect technical solutions and write production-grade code in Python.

• Ability to independently drive ambiguous machine learning problems from initial exploration and prototyping through production deployment, monitoring, iteration, and measurable impact.

• Experience working with large-scale datasets using SQL and distributed data-processing technologies such as Spark.

• Experience with modern deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

• Strong understanding of model evaluation and experimentation, including offline evaluation, A/B testing, and translating model improvements into measurable product or business outcomes.

• Ability to reason about the tradeoffs involved in production ML systems, including model quality, latency, scalability, reliability, and computational cost.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence technical decisions and communicate complex concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Intellectual curiosity and a demonstrated ability to learn and apply new machine learning techniques to practical problems.

Why You’ll Love Working at Stitch Fix

• We are a group of bright, kind people who are motivated by challenge. We value integrity, innovation and trust. You’ll bring these characteristics to life in everything you do at Stitch Fix.

• We cultivate a community of diverse perspectives—all voices are heard and valued.

• We are an innovative company and leverage our strengths in fashion and tech to disrupt the future of retail.

• We win as a team, commit to our work, and celebrate grit together because we value strong relationships.

• We boldly create the future while keeping equity and sustainability at the center of all that we do.

• We are the owners of our work and are energized by solving problems through a growth mindset lens. We think broadly and creatively through every situation to create meaningful impact.

• We offer comprehensive compensation packages and inclusive health and wellness benefits.

Compensation and Benefits

This role will receive a competitive salary, benefits, and equity. The salary for US-based employees hired into this role will be aligned with the range below, which includes our three geographic areas. A variety of factors are considered when determining someone’s compensation–including a candidate’s professional background, experience, location, and performance. This position is eligible for an annual bonus, and new hire and ongoing grants of restricted stock units, depending on employee and company performance. In addition, the position is eligible for medical, dental, vision, and other benefits. Applicants should apply via our internal or external careers site.

Salary Range

$200,000—$237,000 USD

We give AI apps and agents the connectivity, context, and governance to work across more than 1,000 enterprise systems in real time, and we process over a trillion records a month doing it. DoorDash, LinkedIn, Johnson & Johnson, Instacart, and LiveRamp run mission-critical data on us. Honorable Mention in the Gartner Magic Quadrant™ for Data Integration Tools, and top-rated by customers on Gartner Peer Insights four years running. Founded 2016, remote-first, headquartered in San Mateo.

Our values are short and we actually use them: Have Empathy. Be Curious. Be Intellectually Honest. Achieve Excellence. Remember to Relax.

About the role

You’ll own the technical relationship with our accounts: onboarding, implementation, adoption, escalations, and everything that happens when a pipeline that used to work stops working.

You are the person the customer's data team calls, and the person who tells them the truth when the answer is inconvenient. Most of the job is conversation: understanding what they are actually trying to do, explaining what the platform will and will not do for them, keeping their expectations aligned with reality, and raising problems while they are still small.

The technical part matters, but not in the way people usually assume. We want a generalist who has built things before and therefore understands how the pieces fit together: what a Kubernetes cluster is for, why a VPN tunnel might be the bottleneck, what a stack trace is telling you, what a slow query looks like. You will not be asked to be the deepest engineer in the room. You will be asked to be the person who can talk to the deepest engineer in the room, understand them, and translate what they said to a VP who has thirty seconds.

What you will do

• Own the technical relationship for a portfolio of accounts. You are the continuity: the person who knows their environment, their history, and their constraints.

• Lead onboarding and implementation. Understand what the customer is trying to build, design the integration with them, and guide it to production.

• Run the hard conversations. A missed date, a degraded pipeline, a limitation they did not expect, a customer who is upset and technically wrong. You stay calm, keep credibility, and land on a next step everyone agrees to.

• Flag risk early and in writing. Adoption stalling, a champion who left, a project quietly losing sponsorship, an architecture heading somewhere that will not scale. Flagging a risk three weeks early is worth more here than fixing it heroically after it lands.

• Translate between audiences. The same situation explained to a data engineer, to a security reviewer, and to a VP, without losing any of them.

• Troubleshoot alongside the customer: failed runs, schema drift, connector and authentication failures, connectivity problems, performance issues. You do the first-line diagnosis and bring engineering a clear reproduction when it needs to escalate.

• Partner with CSM and Support on renewal risk, and hand expansion signals to Sales.

• Mentor other SAs on how to handle customers, not just how to solve problems.

What you need

Communication and customer ownership (the core of the role)

• You can explain a technical concept to a non-technical stakeholder without either dumbing it down or losing them.

• You handle conflict without escalating it. You can tell a customer no, or "that was our mistake" and keep the relationship intact.

• You build trust over months, not meetings. Customers should ask for you by name.

• You write clearly and unprompted: summaries, next steps, and owners after every meaningful call.

• You raise problems early, including your own. We would much rather hear "this is slipping and here is why" than a confident status update that turns out to be wrong.

• You push back on bad requirements instead of silently building them.

Technical breadth

You should be a generalist who has built software or data systems at some point. Not necessarily an expert in any one of these, but genuinely conversant in most of them, in the way someone is conversant after having actually worked with them:

• Python. You can read someone else's script, follow what it does, make a modification, and understand stack traces.

• SQL. Comfortable writing joins, aggregations, and filters. You can look at a slow query and have a sensible first guess about why.

• Data pipelines and integration. APIs and their common failure modes (rate limits, pagination, retries, auth expiry), webhooks, CDC, file-based ingestion, batch versus streaming trade-offs.

• Cloud data platforms. Working familiarity with at least one of Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, or a major cloud data warehouse.

• Authentication. You understand what OAuth, SSO, service accounts, and API keys are and roughly how they work. You can follow a conversation about a failing token exchange.

• Networking. DNS, firewalls, private connectivity, VPNs and SSH tunnels. You do not need to configure them, but you need to understand the concepts well enough to hold a productive call with a customer's network team and know when the network is the problem rather than the platform.

• Containers and Kubernetes. Conceptual understanding only: what a container is, what Kubernetes does, why workloads run in pods, what it means when something runs out of memory. You will not be administering clusters.

• Linux. Comfortable enough in a terminal to read a log file, check a process, or run a curl command.

Experience

• 5+ years in technical customer-facing work: solutions architecture, implementation, technical account management, professional services, consulting, support engineering, or a data engineering role that involved heavy stakeholder contact.

• At least some of that spent hands-on building, not only advising.

• Experience owning accounts or projects through delivery, not just handing off.

Nice to have

• Prior experience at a data integration, ETL, or data platform vendor.

• Background in data engineering or software engineering earlier in your career.

• Experience in a regulated industry (healthcare, financial services, insurance).

• Entrepreneurial experience or similar (having worked at a fast-paced startup environment).

What this role is not

• Not a support queue. You own outcomes on named accounts.

• Not a deep engineering role.

• Not a pure relationship role either. You need to be technical enough to earn the customer's respect in the first meeting.

Interview process

• Recruiter screen (30 min)

• Hiring manager conversation (45 min)

• Technical breadth session (60 min): troubleshooting reasoning, plus basic Python and SQL

• Customer scenario (60 min): you handle a difficult account situation with a panel playing customer roles

Why Nexla? Why now?

A few large companies - DoorDash, SentinelOne, Johnson & Johnson, LinkedIn, Amex, Integrity Marketing, among them use Nexla for data integration. Connectors, runtime, transformations, scheduling, the parts of the stack where data has to move between systems reliably.

The reason this is an interesting moment to join is what the agent shift is doing to the category. Data integration used to mean "land this data in that warehouse so a human can look at it." That product is mature. What it's becoming is closer to "an agent asks a business question, and the platform figures out which data and what code and which APIs add up to a real answer." That's a much bigger problem, and most of the architecture for it hasn't been built yet by anyone.

A concrete example. A revenue team wants to ask "which enterprise customers are showing renewal risk" and get a real answer through whatever agent or app they work in. Today there is no clean way to answer that question, it requires CRM, usage, support, and billing data joined in org-specific ways, and the calling agent can't just invoke a tool that returns the right answer unless someone first establishes whether the underlying data is even capable of producing one.

That is the system we are building. A probe agent investigates the data plane whether the right fields are populated, whether freshness is adequate, whether the joins exist, whether credentials cover the required scope and returns a grounded feasibility answer. Where there are gaps, Express.dev composes the pipelines to close them. The capability is then exposed as an MCP server: "renewal risk" as a curated product, with the business logic correct and the query semantics described well enough that the calling agent uses it as intended. The MCP Gateway governs which agents can call which capabilities, with the policies, audit, and observability an enterprise control plane requires.

The bet is that ten years of connector work, an enterprise customer base, and a runtime that already moves real volume are the right foundation to define this layer from.

jobs.title: GTM Strategy & Operations Senior Associate
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Associate to join our growing GTM Strategy & Operations team as the product owner for our GTM data and tooling products. Our team solves complex problems that require insight, creativity, and execution through building scalable processes, tools, and systems for our rapidly growing global business. You will own the roadmap, delivery, and adoption of the data products and sales productivity tools that power our Sales and Customer Success organizations, spanning both internally built products and third-party solutions, with decisions guided by speed, cost, scalability, and long-term maintainability. Doing this successfully requires a deep understanding of the “day in the life” for field teams, strong product management instincts, and the ability to translate business needs into build-versus-buy decisions and tooling solutions that help Datadog grow 10x.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

You Will

• Own the product roadmap: Set the vision, strategy, and prioritized roadmap for GTM data products and sales productivity tools. Balance field needs, business impact, technical feasibility, cost, and maintainability while making clear decisions about where to invest, consolidate, replace, or retire.

• Run the end-to-end product lifecycle for in-house tools: Write requirements and user stories, define MVPs, establish acceptance criteria, manage the backlog, and partner with GTM Systems, Data Engineering, and Analytics to ship, iterate, and sunset internally built products.

• Establish the product operating model: Create a consistent approach to intake, prioritization, roadmap planning, product ownership, release readiness, feedback collection, and lifecycle management across our portfolio of products.

• Make build-versus-buy calls: Lead structured evaluations (e.g., RFPs, pilots, time-boxed POCs) of third-party tools against in-house alternatives, build business cases, and present investment recommendations to GTM leadership

• Lead AI product strategy: Identify, evaluate, prototype, and scale AI-powered capabilities, whether built in-house or bought, that improve prospecting, enrichment, personalization, and rep workflows, and help define the forward-looking AI roadmap for the Sales and CS organizations

• Measure impact: Define and track success metrics across every tool and data product (e.g., adoption, data quality, time saved, pipeline influenced) and use the findings to make data-driven decisions to invest, consolidate, or retire

• Partner with the field: Work closely with Sales and Customer Success to uncover workflow pain points through interviews, workflow observation, usage analysis and feedback loops. Distinguish user problems from requested features and translate these opportunities into product improvements that directly increase rep productivity.

• Lead launch and adoption: Own release planning, change management, and onboarding in collaboration with Sales Enablement so field teams get maximum value from every product

• Ensure seamless integration: Work with GTM Systems to maintain and improve integrations between our tools, Salesforce CRM, and the broader GTM tech stack and data infrastructure

• Set the standard: Build and enforce governance frameworks, acceptable use policies, and data hygiene standards across all managed tools and data products to ensure consistency and compliance

Requirements

• Experience: 4-6+ years of experience in GTM Strategy & Operations, data or analytics roles, product management, or management consulting, ideally within SaaS or high-growth B2B technology

• Product management fundamentals: Proven ability to take a product from problem definition through requirements, prioritization, launch, and iteration, including writing clear PRDs, user stories, scope tradeoffs, and communicating to technical and non-technical teams why the team will or will not invest in a request.

• Build-versus-buy judgment: Experience weighing in-house development against third-party solutions on cost, speed, scalability, and strategic fit, and making a clear recommendation

• Data fluency: Strong understanding of GTM data (contacts, accounts, intent and enrichment signals) and the ability to define data quality standards; comfortable with SQL and working with data warehouses and BI tools to analyze usage and outcomes

• AI innovation: Strong interest in exploring, launching, and scaling new GTM AI technologies, including practical experience prototyping or deploying AI-enabled workflows

• Cross-functional collaboration: Strong track record of partnering with Sales, CS, Engineering, and Data teams to identify pain points and deliver solutions from requirements through rollout

• Analytical mindset: Comfortable defining product metrics, measuring adoption and ROI, and communicating findings clearly to senior stakeholders

• CRM knowledge: Solid understanding of Salesforce CRM and how data products and sales tools integrate into the broader GTM tech stack

• Communication: Effective communicator, both written and verbal, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

• Ownership mentality: Self-starter who takes initiative, operates independently, and drives projects through to completion without heavy oversight

Bonus Points

• SaaS background: Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS company managing a GTM or sales tool portfolio or an internal data product

• AI passion: Stays current on the latest AI news, has a passion for experimentation, has fully integrated AI into professional workflows, and vibe codes on the weekend

• Technical aptitude: Working knowledge of APIs and how sales tools connect to CRM systems and data infrastructure; has shipped a prototype or internal tool of their own

• Tool fluency: Hands-on familiarity with the B2B sales technology landscape, including contact intelligence (e.g., ZoomInfo, Cognism), outbound sequencing (e.g., Groove, Salesloft, Outreach), and data enrichment tools (e.g., Clay, Clearbit, Crunchbase)

• Broader stack exposure: Familiarity with adjacent tools such as buyer intent platforms (e.g., Bombora, G2) or conversation intelligence (e.g., Gong)

jobs.title: Associate Director, Compliance Training
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

The Associate Director, Compliance Training will own the design, development, delivery and continuous improvement of the compliance training program supporting Revolution Medicines’ US commercial operations (sales, marketing, market access, medical affairs, patient services and commercial operations).

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Compliance Training, this senior individual contributor will translate legal, regulatory and policy requirements (FDA, federal Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act, OIG guidance, PhRMA Code, Sunshine Act/Open Payments, state laws) into engaging, risk-based learning; serve as a trusted advisor to business stakeholders; and lead through influence without direct reports.

Key Responsibilities:

• Support the end-to-end US commercial compliance training program, including annual training plan, curriculum roadmap and calendar aligned with the Compliance program’s risk assessment and priorities.

• Design and develop risk-based curricula and content (eLearning, live/virtual instructor-led, microlearning, case studies, job aids, certifications) on topics such as HCP interactions, promotional and off-label communications, speaker programs, meals and HCP engagements, grants and sponsorships, patient support programs, anti-kickback, Open Payments/transparency reporting, privacy and interactions with patient advocacy organizations.

• Apply adult learning principles and instructional design methodologies (g., ADDIE, SAM) to create engaging, role-specific training for field sales, market access, medical, marketing and home-office audiences.

• Lead onboarding compliance training for new commercial hires and launch-readiness training for new product launches, indications and field force expansions.

• Deliver live training at national and regional sales meetings, POA meetings and cross-functional forums; train-the-trainer support for commercial training partners.

• Translate new or updated policies, SOPs, regulations, industry guidance and enforcement trends (e.g., OIG Special Fraud Alerts, OIG General Compliance Program Guidance, DOJ Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs, CIA-derived practices) into timely training and communications.

• Serve as business owner/administrator for compliance content within the Learning Management System (e.g., Veeva, Workday Learning, Cornerstone, SuccessFactors): curriculum assignments, audience mapping, due dates, escalations, completion tracking and reporting; partner with L&D/HRIS on system enhancements.

• Establish and report training metrics and KPIs (completion rates, assessment results, effectiveness measures, knowledge checks) to Compliance leadership and the Compliance Committee; maintain audit-ready training records and documentation.

• Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Commercial Training/L&D, Sales Leadership, Marketing, Medical Affairs, Market Access, HR and Compliance Monitoring/Auditing to align training with business needs and integrate monitoring and investigation insights into targeted remediation training.

• Manage external vendors and instructional design/eLearning agencies, including scoping, SOWs, budget tracking, timelines and quality review; coordinate content through legal/regulatory/compliance review.

• Develop compliance communications and awareness campaigns (e.g., newsletters, Compliance Week, FAQs, quick reference guides) that reinforce a speak-up culture and ethical decision-making.

• Continuously evaluate and improve the program, benchmarking against industry best practices and emerging learning technologies.

Additional Responsibilities and Role Evolution

• As a growing organization, our compliance function and compliance training program continue to evolve to meet changing business needs. The responsibilities outlined in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by the individual in this role and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications.

• The Associate Directro, Compliance Training will be expected to take on additional assignments, projects, and responsibilities as needed to support the Compliance team and broader business objectives. Responsibilities may change, expand, or shift over time based on organizational priorities, business growth, process improvements, technology implementations, and evolving legal, regulatory and industry requirements.

• The successful candidate will demonstrate flexibility, adaptability, and a willingness to contribute beyond the core responsibilities of the position, partnering collaboratively across functions to support the continued success and growth of the company.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor’s degree required.

• 8+ years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years in healthcare compliance, compliance training, or commercial training with a significant compliance component.

• Demonstrated experience building and managing compliance training programs supporting US commercial operations, including field sales and product launch environments.

• Strong working knowledge of US healthcare laws and industry codes, including the FDCA and FDA promotional regulations, federal Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act, OIG compliance program guidance, PhRMA Code on Interactions with Health Care Professionals, and Sunshine Act/Open Payments.

• Proven expertise in instructional design and adult learning principles, with experience using eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate Storyline/Rise, Adobe Captivate).

• Hands-on experience administering training content and reporting within an LMS.

• Excellent presentation and facilitation skills, with the ability to engage audiences ranging from field representatives to senior leadership.

• Exceptional written communication skills and the ability to translate complex legal and regulatory concepts into clear, practical guidance.

• Demonstrated ability to lead through influence, manage multiple priorities and projects under tight timelines, and collaborate effectively across functions without direct authority.

• High degree of integrity, sound judgment and discretion in handling sensitive information.

• Ability to travel domestically up to approximately 10-15% (g., national/regional sales meetings).

Preferred Skills:

• Advanced degree (MBA, M.Ed., or related field) or professional certification such as CCEP, CHC, CPTD or instructional design certification.

• Experience supporting oncology or specialty pharmaceutical product launches.

• Experience at a company operating under, or with processes informed by, a Corporate Integrity Agreement.

• Familiarity with LMS platforms such as Workday Learning, Cornerstone or SuccessFactors.

• Experience with learning analytics and measuring training effectiveness.

• Working knowledge of state marketing and transparency laws, state price transparency requirements, HIPAA, and patient support program compliance.

• Experience developing video, gamified, or scenario-based interactive learning.

jobs.title: Applied Research - Sovereign AI
jobs.description:
OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

National institutions, public-sector organizations, and regulated industries need capable models and agents that operate within strict boundaries around data, deployment, access, auditability, and human authority. They also need the ability to improve those systems on their own workflows rather than depend indefinitely on a closed external model. You will build post-training and agent systems in public-sector and regulated-industry settings.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Role scope

The work happens inside partner constraints, sometimes on their infrastructure and under their access rules.

Representative early problems

 - Build a private improvement loop that turns sensitive traces into environments, training signal, evaluations, and deployable model updates without crossing the operator's data boundary.

 - Train a tool-using domain agent whose actions are permissioned, traceable, recoverable, and evaluated against real procedures rather than generic benchmarks.

 - Develop high-assurance evaluations for reliability, calibration, robustness, human escalation, and compliance with domain constraints under adversarial or changing conditions.

What you will own

 - Improvement loops that run end to end inside the operator's boundary, from trace selection to deployed update.

 - Agents with explicit permissions, evidence trails, bounded tools, and human checkpoints.

 - Evaluations that test reliability, calibration, recovery, and compliance with real procedures.

 - Experiments on how privacy, access, and infrastructure constraints change learning, with methods that transfer across high-assurance settings.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Relevant experience: RL/post-training, private ML systems, high-assurance evaluation, agent safety, regulated-domain ML, public-sector technical work, or deployment under strict data and infrastructure constraints.

 - You should want to build and evaluate these systems directly.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

 - Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

 - Visa Sponsorship & relocation support

 - Professional Development budget

 - Team Off-sites & conference attendance

If you're excited about the opportunity to build the foundation for the future of decentralized AI and create a platform that empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what's possible, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Applied Research - Quantitative Finance
jobs.description:
OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

Quantitative finance is a demanding setting for agentic reinforcement learning: observations are noisy and non-stationary, actions have delayed and path-dependent consequences, naive objectives invite exploitation, and a convincing historical result can disappear under costs, constraints, or a new regime. You will build environments, evaluations, agents, and post-training methods for quantitative research and systematic decision-making. We have active programs with quantitative funds and other finance teams. The work may span research agents, market and portfolio simulators, time-series reasoning, execution, risk, and the production feedback loops that connect hypotheses to deployed systems.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

 - Build a quantitative-research environment where an agent forms a hypothesis, writes and runs analysis, runs a backtest on point-in-time data, diagnoses the result, and decides what to test next.

 - Design rewards and evaluations that distinguish durable improvement from the artifacts of look-ahead bias, data leakage, overfitting, favorable execution assumptions, or hidden concentration and tail risk.

 - Train long-horizon agents to use data, research, coding, simulation, and portfolio tools while preserving provenance, respecting risk constraints, and adapting when market conditions change.

What you will own

 - Environments grounded in point-in-time data, realistic market mechanics, transaction costs, latency, capacity, and operational constraints.

 - Agents that conduct quantitative research, use analytical and execution tools, inspect their evidence, and recover from failed hypotheses.

 - Verifiers and evaluations that test robust out-of-sample behavior across assets, horizons, regimes, and adverse conditions.

 - Production loops with monitoring, human authority, regression gates, and failure attribution across models, data, simulation, and infrastructure, producing methods that transfer to other noisy, high-stakes decision systems.


REQUIREMENTS

 - We are looking first for depth in RL, agents, or post-training systems and the ability to become fluent in quantitative research.

 - Prior work in systematic trading, market microstructure, time-series modeling, econometrics, or financial simulation is useful but not required.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

 - Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

 - Visa Sponsorship & relocation support

 - Professional Development budget

 - Team Off-sites & conference attendance

If you're excited about the opportunity to build the foundation for the future of decentralized AI and create a platform that empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what's possible, we'd love to hear from you.

WHAT we do is every bit as important as HOW we do it! Our work together is guided by four enduring core values:

Summary:

This role within Technical Operations’ Commercialization Capabilities and Strategic Projects function is critical for building and strengthening the business operations, data, digital tools, and performance insights that help Technical Operations leaders make better decisions, allocate resources effectively, anticipate risks, and execute with greater clarity as the organization advances toward commercialization and future growth.

This role creates an integrated view of Technical Operations priorities, capacity, risks, dependencies, progress, and performance, while identifying opportunities to simplify and automate how the organization works. Working across Technical Operations and with teams across Vaxcyte, this role will translate business needs into practical, scalable solutions that improve visibility, decision-making, and organizational performance.

The successful candidate combines strong business judgment with analytical, systems, and digital fluency. This is not simply a reporting or technology role; it calls for someone who understands how the business operates, can turn data into actionable insight, and can apply systems, automation, analytics, and AI to strengthen the organization’s ability to scale.

Essential Functions:

Business Operations & Portfolio Management:

• Build and continuously improve business operating practices that give leaders an integrated view of Technical Operations priorities, initiatives, capacity, risks, dependencies, milestones, and performance.

• Establish and support portfolio and capacity-management processes that enable proactive prioritization, resource tradeoffs, and leadership decisions.

• Support demand intake, strategy realization, and execution-readiness processes with business analysis, data, and decision support.

• Partner with leaders to identify resource constraints, emerging risks, cross-functional dependencies, and opportunities that need leadership attention.

• Develop scalable operating rhythms and business review mechanisms that connect strategy, portfolio performance, and organizational decision-making.

Performance Insights & Decision Support:

• Develop executive dashboards, KPIs, reporting, and operational insights that improve visibility and enable timely, data-informed decisions.

• Create shared visibility into priorities, risks, progress, improvement efforts, and performance where transparency improves execution.

• Translate complex operational data into clear insights, scenarios, tradeoffs, and recommendations for leadership.

• Establish sustainable performance-management practices that connect strategic priorities to measurable execution and business outcomes.
