jobs.description:
OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

You will own applied RL programs from the first ambiguous customer problem through a deployed improvement loop. You will understand the workflow and business stakes, decide what can be measured and learned, build the environment and evaluation, run post-training experiments, deploy the result, and determine what should generalize into Prime's shared stack. The majority of your work will be organized around external programs. You will work directly with customer researchers, engineers, and leaders, and you will be accountable for both the research result and its practical impact.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Role scope

We have active programs across technology, science, engineering, regulated industries, and the public sector.

Representative early problems

 - Turn a partially documented workflow and business goal into an environment, baseline, and evaluation that the customer team agrees measures the right outcome.

 - Improve a domain agent through RL or another post-training method while separating model limitations from task, harness, inference, and integration failures.

 - Carry a successful experiment into deployment, measure its effect on the customer outcome, and convert the recurring parts into reusable environments, recipes, data loops, or platform capabilities.

What you will own

 - Technical and business discovery that produces a clear research plan, success measure, environment, and baseline.

 - RL, distillation, and other post-training experiments tied to deployment outcomes.

 - Agent systems that handle tool use, memory, recovery, long horizons, and human oversight.

 - Deployment and adoption decisions, plus reusable artifacts carried back to Prime's research, engineering, and product teams.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Relevant experience: customer-embedded technical work, research engineering, technical founding experience, applied ML consulting with real build ownership, or end-to-end post-training programs.

 - You should be comfortable with senior external teams and able to connect experimental evidence to business decisions without lowering the research bar.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

 - Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

 - Visa Sponsorship & relocation support

 - Professional Development budget

 - Team Off-sites & conference attendance

If you're excited about the opportunity to build the foundation for the future of decentralized AI and create a platform that empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what's possible, we'd love to hear from you.

🔹 Title: Senior Financial Analyst

📍 Locations (Remote): United States (East Coast)

💼 Role Type: Individual Contributor

⭐ OPPORTUNITY HIGHLIGHTS

Are you passionate about turning financial data into strategic business decisions? Do you enjoy building financial models, owning planning processes end to end, and partnering with leadership to drive business performance?

SafeBreach is looking for a Senior Financial Analyst to own and drive the company’s financial planning and analysis function. This is a high-visibility, hands-on role with direct exposure to the CFO, executive team, and investors. You will lead the annual budgeting process and rolling forecasts, deliver executive-level financial reporting, and partner closely with Sales, Marketing, HR, and Accounting to support business decisions.

This is an opportunity to take real ownership, build scalable financial processes, and help shape the future of a finance function that puts AI at the center of how it works.

👋 WHO WE ARE

SafeBreach is on a mission to help organizations have certainty in their security. Long trusted as the global leader in adversarial exposure validation (AEV), SafeBreach empowers organizations to take command of risk by operationalizing the full CTEM lifecycle with the SafeBreach CTEM Platform. Powered by the SafeBreach Helm AI infrastructure layer and grounded in the award-winning SafeBreach Exposure Validation Platform, the SafeBreach CTEM Platform is the first enterprise-grade, closed-loop solution designed to move organizations beyond siloed security activities toward a continuous, intelligence-driven exposure management program. Backed by world-renowned threat researchers and an unrivaled customer success team, SafeBreach provides the capabilities enterprises need to holistically understand threat exposure, make data-driven decisions that reduce risk, and measurably improve cyber resilience—safely and at scale. We are a team of passionate security professionals and innovators. If you’re ready to tackle complex security challenges and make a tangible impact on enterprise defense, we’d love to meet you.

💰 WHAT WE OFFER

• Excellent growth opportunities: Make an impact and advance your career

• Fully remote work and flexible PTO

• Highly competitive salary and equity grants

• Health, dental and vision insurance

• Generous Parental leave

• Monthly phone and internet stipend

• Learning & Development stipend

• Competitive employee referral bonus program

🚀 THE IMPACT YOU WILL HAVE

• Budgeting & Forecasting: Own the annual budget, monthly rolling forecasts, and quarterly reforecasts. Analyze budget variances and partner with department heads on financial planning.

• Executive & Investor Reporting: Prepare management reports, board presentations, and investor materials. Present financial insights and recommendations directly to the executive team.

• SaaS Metrics & Analysis: Track key metrics such as ARR, NRR/GRR, churn, CAC, LTV, and burn multiple to support strategic decision-making.

• Go-to-Market Partnership: Partner with Sales and Marketing on revenue forecasting, pipeline analysis, capacity planning, commissions, and marketing ROI.

• Accounting & Compliance: Collaborate with Accounting on month-end close, revenue recognition (ASC 606), audits, and tax-related analysis.

• AI & Automation: Use AI tools to improve financial modeling and reporting, automate recurring processes, and reduce manual work across the finance function.

🧬 WHAT SETS YOU APART

• 5–8 years of FP&A experience, including at least 2 years in B2B SaaS or software. Investment banking, PE, or Big 4 transaction services experience combined with SaaS FP&A is also relevant.

• Proven ownership of a full annual budget cycle and rolling forecasts, with expert three-statement and driver-based modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets.

• Deep understanding of SaaS metrics and ARR-based revenue models, with working knowledge of ASC 606.

• Experience presenting directly to C-level executives; board or investor exposure is a plus.

• Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in finance, with examples of practical applications.

• Ability to operate independently with high ownership, navigate ambiguity, and communicate financial insights clearly to non-finance stakeholders.

• BA/BS in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

💥 EVEN BETTER IF YOU HAVE

• CPA, CFA, or MBA.

• Experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and financial planning tools such as Adaptive, Pigment, Mosaic, Cube, or similar platforms.

• Experience with SQL, Python, or BI tools such as Looker, Tableau, or Power BI.

• Exposure to debt financing, fundraising, or M&A processes.

• Experience working with international entities, including multi-currency and intercompany transactions.

🤝 HOW WE'LL GET TO KNOW EACH OTHER

We view interviewing as a two-way street. We want you to interview us just as much as we interview you! (Avg. timeline: 21-28 days)

Step 1: The Intro (15 min)

A casual meeting with the Talent team to break the ice.

Step 2: The Vision (45 min meeting)

Connect your future manager to discuss the role, the challenges, and how you can make an impact

Step 3: The Home Assignment

An opportunity to demonstrate your skills through a practical assignment.

Step 4: The Presentation

Present your assignment and walk us through your approach and recommendations.

Step 5: The Business Perspective

A peer interview focused on Go-to-Market and cross-functional collaboration.

Step 6: The HR Interview

A conversation with our People team to discuss culture, values, and mutual fit.

Step 4: The Offer

If the vibe is right, we make it official!

DEI&B (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Belonging)

At SafeBreach, we celebrate the rich diversity of our team, where every employee's unique perspective is a valued thread in our collective success. We are unwavering in our commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace that nurtures a sense of belonging and empowers each individual to unleash their full potential. We are dedicated to creating opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and meaningful career growth, ensuring that every voice is not just heard, but cherished.

jobs.title: Mechanical Technician III
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

Rocket Lab Robotics

At Rocket Lab Robotics, we build robotic systems that push the boundaries of what's possible in space. From Mars-proven robotic arms to precision motion control systems for the most demanding environments in our solar system, our team delivers advanced electro-mechanical solutions for planetary exploration and various satellite programs. We've engineered hardware that has operated on the surface of Mars on NASA's Perseverance rover, supported lunar exploration through the CADRE rover program, and developed precision mechanisms for spacecraft subsystems including solar array drives, antenna gimbals, and optical payloads. As part of Rocket Lab, we combine the focus of small, dedicated robotics teams with the resources of a leading end-to-end space company, empowering some of the boldest missions in history. We're looking for people who take ownership and drive a problem from first principles all the way through manufacturing and delivery.

ELECTRO-MECHANICAL TECHNICIAN III

We are currently seeking a Electro-Mechanical Technician to join our manufacturing team. The Electro-Mechanical Technician will play a crucial part in the precision assembly of avionics and electronic systems.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

• Work on a high caliber cross functional team

• Perform mechanical and electrical assembly of PCB assemblies for flight hardware

• Build electrical sub-assemblies and fabricate wire harnesses

• Execute soldering and resoldering operations on through-hole and SMT components

• Support conformal coating, masking, epoxy application and coating operations

• Support mechanical assembly and integration of electro-mechanical systems

• Assist with functional testing on flight and non-flight hardware

• Fabricate first article harness assemblies and prototype electro-mechanical assemblies

• Validate parts lists for avionics and electronics hardware

• Assist with development of production processes for first-time production runs

• Watch the hardware you build evolve into a completed Rocket and go to space

• Uphold shop cleanliness and organization

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS AN ELECTRO-MECHANICAL TECHNICIAN I:

• High School Diploma or GED with relevant experience in electro-mechanical assembly

• Proficiency in both through-hole and SMT soldering/resoldering techniques

• Experience using or soldering under a microscope

• Demonstrated experience fabricating harnesses and electro-mechanical assemblies

• Proven experience in prototype development and first article builds

• Experience performing electronic testing and inspection using portable measuring devices

• Ability to read, interpret, and follow schematics, engineering drawings, circuit layouts, and parts lists

• Proficient with computers and MS Office applications (Outlook, Excel, Word)

• Due to program requirements, must be a U.S Citizen

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

• Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to focus

• Regularly required to sit, use hands and fingers, operate computer keyboard and controls, and communicate verbally and in writing

• Must be physically able to commute to buildings

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion.

Hourly Pay Range (CA Only)

$28—$35 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

Chip design is a natural fit for agentic reinforcement learning: long-horizon work, specialized tools, expensive mistakes, hard constraints, and objective feedback from simulation, verification, timing, power, and area. You will build agents, environments, evaluations, and post-training systems for real semiconductor design and verification workflows. The work is grounded in an external design workflow, with access to relevant domain experts and toolchains. It may span RTL generation and debugging, formal verification, simulation, physical design, optimization, and orchestration across EDA tools.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

 - Build an interactive verification environment where an agent reads a specification, writes or repairs RTL, invokes simulation or formal tools, interprets failures, and iterates toward a verified result.

 - Design rewards and evaluations that combine functional correctness with tool efficiency, robustness, and performance/power/area constraints without opening easy shortcuts.

 - Train long-horizon agents to recover from design and tool failures, preserve useful state, and generalize across blocks, designs, and constraint sets.

What you will own

 - Interactive environments where agents use EDA tools to modify designs, debug failures, and plan multi-step work.

 - Verifiers and rewards grounded in tests, simulation, formal methods, design rules, and engineering outcomes.

 - Experiments on credit assignment when feedback arrives late and several tools contribute.

 - Evaluations for correctness, recovery, and generalization, with reusable methods for other simulator-grounded engineering domains.


REQUIREMENTS

 - We are looking first for depth in RL, agents, or post-training systems and the ability to become fluent in semiconductor workflows.

 - Prior work in design automation, compilers, formal methods, or ML for systems is useful but not required.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

 - Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

 - Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

 - Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.

The Community Strategy Manager will provide the operational and analytical backbone that allows the Community Strategy Leadership to focus on designing and executing on a cross-functional vision for the connection between our customers and their community partners. jobs.title: Entry-level Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Woodard & Curran is an employee-owned engineering, science, and operations firm dedicated to clean water, a safe environment, healthy communities, and happy people. We foster an inclusive, collaborative culture that supports professional growth, flexibility, and meaningful work, empowering our employees to make a lasting impact on our clients, communities, and the planet.


We are recruiting for an entry-level scientist to work in our Duluth, Georgia office who can support environmental assessment, compliance, and remediation projects as part of a multi-disciplinary team. Successful candidates will be interested in ecology, wildlife biology, soil science, hydrology, environmental policy, geography, botany, earth sciences, natural resources stewardship, and water resource management. This position would report to and interact with senior scientists, engineers, and project managers, and would be involved with industrial, linear utility, oil and gas, water resources, site remediation, ecological restoration/conservation, and other environmental engineering projects. The right candidate will be professional, courteous, self-motivated, and diligent. The preferred candidate will be flexible team player and should be prepared to travel for up to 2-4 weeks at a time for certain assignments.
 
Typical field work activities would likely include wetland and waterbody delineations, stream assessments, threatened and endangered species habitat surveys, global positioning system (GPS) data collection, environmental site assessments, environmental sampling (i.e. soil, surface water, ground water, wastewater, etc.), and erosion and sediment control (E&SC) inspections.  Typical office duties would include assistance with technical report preparation, preparation of environmental permit applications, desktop analysis of project sites using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), GIS mapping of field-collected scientific data, assistance with development of presentations for technical workshops and conferences, communication with local/state/federal regulatory agencies, and some limited client communications.

jobs.title: Director, Development — Metro DC Area
jobs.description:
ABOUT PER SCHOLAS:

For 30 years, Per Scholas has been on a mission to drive mobility and opportunity in the ever-advancing technology landscape by unlocking the untapped potential of individuals, uplifting communities, and meeting the needs of employers through rigorous tech training. By teaming up with dynamic employer partners, ranging from Fortune 500 companies to innovative startups, we're forging inclusive tech talent pipelines, fulfilling an ever-increasing need for skilled talent. With national remote training and campuses in 20+ cities and counting, Per Scholas offers no-cost training programs in the most sought-after tech skills, spanning Cloud, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, IT Support, Software Engineering, and more. To date, 30,000+ individuals have been trained through Per Scholas, propelling their professional trajectories into high-growth tech careers with salaries three times higher than their pre-training earnings. Learn more by visiting PerScholas.org and follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.

Per Scholas candidates must reside in one of the following states, provided the position does not carry a specific office location requirement: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, MD, MA, MI, MO, NC, NJ, NY, OH, PA, TX, WA.

OFFICE: DC Metro Area (Baltimore and Northern VA)
REPORTS TO: VP of Local Markets

Per Scholas is seeking a strategic, entrepreneurial, and results-driven Director, Development to lead development efforts in the Metro DC, Baltimore, and northern VA and other markets as assigned. The Director will have primary responsibility for building and growing a sustainable local revenue pipeline in the NCR area, while also supporting development priorities, opportunities, and portfolios in additional Per Scholas markets as organizational needs and priorities evolve.

The Director will focus on four core areas of work: generating new local leads and building market pipelines, stewarding and growing a portfolio of local partners, advancing government funding opportunities, and collaborating with national channel teams on larger and multi-market investments.

This role is designed to strengthen Per Scholas' presence and revenue potential in the metro DC area while providing flexible development capacity across other assigned markets. The Director will develop relationships across corporate, philanthropic, civic, workforce-development, and public-sector communities and work closely with local market leadership to understand growth priorities and translate those priorities into compelling opportunities for investment.

In the NCR area, the Director will serve as the primary development lead, building a strong local pipeline, cultivating and growing relationships, advancing government funding opportunities, and partnering closely with NCR market leadership. The Director may also be assigned to support other markets where additional development capacity, prospecting, portfolio management, or strategic opportunity development is needed.

The Director will also serve as a critical connector between local markets and Per Scholas' national development infrastructure, ensuring that local intelligence and relationships inform national channel strategies while coordinating partner engagement across teams.

This is a highly collaborative position requiring close partnership with Corporate, Foundation, Government Relations & Contracts, Individual Giving, Development Operations, Program, Finance, and local market leadership.

The ideal candidate is a relationship-oriented fundraiser and business developer who combines strong prospecting and pipeline-building skills with disciplined portfolio management, strategic thinking, and the ability to navigate complex, cross-functional partnerships across the NCR area and other assigned markets.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

In this role, you will focus on four core priorities:

Generate local leads and build a strong development pipeline in the NCR area and other assigned markets

Steward and grow a portfolio of local partners

Identify and advance government funding opportunities

Collaborate with national channel teams on larger and multi-market opportunities

Local Lead Generation & Pipeline Development

• Build and continually expand a qualified pipeline of prospective corporate, philanthropic, civic, and public-sector partners in the NCR area and other assigned markets.

• Proactively identify new funding prospects through research, networking, referrals, community engagement, and existing Per Scholas relationships.

• Develop relationships with NCR-area business, philanthropic, civic, and workforce-development leaders, while also supporting relationship development in other assigned markets.

• Use market intelligence, Salesforce data, and other prospecting tools to prioritize opportunities based on potential value, strategic alignment, relationship strength, likelihood of success, and timing.

• Create and execute prospect strategies that move relationships from identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, and close.

• Build a balanced pipeline that includes both near-term revenue opportunities and longer-term strategic prospects across the NCR area and assigned markets.

• Maintain accurate and actionable pipeline information in Salesforce, including prospect stage, next steps, anticipated timing, relationship ownership, and revenue potential.

• Work closely with NCR market leadership, other assigned market leaders, and national channel colleagues to identify warm introductions and leverage existing relationships.

• Develop strategies to convert emerging relationships into sustained philanthropic, corporate, and public-sector partnerships.

Local Portfolio Stewardship & Revenue Growth

• Manage and steward a portfolio of local corporate, foundation, philanthropic, and other partners, with primary responsibility for the NCR area and additional markets as assigned.

• Build trusted relationships with funders and partners by understanding their priorities and connecting them to Per Scholas' mission, outcomes, and local market opportunities.

• Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, renewal, and stewardship strategies for portfolio accounts.

• Identify opportunities to deepen existing relationships through increased investment, multi-year commitments, expanded engagement, sponsorships, or other forms of partnership.

• Ensure partners receive timely, meaningful, and high-quality stewardship in coordination with program, market, and development colleagues.

• Maintain strong knowledge of portfolio partner priorities, giving history, relationships, engagement, and potential for future investment.

• Lead or support proposals, presentations, solicitations, renewals, and negotiations for local funding opportunities.

• Develop strategies to retain and grow key partners while continually identifying opportunities to introduce new prospects into the portfolio.

• Ensure portfolio activity, relationship strategies, and revenue forecasts are accurately reflected in Salesforce.

Government Funding Opportunities

• Partner closely with the Government Relations & Contracts team to identify, qualify, and advance local, state, and federal government funding opportunities relevant to the NCR area and other assigned markets.

• Develop and maintain relationships with relevant government, workforce-development, economic-development, and civic stakeholders throughout the NCR area and, as assigned, other markets.

• Bring local market intelligence, relationships, and emerging opportunities to the Government Relations & Contracts team to inform public funding strategies.

• Identify government funding opportunities that align with Per Scholas' workforce-development programs, learner outcomes, and market growth priorities.

• Support the development of government proposals, applications, contracts, and related materials by coordinating with Government Relations & Contracts, Program, Finance, and other internal partners.

• Coordinate local government engagement while ensuring alignment with Per Scholas' broader government funding strategy.

• Track emerging public-sector priorities, funding announcements, workforce initiatives, and policy developments that may create opportunities for Per Scholas.

• Help position Per Scholas as a trusted workforce-development partner in the NCR area and other assigned markets.

Collaboration with National Channel Teams

• Collaborate closely with Per Scholas' Corporate, Foundation, Government Relations & Contracts, and Individual Giving teams to identify and advance larger, strategic, or multi-market opportunities.

• Serve as a local market connector for national channel teams, providing NCR-specific and other assigned-market relationships, intelligence, context, and opportunities.

• Coordinate partner strategy and engagement across local and national teams to ensure clear roles, consistent communication, and a seamless partner experience.

• Identify when a local prospect has the potential to become a larger or multi-market partnership and engage the appropriate channel team early in the process.

• Support national channel teams in cultivating relationships with companies, foundations, and other funders that have a presence or strategic interest in the NCR area or other assigned markets.

• Participate in joint cultivation, site visits, meetings, proposals, presentations, solicitations, and stewardship activities as appropriate.

• Ensure local market priorities and opportunities are represented in broader channel strategies.

• Help resolve relationship ownership and coordination questions across local and national teams in partnership with development leadership.

NCR Market Partnership & Growth

• Partner closely with NCR market leadership to understand programmatic priorities, learner demand, employer needs, and market growth opportunities.

• Translate NCR's programmatic and workforce-development priorities into compelling cases for investment.

• Build Per Scholas' visibility and relationships within the NCR business, philanthropic, civic, government, and workforce-development ecosystem.

• Identify strategic relationships that can contribute not only to revenue generation but also to employer engagement, program growth, community visibility, and long-term market sustainability.

• Support NCR market leadership and national development leaders with funder meetings, site visits, community events, and other high-value engagement opportunities.

• Represent Per Scholas at relevant NCR-area community, philanthropic, business, government, and workforce-development events.

• Contribute NCR market intelligence and recommendations to broader Per Scholas development and growth strategies.

• Help establish and strengthen Per Scholas' position as a leading workforce-development and economic-mobility partner in the NCR area.

• Apply lessons, relationships, and strategies developed in the NCR area to support other assigned markets and contribute to broader local-market development.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Professional Qualifications

• 7+ years of progressive experience in fundraising, business development, corporate partnerships, sales, or a related revenue-generating field, with demonstrated success securing significant investments.

• Proven ability to generate new leads, build qualified pipelines, cultivate relationships, and convert prospects into revenue.

• Demonstrated success managing and growing a portfolio of corporate, philanthropic, or institutional partners.

• Experience securing or supporting significant philanthropic, corporate, government, or public-sector investments.

• Experience developing or supporting government funding proposals, grants, contracts, or public-sector partnerships strongly preferred.

• Strong knowledge of the NCR-area corporate, philanthropic, civic, government, and workforce-development landscape, with the ability to quickly develop market knowledge and relationships in other assigned markets.

• Established relationships with NCR-area corporate, foundation, philanthropic, civic, workforce-development, or public-sector leaders strongly preferred.

• Exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior executives, funders, government leaders, and community stakeholders.

• Strong prospecting and business-development skills, including the ability to identify new opportunities and independently move relationships forward.

• Excellent proposal-writing, presentation, case-making, and solicitation skills.

• Highly organized and disciplined in managing multiple prospects, portfolio relationships, deadlines, and cross-functional initiatives across multiple markets.

• Highly data-driven and results-oriented, with experience using pipeline and revenue data to prioritize activity and manage performance.

• Proficiency with Salesforce or another CRM; ability to maintain accurate pipeline, portfolio, forecasting, and relationship-management data.

• Strong financial acumen and ability to manage revenue forecasts, pipeline projections, and funding opportunities.

• Ability to collaborate effectively across local market teams and national development channels without relying solely on formal reporting relationships.

• Willingness to travel approximately 15–20%, including travel within the NCR area, to other assigned markets, and nationally as needed.

Personal Attributes

• Entrepreneurial and proactive, with a demonstrated ability to create opportunities rather than wait for them to emerge.

• Relationship-driven, with the ability to build authentic connections across corporate, philanthropic, government, and civic communities.

• Pipeline-oriented and persistent, with comfort initiating new relationships and moving prospects through a development cycle.

• Strategic and collaborative, with the ability to determine when an opportunity should be pursued locally and when to engage a national channel team.

• Highly organized and accountable, with strong follow-through on both revenue opportunities and partner relationships.

• Solutions-oriented, bringing forward recommendations, identifying barriers, and finding ways to move opportunities forward.

• Adaptable and comfortable with ambiguity, particularly in a growing organization where market assignments and opportunities may evolve.

• Strong communicator, able to translate Per Scholas' mission, learner outcomes, and workforce-development model into a compelling case for investment.

• Mission-driven, with a commitment to advancing economic mobility, workforce development, equity, and opportunity through Per Scholas' work.

#LI-Hybrid

For this role specifically, we are targeting a salary range of $105,000–$115,000, where the difference in salary is typically determined by several factors, including geography in which the selected candidate resides and alignment with qualifications and experience.

Benefits & Perks

Per Scholas offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and overall quality of life!

Holidays & PTO: Full-Time Per Scholas team members enjoy over 40 days of paid time off each year through a mix of holidays, vacation, and sick/personal time! All employees are eligible for Holiday pay upon hire (a total of 22 holidays annually, including a week off for Independence day and a week before the New Year). Full-Time Benefits Eligible employees also receive 80 Wellness Hours to use for Sick, Safe, or Personal reasons and accrue Vacation at a rate of 8 hours at the beginning of every month, supporting rest, recharge, and work-life balance. Vacation accruals increase with tenure. Part-time employees are afforded time off on a prorated basis and in accordance with local requirements.

Comprehensive Medical Coverage: Benefit eligible employees can choose from multiple medical plans through Cigna or Kaiser Permanente (where available), with options to fit your needs. Eligible employees also have access to a Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) that reimburses eligible out-of-pocket expenses, up to $4,000 for individuals and $8,000 for families.

Dental and Vision Insurance: Eligible employees can select from two dental plan options and a vision plan. Employees who waive medical coverage receive employer paid dental and vision premiums.

Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a current 100% employer match on contributions up to 6%, eligible employees are offered entry and full vesting after 90 days with the company.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Free, confidential, 24/7 access to counseling, legal support, and financial resources for employees and their household members

Parental Leave: Eligible employees are offered up to 6 weeks of 100% paid parental leave to support employees as they welcome a new child and bond with their family.

Additional Benefits & Perks: Eligible employees have access to employer-paid life and AD&D Insurance, as well as employer-paid short-term disability coverage, with the option to elect additional life coverage and long-term disability insurance. Flexible Spending accounts are available for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting expenses. Per Scholas also offers a range of voluntary benefits, including: Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Legal Services, and Pet Insurance. Additional resources include healthcare concierge support, financial wellness tools, and employee discount programs.

jobs.title: Senior UX Designer
jobs.description:
We are seeking an AI-native Senior UX Designer to help shape the future of enterprise software in an AI-first world. This role is for designers who are driven to deeply understand users and translate complex supply chain challenges into intuitive, elegant experiences. You will join a team redefining how products are conceived, designed, and built — leveraging AI to accelerate insight, decision-making, and execution. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise UX, AI-enabled workflows, systems thinking, and business outcomes. You will help define how intelligent capabilities are surfaced inside complex operational workflows while also evolving how UX itself is practiced in an AI-centered product development lifecycle. You will work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Architecture, Data/AI teams, and executive stakeholders to design scalable, trustworthy, and high-impact experiences for some of the world's most complex supply chain environments.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

• Partner with Product Management and Architecture to define experience strategy across key platform areas — shaping not just what we build, but how intelligent, AI-driven capabilities are surfaced and experienced.

• Lead problem framing and user insight development for complex supply chain workflows, leveraging a mix of user research, data, and AI-assisted discovery techniques to uncover high-impact opportunities.

• Translate ambiguity into clear experience direction using appropriate fidelity — from rapid concepts to information architecture, wireframes, prototypes, interaction models, design specifications, and polished high-fidelity UI designs.

• Design AI-centered user experiences that leverage recommendation systems, intelligent automation, conversational interfaces, predictive intelligence, decision-support workflows, and agentic interaction models.

• Use AI-assisted workflows throughout the UX process — including research synthesis, ideation, prototyping, content generation, design exploration, usability analysis, and documentation acceleration.

• Drive continuous validation and learning, combining qualitative and quantitative methods to evaluate experience effectiveness and inform product decisions.

• Collaborate deeply with engineering teams to ensure high-quality implementation — iterating in real time, influencing trade-offs, and ensuring experiences meet a high bar for usefulness, usability, and polish.

• Act as a strong UX voice in cross-functional decision-making, advocating for user and business outcomes while helping teams navigate complexity and ambiguity.

• Shape and scale design systems and interaction patterns that support consistency while enabling innovation — particularly for AI-driven and data-rich experiences.

• Contribute to a culture of design excellence and innovation, raising the bar for craft, systems thinking, and the role of UX in an AI-centered product development lifecycle.

AI Fluency Competencies

• Demonstrates advanced AI-enabled design workflows that materially improve speed, quality, insight generation, and collaboration effectiveness

• Can define scalable UX patterns for AI-native enterprise experiences balancing intelligence, trust, explainability, and user control

• Operates with expert-level discernment. Establishes best practices and governance for responsible AI-assisted UX work

• Connects AI capabilities to measurable operational outcomes without over-designing or over-promising AI functionality

• Creates highly trusted AI experiences that improve decision-making while preserving transparency and accountability

Prerequisites

• 5+ years designing complex, data-rich enterprise applications, with a track record of simplifying challenging workflows into intuitive, high-impact experiences.

• Experience designing adaptive AI-infused experiences that combine intelligent guidance, automation, conversational workflows, and decision-support capabilities while preserving usability, explainability, user agency, and operational trust.

• Strong demonstrated curiosity, strategic thinking, and learning agility are valued where direct experience may be limited.

• Experience leading UX for meaningful product areas or initiatives, influencing direction across product, engineering, and design.

• Portfolio demonstrating end-to-end product thinking — from problem framing and user insight through to shipped outcomes.

• Strong systems thinking, with the ability to understand and design within complex technical domains (e.g., integrations, data platforms, supply chain systems).

• Ability to navigate ambiguity and define clear experience direction, translating loosely defined problems into actionable design strategies.

• Experience integrating user research and product data into decisions, combining qualitative and quantitative inputs to drive outcomes.

• Deep collaboration with engineering teams, influencing trade-offs and ensuring high-quality implementation in iterative environments.

• Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to articulate rationale and align cross- functional stakeholders.

• High bar for craft and detail, delivering polished, cohesive experiences that balance usefulness, usability, and visual quality.

A few things we offer

• Flexible PTO

• Culture of support, encouraging Life-Work balance

• 401k match

• FSA and HSA options

jobs.title: Senior HR Generalist
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Blue Energy is transforming how nuclear power gets built. Instead of constructing each plant on-site from scratch - a process that takes 10-15 years and is too expensive and unpredictable to finance - we build our plants like ships: in a factory, on an assembly line, then transport and assemble them at the site. This cuts costs by over 60% and brings plants online in just three years. We also pair natural gas with nuclear at our sites, so customers can start receiving power from gas turbines right away and then switch over to clean nuclear power once it comes online - getting energy to the grid faster while nuclear is being built. Our mission is to make nuclear energy abundant, affordable, and repeatable at global scale. We use proven, already-approved reactor designs and work with existing nuclear and industrial sites, giving us a faster path to regulatory approval. By manufacturing this way, we put nuclear power on the same cost-reduction curve that has made wind, solar, and batteries cheaper every year.




ROLE SUMMARY

Blue Energy is building its people function to support the company as it scales from 80-250+ employees to launch multi-site, multi-decade growth. Pay and benefits, the employee handbook and policies, the HR system of record and people data, the employee relations framework and talent management are all in the process of being designed and launched.

The Senior HR Generalist will support the build of that foundation and its administration. Reporting to the Head of HR and based in our Houston office, this role will collaborate on finalizing the design of the HR fundamentals then own/oversee the ongoing execution/day to day operations of core HR — including systems and reporting, benefits administration, the employee handbook and supporting procedures, employee relations and case management, compensation administration, & performance enablement.

This is a hands-on role with genuine ownership. It is currently scoped as a Senior HR Generalist who will focus on building HR Operations to scale. This role executes day-to-day HR and the results that need to be delivered. It oversees what has to happen in what order, keeps the work moving, and delivers on time and to a high bar in a regulated environment. It requires a balance of accountability and collaboration – knowing when to decide and when to escalate / seek guidance. To succeed in this role, we are looking for HR professionals who can build solutions while building relationships. We are committed to delivering on our mission of energy abundance by building trust with our employees and in the communities in which we operate. When there is a gap – this position will play a critical role in stepping up to provide solutions that align with our culture and our values. As the function matures and the business grows, there will be an opportunity to evolve into a more strategic Business Partner / HR Manager role.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - HR systems and people data. Own the HR system of record. Maintain data integrity and reporting. Contribute to requirements and selection for the next-generation HRIS. Define and own the single source of truth for people data, and collaborate with the head of HR to build the monthly people reporting pack for leadership.

 - Benefits administration. Run annual enrollment end to end. Administer eligibility, life events, leave and day-to-day benefits service. Hold the broker and carrier relationships to an agreed service standard. As Blue Energy moves to administering benefits directly, partner with the business to build out the employer stack — payroll and tax registrations, 401(k), COBRA, FSA/HSA, workers' compensation and ERISA filings.

 - Handbook, policy and compliance. Oversee the handbook sections through final approval and annual audit cycles. Maintain the supporting procedures that sit beneath each section, and build the annual training plans. Maintain the multi-state compliance requirements: postings, pay transparency, mandatory training and statutory filings, across the 14+ states in which Blue Energy employs.

 - Employee relations. Be the first point of contact for managers and employees on concerns, performance and conduct. Run intake and fact-finding, document to an audit-ready standard, and administer the conduct, discipline and termination procedures exactly as written — including the escalation points to HR leadership and counsel. Own the case management system, the case taxonomy and the register of concerns, and coach managers through the cases they own.

 - Compensation administration. Administer the compensation structure, bands and leveling records. Run the merit and review calendar. Prepare offer, promotion and change documentation accurately and on time, keeping the comp and leveling data up to date, reportable, and audit-ready.

 - People operations and service delivery. Oversee onboarding and offboarding of US hires. Ensure that employees are welcomed, have the resources they need to succeed, and that barriers or concerns are raised and removed. Make the people function the go-to team by providing solutions that make it easier, more efficient, and more effective for our business to operate.




WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE

This role is a Senior Level Individual Contributor who plans and executes a sequence of dependent tasks; is answerable for a workstream's outcome; and make decisions inside the function / escalates across as needed. In practice:

 - You take a workstream from definition to delivery without needing the sequence drawn for you.

 - You set the quality bar for the work, not only the deadline — documentation, records and procedure hold up internally and externally/to audit.

 - You raise problems early, with the analysis attached and a proposed solution.

 - You are candid, and you are discreet. You protect confidential decisions and data without exception.

 - You coach managers to solutions rather than taking the problem on for them.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years of progressive HR generalist experience, including time accountability for day-to-day HR operations.

 - Investigations Training.

 - Demonstrated employee relations experience: intake, fact-finding, documentation, performance and conduct process, terminations, and working alongside employment counsel.

 - Experience in a regulated or safety-critical industry — nuclear, power generation, oil and gas, chemicals, aerospace, med device/pharma, industrial or large-scale construction — where the compliance a must.

 - Working command of multi-state US employment compliance: FLSA, FMLA, ADA, Title VII, state wage, leave and pay-transparency variation.

 - Hands-on ownership of an HRIS and benefits administration — configuration, data integrity and reporting.

 - Ability to write clear policies and procedures, and to train people on what you wrote.

 - Based in Houston, working Tues/Weds/Thurs from our Houston office.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - PHR Certification.

 - Experience moving a company from a PEO onto a direct employer stack.

 - Experience administering a case management or employee relations system.

 - Experience in a company scaling past 150 people/Building solutions that grow with the business.

 - Exposure to multi-entity or international employment, including the UK.

 - Experience supporting a field, site or shift-based workforce as well as a corporate population.



We look forward to your application and helping foster an era of safe, clean, affordable, and abundant energy.

Blue Energy is dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the right candidate for this or other roles at Blue Energy now or in the future.

jobs.title: Finance Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)

Who we are looking for

Manufacturing Experience is Not Necessary

We're seeking a Finance Operations Manager who is energized by the intersection of finance and operations—someone who sees financial management as a tool for driving business performance, not just recording it. You will partner closely with our operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to support decision-making through insightful analysis, reliable reporting, and forward-looking planning. Leading our accounting operations and directly supervising our Staff Accountant, you'll ensure we have the financial infrastructure and rigor to support Oribi's growth while maintaining the agility of a nimble, innovative manufacturer. The ideal candidate brings 3-5 years of hands-on finance experience, a strong operational approach, and the desire to build both technical expertise and leadership capabilities in a dynamic, purposeful environment.

What you get to do

• Lead the monthly financial close process and deliver accurate, timely reporting that keeps leadership informed and empowered to act quickly

• Partner directly with the General Manager and operations leadership to translate financial performance into actionable business insights

• Develop annual budgets and quarterly forecasts that align with strategic goals and support data-driven decision-making

• Build and track operational benchmarks and input metrics that drive continuous improvement and long-term value creation

• Mentor and develop the Staff Accountant, providing coaching, feedback, and opportunities for professional growth

• Transform financial data into clear, compelling narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences across the organization

• Collaborate with operations, engineering, supply chain, and quality teams to support new product launches, customer programs, and business development opportunities

• Continuously improve accounting processes and internal controls, finding opportunities for automation, standardization, and efficiency gains

• Serve as the financial liaison between Oribi and Re:Build Manufacturing corporate finance, ensuring seamless reporting and policy alignment

• Support business development efforts with cost modeling, pricing analysis, and financial feasibility assessments for advanced composite component opportunities

• Champion a culture of transparency, continuous improvement, and financial literacy across the organization

What you bring to the team – A Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Finance, Accounting, or Business Administration. You have 3-5 years of progressive experience in financial operations or management accounting. Your background includes exposure to manufacturing cost accounting, operational metrics, and cross-functional collaboration.   You're equally comfortable building a forecast, closing the books, and walking the production floor to understand how the business really works.

Additional information – This role is office-based but requires a "go to the gemba" mindset. We expect you to regularly walk the production floor, observe our manufacturing processes, and build relationships with operators, engineers, and supervisors. The best financial insights come from understanding how continuous fiber-reinforced thermoplastic components are actually made—not just reviewing spreadsheets. Your willingness to get out of the office and into the operation will make you a more effective business partner.

The base salary range for this position is $80,000 – $110,000 per year. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.

Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate

We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.

Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. jobs.title: Instrumentation and Controls Technician
jobs.description:
The Instrumentation & Controls (I&C) Specialist is a high-level technical role that bridges the gap between field maintenance and system engineering. This individual is a subject matter expert responsible for the design, integration, and advanced troubleshooting of complex electrical and automated control systems within the plant. Unlike a standard technician, the Specialist leads capital projects, authors technical documentation, and develops PLC/SCADA logic while remaining "hands-on" for critical plant repairs and commissioning.

Key Characteristics

• Systems Thinking: Ability to design integrated control loops and understand the "big picture" of plant water treatment functions
• Advanced Problem-Solving: Capability to resolve chronic equipment issues through root-cause analysis and logic modifications
• Leadership without Management: Acts as a technical lead for contractors and junior technicians during plant outages and system upgrades
• High-Stakes Decision Quality: Makes critical decisions regarding system architecture and safety protocols to ensure 24/7 operational efficiency

Duties & Responsibilities

• System Design & Integration: Author and modify technical drawings, P&IDs, and electrical schematics for new plant installations or equipment repositioning
• Advanced Programming: Design, program, and configure PLCs, DCS, and HMI systems (primarily Allen-Bradley) to optimize plant processes
• Complex Electrical Work: Execute high-level electrical tasks including wiring, power distribution, and the layout of new metering and signaling devices
• Project Commissioning: Lead the commissioning of new mobile equipment and fixed plant facilities, ensuring all instrumentation meets business and regulatory specifications
• Lifecycle Documentation: Prepare comprehensive system design diagrams, maintenance reports, and "as-built" documentation for the facility
• Safety & Compliance Leadership: Set the standard for OSHA and environmental safety compliance, including the development of spill response and arc flash protocols)
• Emergency Technical Support: Provide expert-level response to plant emergency repairs that exceed the scope of standard technician capabilities

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Preferred:

• Expertise in Control Theory: Deep knowledge of analog/digital integrated circuits and modern electronics technology
• Industrial Networking: Proficiency in configuring communication protocols between field devices, PLCs, and SCADA systems
• Regulatory Mastery: Advanced knowledge of water industry regulations, OSHA standards, and National Electrical Code (NEC)
• Physical Dexterity: Ability to perform physical duties including lifting 50lbs, climbing, and working in various weather conditions at industrial sites

Compensation: $38.00-$40.50 per hour

Qualifications:

• Associate Degree or Diploma in Electronic Engineering/Technology or a related field
• Minimum of 8–10 years of experience in process control (exceeding the standard 5-year requirement)

Preferred:

• Proven Project Leadership experience and relevant professional certifications (e.g., ISA CCST or Journeyman Electrician License)
• Relevant certifications
• Experience in the water industry
• Proven project leadership experience in this domain
• Ability and willingness to work in various weather conditions (indoor / outdoor)
• Ability and willingness to perform physical duties such as lifting up to 50 pounds, climbing, working at elevated heights, and manual dexterity
• Ability and willingness to work in industrial facilities, manufacturing facilities, and power industry facilities
• Ability and willingness to travel (10%) for install and repair if needed
• Ability and willingness to work holidays and weekends based on business demand

Why Veolia?

• Join a company that values Responsibility, Solidarity, Innovation, Customer Focus, and Respect.
• You'll receive comprehensive technical and commercial training, direct mentorship from experienced Account Managers, and a clear pathway to Account Manager promotion with direct account responsibilities.

Career Development Path:

• This position is designed as a stepping stone to Account Manager, where you'll assume direct customer responsibility and independent account management upon demonstrating commercial excellence.

Ready to transition your technical expertise into a rewarding customer-facing career while

making a difference in water treatment and sustainability? Apply today!

We realize diverse teams make smarter decisions, deliver better results, and build stronger communities. We’re an organization that champions diversity and inclusion at every rung of the ladder and are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

jobs.title: CRM Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Success Academy! Running a large, fast-growing, and high-performing network of public charter schools takes a village - families, children, teachers, staff and faculty, advocates, and supporters alike. We are growing fast in New York and expanding to Florida, and we would love to welcome you to our community! We work tirelessly every day to ensure children have access to a fun, rigorous, whole-child education regardless of zip code or economic status. When you join SA, you play a part in giving every student who walks through our doors a fair shot at reaching his or her potential.

About the Role

The CRM Business Analyst translates CRM, marketing, and business needs into effective Salesforce and Hubspot solutions that improve customer engagement, campaign execution, lead and opportunity management, data quality, and reporting while partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to define requirements, optimize capabilities, and support continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

• CRM Platform Roadmap: Translate organizational objectives into a prioritized roadmap that improves efficiency, visibility, and adoption, ensuring to communicate risks to project deliverables and timelines.

• Business Analysis & Requirements Management: Gather, analyze, document, and align business requirements with stakeholders and technical partners through clear user stories, process flows, acceptance criteria, and solution documentation.

• CRM & Marketing Process Optimization: Optimize acquisition, campaign, segmentation, nurturing, conversion, and engagement processes to reduce manual work, improve data quality, and strengthen platform adoption.

• CRM Platform & Solution Delivery: Coordinate platform solution delivery by defining requirements, validating, enhancements, managing dependencies, and supporting planning, testing, releases, and post-release validation.

• Data, Reporting & Analytics: Define and improve CRM and marketing data, reporting, dashboard, KPI, segmentation, and governance requirements to support accurate insights and informed decision-making.

• Testing, Training & Continuous Improvement: Coordinate testing, training, communications, documentation, adoption, post-release monitoring, and continuous improvement to ensure effective platform use and governance.

Qualifications

• 3-5 years of experience as a Salesforce/Hubspot/Equivalent Platform Business Analyst, CRM Analyst, Marketing Analyst, Systems Analyst, or in a related role.

• Hands-on experience with data analysis, user acceptance training, process mapping, and requirements gathering.

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Marketing, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Competencies

• Data Literacy & Governance: Understand data structures, business rules and processes, data quality, integrations, and governance requirements to support reliable and responsible use of CRM data.

• Business Requirements & Analytical Thinking: Break down complex business challenges into clear requirements, evaluates underlying needs, and develops structured, automated, actionable solutions.

• Process Optimization: Evaluate current workflows, identifies inefficiencies, and recommends scalable improvements that reduce manual effort and improve business outcomes.

• Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership: Build trusted relationships, translate technical jargon into business language, and incorporate feedback constructively.

• Adaptability & Agility: Learn continuously, adapt to changing priorities and information, incorporate feedback, and respond thoughtfully to evolving business needs.

Compensation, Benefits, & Perks

• Financial Security: 403(b) retirement plan with a 3% employer match, up to $2,400/year in employer HSA contributions, employer-paid life/disability insurance, and Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligibility.

• Time to Recharge: Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave.

• Perks & Stipends: A $50/month cellphone stipend ($600/year), pre-tax commuter benefits, backup family care, and performance-based earning incentives.

This is a hybrid position based in our NYC Financial District office, requiring on-site work Tuesday through Thursday and remote work on Monday and Friday.

Exact compensation may vary based on skills and experience. This position is not bonus eligible.

$115,000—$125,000 USD

jobs.title: Case Manager, Rare Disease Patient Services
jobs.description:
Kyowa Kirin is a fast-growing global specialty pharmaceutical company that applies state-of-the-art biotechnologies to discover and deliver novel medicines in four disease areas: bone and mineral; intractable hematologic; hematology oncology; and rare disease.  A Japan-based company, our goal is to make people smile by delivering breakthroughs where no adequate treatments currently exist, working from drug discovery to product development and commercialization. In North America, we are headquartered in Princeton, NJ, with offices in California, Massachusetts, and Ontario.

Summary of Job

The Case Manager is responsible for working with patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers (HCPs) to guide patients through the access and initiation process for Kyowa Kirin's rare disease products while providing ongoing support throughout their treatment journey. The Case Manager collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to help meet each patient's individual needs.

Essential Functions

• Manage a caseload efficiently while consistently meeting established key performance indicators (KPIs)

• Review new and restart patient enrollments for completeness and oversee the entire enrollment process from receipt through product shipment including benefits investigations, prior authorization, specialty pharmacy, nurse training coordination and shipment scheduling

• Serve as the primary point of contact for patients, providing consistent support from enrollment through treatment initiation and throughout their treatment journey

• Build and maintain strong relationships with patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers by delivering timely, personalized communication based on individual needs and preferences

• Educate patients and caregivers on insurance benefits, financial assistance programs, patient support services, and available resources.

• Coordinate treatment access, initiation, and ongoing therapy by collaborating with healthcare providers, payers, specialty pharmacies, and internal cross-functional teams.

• Monitor each patient's treatment progress, proactively identify barriers to therapy, and implement timely solutions to prevent delays or interruptions in care.

• Establish and maintain compliant relationships with internal stakeholders, including Sales and Market Access teams, as well as external partners such as specialty pharmacies and HCP staff to ensure seamless patient experience.

• Identify and communicate trends related to reimbursement challenges, access delays, patient concerns, and operational issues, providing recommendations for process improvements.

• Maintain accurate and timely documentation while ensuring compliance with program guidelines, HIPAA regulations, and all applicable privacy and regulatory requirements.

• Participate in team meetings, contribute to continuous process improvement initiatives, and collaborate on solutions to enhance operational efficiency and patient outcomes

Education

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.

Experience

• 5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry

• 2–5 years of experience in case management, patient access, patient support, healthcare, specialty pharmacy, reimbursement, or a related healthcare setting

• Experience managing a high-volume caseload while meeting productivity goals and service-level expectations.

• Ability to prioritize multiple cases, manage competing deadlines, and work independently in a fast-paced environment.

• Knowledge of insurance verification, benefits investigations, prior authorizations, appeals, and reimbursement processes.

• Previous experience with Specialty and Medical Benefits process and billing

• Rare disease experience a plus

• Experience collaborating with patients, healthcare providers, specialty pharmacies, payers, and multidisciplinary teams.

• Excellent communication, customer service, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Experience working with specialty medications, rare disease, oncology, immunology, neurology, or other specialty therapeutic areas is preferred

Technical Skills

• Proficient in MS Office Suite.

Non-Technical Skills

• Demonstrated ability to organize, prioritize, meet deadlines, make sound decisions, and adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong interpersonal, communication, and relationship-building skills.

• Strong work ethic with exceptional attention to detail and follow-through.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing business needs in a dynamic, high-growth environment.

• Commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and ongoing improvement.

Travel

Requires up to 10% domestic and international travel

Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated salary for this position is $95,000 to $118,000. The actual salary offered at the commencement of employment may vary based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skill set, qualifications, education (including applicable licenses and certifications), job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs.
