jobs.title: Head of Business Development and Partnerships
jobs.description:
About Pulley

Pulley helps the country’s top architects, builders, and retailers speed up every project in their portfolio. With AI-powered permitting intelligence and expert guidance, we eliminate costly delays and bring predictability across the full lifecycle of commercial projects. 

Today, permitting is the slowest, most uncertain part of building, spread across 19,000+ jurisdictions with different rules, timelines, and surprises. Pulley gives project teams the clarity and predictability they need to move from planning to opening without delays.

We support rollout programs for brands like J.Crew, Solidcore, and Hibbett Sports, as well as major data center buildouts, EV charging networks, and other commercial projects. Our platform dramatically reduces approval timelines, improves forecasting accuracy, and removes thousands of hours of manual work from design and construction teams.

Founded in 2021, Pulley combines deep permitting expertise with purpose-built AI from people who have created products used by millions. We’re backed by CRV, Susa Ventures, Fifth Wall, and leaders from Plaid, Segment, ServiceTitan, and Procore.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

As Pulley’s Head of Business Development and Partnerships, you’ll work directly with our co-founder Andreas to grow partnerships into a meaningful, repeatable source of revenue. You’ll build on existing relationships and early successes, bring structure to what’s working, and identify new opportunities across our markets.

In this role, you will:

 - Set priorities across existing and new partnership opportunities, focusing on those with the greatest business potential.

 - Develop and deepen relationships with partners and industry leaders who can expand Pulley’s reach.

 - Source, pitch, negotiate, and launch partnerships, owning the work from the first conversation through execution.

 - Build programs that give partners compelling reasons to work with Pulley and stay engaged over time.

 - Work closely with Sales to turn partner relationships and introductions into qualified opportunities and revenue.

 - Collaborate with Marketing and our founders on initiatives that strengthen relationships, build awareness, and generate pipeline.

 - Establish the processes and playbooks to make successful partnerships repeatable and scalable.

 - Measure results and bring market feedback into our positioning and go-to-market strategy.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You’re an entrepreneurial builder who can turn early traction into a program that scales.

 - You’re a systems thinker who brings structure to multiple opportunities without losing momentum.

 - You can spot the people and organizations that open doors, earn their trust, and turn relationships into business.

 - You move easily between strategy and hands-on execution.

 - You’re comfortable with ambiguity and bring your own ideas about where to focus and what to try.

 - You collaborate naturally across Sales, Marketing, and leadership, and follow through on what you start.


NEED TO HAVE

 - Experience building or growing partnerships, business development, or go-to-market initiatives with measurable results.

 - A track record of developing external relationships that create sustained business opportunities.

 - Evidence that you’ve taken an initiative from idea through execution and built processes that support its growth.

 - Strong commercial judgment: you can evaluate opportunities, prioritize your time, and negotiate agreements.

 - Excellent relationship-building, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building or scaling a partner or channel program.

 - Familiarity with construction, commercial real estate, or selling technology and services into those industries.

 - Experience navigating large enterprise organizations and engaging senior decision-makers.

 - Experience working with Marketing on initiatives that generate pipeline.

jobs.title: Account Executive (m/w/d) im Außendienst (new markets) - Braunschweig
jobs.description:
Salonkee kommt nach Braunschweig und sucht die erste Person im Vertrieb. Du fühlst dich im Sales zu Hause und hast Lust, ein eigenes Gebiet im Außendienst aufzubauen? Bei uns heißt das: Verantwortung übernehmen, kurze Sales-Zyklen betreuen, ungedeckelte Provision verdienen und echte Entwicklungschancen nutzen.

Salonkee ist Marktführer für Salon-Software in Luxemburg, Belgien und der Schweiz. Über 10.000 Beauty- und Wellness-Betriebe in sieben Ländern nutzen unsere All-in-one-Software – von der Terminbuchung über die Kundenverwaltung und die Kasse bis hin zu Marketing- und KI-Funktionen.

Für einen Salon bedeutet das im Schnitt 70 % weniger Terminausfälle und 8 bis 12 Stunden weniger Verwaltungsaufwand pro Woche.




DEINE ROLLE

 - Du verantwortest das Wachstum in deiner Region und bist die zentrale Ansprechperson vor Ort

 - Du gehst aktiv auf Saloninhaber:innen in deiner Region zu – telefonisch, per Walk-in oder über Social Media (Kaltakquise).

 - Vor Ort ermittelst du den Bedarf des Salons mithilfe von Fragen und zeigst anhand von Produktdemos, wie Salonkee den Alltag vereinfachen kann.

 - Du verantwortest deinen eigenen Funnel vom Erstkontakt bis zum Abschluss.

 - Deine Woche planst du eigenverantwortlich, mit klaren Zielen und einer Führungskraft, die dich unterstützt und weiterentwickelt.

 - Du gibst dein Wissen weiter – im Roleplay, im Shadowing und im Austausch mit Kolleg:innen, die neu dabei sind.
   
   


DAS BRINGST DU MIT

 - Nachweisbare Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb mit eigener Abschlussverantwortung über den gesamten Sales-Cycle hinweg, von der Kaltakquise bis zum Closing.

 - Hohe Selbststeuerung und Eigenverantwortung – du gehörst zu den ersten Teammitgliedern vor Ort.

 - Du bist es gewohnt, an KPIs gemessen zu werden und hast deine eigenen Zahlen stets im Blick.

 - Du schaffst es, ein komplexes Produkt verständlich zu vermitteln und dabei zu begeistern.

 - Du bist lernbereit, setzt Feedback um und willst dich weiterentwickeln.

 - Du bist sicher im Umgang mit digitalen Tools.

 - Verhandlungssicheres bis muttersprachliches Deutsch sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

 - Führerschein der Klasse B und Freude daran, in deiner Region unterwegs zu sein.
   
   


DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

 - Klare Entwicklungschancen: Nächste Senioritätsstufen erreichst du mit deiner Performance - simpel gehalten und schnell erreichbar. Außerdem besetzen wir Team-Lead-Rollen bevorzugt aus dem eigenen Team und begleiten den Weg dorthin mit unserer Sales Manager Academy.

 - Eine Führungskraft und Kolleg:innen, die dich jederzeit unterstützen.

 - Strukturierte Einarbeitung und praxisnahe Begleitung über die ersten Monate hinweg (Ramp-Up Programm).

 - Klare KPIs & Performance-Transparenz, damit du jederzeit weißt, wo du stehst.

 - Eigenverantwortliche Wochenplanung und Vertrauensarbeitszeit.

 - Firmenwagen inkl. Tankkarte sowie MacBook und iPhone.

 - 50 € steuerfreies Guthaben pro Monat über Probonio.

 - Fixgehalt und ungedeckelte Provision.

 - Teamevents, die ihren Namen verdienen: Sommerfest, Winterfeier und regelmäßige Teamformate.




WIE GEHT ES WEITER?

 1. Bewerbung & Sichtung – wir melden uns so schnell wie möglich bei dir.

 2. Erstgespräch mit unserem Recruiting-Team (ca. 30–45 Minuten).

 3. Video-Call mit deiner künftigen Führungskraft.

 4. Field Day – zwei Stunden bei uns im Office. Du siehst, wie wir arbeiten, wir sehen dich in Aktion.

 5. Abschlussgespräch mit unserer Head of Sales.



Salonkee steht für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Fähigkeiten – unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Alter, Behinderung, Religion oder Identität.

jobs.title: Production & Supply Development Program Associate
jobs.description:

Through three business-critical rotations over approximately two and a half years, associates develop technical, analytical, and business capabilities while contributing to meaningful work that supports Syngenta's operations. Rotations are shaped by business needs, development goals, and the requirements of the selected track.

PSDP Associates are not observers. Each rotation provides defined responsibilities, a team that depends on your contribution, and opportunities to solve real business challenges while working alongside experienced professionals across the organization.

In addition to rotational experiences, associates receive development support through coaching, mentoring, feedback, and networking opportunities. Through exposure to varied business functions, locations, subject matter experts, and senior leaders, associates build confidence influencing without authority, strengthen their leadership capability, and gain insight into a variety of career paths across the organization.

jobs.title: Staff Backend Engineer | Remote, US & Canada
jobs.description:
Cube is the financial intelligence platform built for the AI-era.

The world has evolved, but FP&A is still trapped in manual reconciliation cycles. While most platforms try to replace the spreadsheets finance teams love, Cube is different: we are the intelligent finance layer that unifies fragmented data into a centralized command center. By automating data management, we empower the Office of the CFO to stop moving numbers and start driving the strategic analysis that turns data into growth.

We don’t compete with AI; we make it trustworthy. In a world where AI is often only 80% right, Cube provides the 100% truth and governance finance teams need to turn data into growth. Our mission is clean data, everywhere, allowing the modern Office of the CFO to move beyond manual data management and lead with strategic certainty.

Cube has raised >$65M and is backed by top-tier investors such as Battery Ventures and Mayfield. We’re also proud to be recognized by Forbes as one of the Best Places to Work in 2026. Together, we’re building a culture that challenges and celebrates everyone with a path to growth. We’re guided by our company values: act with urgency, keep it simple, build with joy, obsess over the details, own the outcome, raise the bar, champion our customers, and win together. As we enter our next phase of growth, we believe having the right Cubers on our team will be the reason we win.



Note: This position requires working onsite at our New York office Tuesday through Thursday.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Staff Back-End Engineer to serve as a technical North Star for our engineering organization. In this role, you won’t just ship features; you will shape the architectural patterns, infrastructure standards, and engineering habits that allow our entire team to scale.

Reporting to an Engineering Manager, you will act as a highly strategic individual contributor working across multiple problem spaces. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Customer Success to transform ambiguous business needs into robust distributed systems that power real financial workflows.

This role exists at a pivotal moment in Cube’s growth. As our platform expands in complexity and scale, we’re looking for someone who can elevate system design, improve long-term reliability, and help define what great engineering looks like across the organization.

You will take ownership of complex initiatives end-to-end, influencing infrastructure, deployment strategies, observability practices, and long-term system health. This is an opportunity to help build scalable engineering foundations, reusable abstractions, and internal frameworks that accelerate the entire team.




TECH STACK

 - Python (Django + DRF)

 - MySQL, ClickHouse, Redis, RabbitMQ, Celery

 - AWS (deployed via CDK), CI/CD automation

 - JavaScript/TypeScript (React/Redux) on the front end

 - AI-driven workflows, LLM agents, enterprise integrations, and advanced observability


WHO YOU ARE

 - Experienced Technical Leader: Typically brings 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with flexibility for exceptional candidates who demonstrate strong Staff-level impact, ownership, and technical leadership.

 - A Technical Strategist: You have clear, experience-backed opinions on distributed systems and long-term architecture. You don’t just solve today’s problem; you design systems that support years of growth.

 - Python/Django Expert: Deep knowledge of Django internals including middleware, database routing, management commands, signals, and performance optimization in high-scale, multi-tenant environments.

 - Systems Architect: Strong experience building and evolving distributed systems across cloud infrastructure. Comfortable debugging complex concurrency challenges such as race conditions, distributed deadlocks, async failures, and large-scale database performance issues.

 - Data Fluent: Experience with dataframe-based computation tools such as Pandas, Polars, or NumPy to power data-intensive workflows and financial modeling pipelines.

 - Engineering Leader: Proven ability to define engineering standards, design reusable abstractions, and improve developer velocity through internal tooling and frameworks.

 - Efficiency Minded: Early adopter of AI-assisted engineering workflows (Cursor, Claude Code, automated refactoring, or similar tooling) to increase velocity without sacrificing reliability or code quality.

 - Effective Communicator: Able to clearly explain architectural trade-offs to executives, product partners, and engineers at all levels.

 - Nice to Have: Familiarity with FP&A domain concepts such as trial balances, charts of accounts, fiscal calendars, scenario modeling, and multi-currency workflows.


HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT


TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP

 - Define the Standard: Set architectural direction and establish engineering patterns that become the golden path across teams.

 - Own the Core: Design and evolve complex backend systems including multi-tenant database routing, distributed task orchestration, async pipelines, and enterprise integrations.

 - Modernize Workflows: Lead adoption of AI-assisted development practices and LLM agent systems within production environments.


EXECUTION & EXCELLENCE

 - Ship Strategic Initiatives: Take ambiguous product goals and deliver them end-to-end, from infrastructure (CDK) and deployment to monitoring and documentation.

 - Observability First: Foster a culture of observability by default, owning strategies around structured logging, APM tooling, metrics, and production debugging workflows.

 - High-Stakes Resolution: Act as a steady technical leader during production incidents, guiding root-cause analysis and long-term remediation strategies.


MENTORSHIP & CULTURE

 - Elevate the Team: Remove technical blockers, mentor engineers, and promote psychological safety alongside a culture of continuous improvement.

 - Scale the Org: Continuously improve CI/CD pipelines, testing infrastructure, release processes, and deployment strategies so teams can ship safely at speed.



The expectations above are meant to represent the ideal candidate, but if you don’t meet all of them and think you’d be a great fit for this role, please apply. This position is open to candidates who are authorized to work in the posted location. Immigration sponsorship is not available at this time.



Full-Time Employee Benefits

 - We provide 100% covered employee medical, dental, and vision insurance options, including FSA/HSA options plus free memberships to OneMedical, Teladoc, and Talkspace.

 - Our flexible paid vacation and sick/mental health time guidelines help you get the time and space you need.

 - We offer stock options to all full-time employees of Cube, as we want you to be connected to the success of the company.

 - We offer 12 weeks of 100% paid parental leave for the birthing parent.

 - We offer each Cuber a quarterly learning budget to spend on books, classes, or events that support your development.

 - You’ll be joining an experienced team of tech startup leaders who are eager to work with you and provide support and mentorship!

 - You’ll work for a company that our customers are truly excited about https://www.cubesoftware.com/customers!

jobs.title: Dry Van Logistics Coordinator
jobs.description:
Overall Purpose and Objective of Position

This position is responsible for scheduling freight and servicing customers of liquid food and feed ingredients in North America, with a focus on product manufactured in Upper Sandusky, OH.  This role will concentrate on dry vans to achieve the most efficient, cost effective, reliable and quality transportation while ensuring shipment timing meets the needed cadence for optimal inventory levels. This position would be responsible to develop key relationships with various carriers in order to maintain and/or improve our competitive position within our industries. This position would also have responsibility to help with negotiating and managing freight contracts with freight providers. This position would also perform various reporting tasks, communicating documents with customers, and any other customer service needs.

Primary Responsibilities/Essential Functions

• Generate load numbers for customer orders in a timely and accurate manner
• Schedule orders with carriers and maintain schedule changes
• Prepare and organize paperwork needed for shipments
• Ticket application for multiple products, freight matching, and filing
• Communicate professionally with customers to coordinate deliveries in a timely manner
• Contribute to inventory management of LDC products (warehouse/tanks/rail cars/containers etc.)
• Coordinate quality requirements and issues from customers with LDC lab and operations team
• Assist with setting up carriers and maintaining documents and certificates
• Utilize multiple systems to maintain carrier and freight information to assist with the coordinating of logistics for multiple products for inbound and outbound shipments
• Develop and maintain relationships with carriers, forwarders and warehousing providers as needed
• Communicate with Quality and Food Safety team to ensure compliance with statutory and internal practices
• Work with sales staff to ensure they have competitive transportation rates to accurately quote business for customers and manage existing business lanes
• Communicate with sales team any info that is helpful to determine pricing, freight risk awareness, and customer performance concerns
• Develop competence in LDC products’ markets, product qualities, and transportation needs
• Contribute to group discussions to improve processes and look for ways to elevate our business.

Education/Professional Certifications/Licenses

Basic qualifications:

• Associate Degree in supply chain, industrial management, business, finance, or economics
• Or, 2 years’ experience in oilseeds, or logistics or supply chain management

Preferred qualifications:

• Shipping liquid food grade products, or freight forwarding experience

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Transportation, Logistics, Supply Chain Management, or related field

Own and evolve the clinical process engineering capability within Clinical Development Operations, establishing the methodology, standards, and governance infrastructure that enable scalable, inspection-ready, and operationally excellent processes across the enterprise. The Associate Director, Clinical Process Engineer is the functional authority on process design and engineering practice, operating at the intersection of strategy, compliance, and execution. This role shapes how the discipline works, not just what it delivers, and is accountable for building the infrastructure and talent that sustains the capability long-term. Operates within a multilayered leadership structure and is expected to bring enterprise-level judgment and strong upward credibility.

Major responsibilities

• Define and own the clinical process engineering methodology, standards, and toolset used across Clinical Development Operations; drive adoption and continuous evolution of the practice.
• Serve as the enterprise subject matter authority on clinical process design, advising senior and executive leadership on process strategy, capability investments, and cross-functional process architecture.
• Oversee the design and governance of end-to-end clinical processes across the enterprise; ensure coherence, scalability, and inspection readiness across domains and programs.
• Lead enterprise-level current-state assessments and strategic process analyses; translate findings into capability recommendations and program-level improvement roadmaps for executive audiences.
• Design and lead high-stakes, enterprise-wide process workshops and governance forums; manage executive-level stakeholder dynamics, resolve competing priorities, and drive strategic alignment.
• Establish and own the process compliance, inspection readiness, and quality-by-design frameworks for the function; proactively manage risk and partner with quality and regulatory leadership on emerging expectations.
• Lead and govern complex, cross-enterprise process-to-system programs; accountable for the quality and integrity of process design inputs feeding technology platforms and transformation initiatives.
• Own the process performance measurement framework for the function; define enterprise KPIs, oversee reporting infrastructure, and present insights to senior leadership and governance bodies.
• Set and govern documentation standards, decision record practices, and process governance infrastructure across Clinical Development Operations; responsible for audit readiness at a function-wide level.
• May manage 0–5 direct reports; responsible for team leadership, talent strategy, performance management, and building a differentiated, high-impact process engineering capability.

• Bachelor's degree in engineering, life sciences, business, or a related field required; advanced degree strongly preferred.

• Deep expertise in clinical development operations and regulatory, inspection, and quality frameworks, including the ability to advise senior leadership on emerging compliance expectations.
• Expert proficiency in process mapping, methodology development, and governance design; demonstrated experience building and scaling process engineering capabilities within a large, regulated organization.
• Proven ability to lead enterprise-level, multi-stakeholder programs and governance forums with executive presence and strong facilitation skills.

jobs.title: Provider Sales Director
jobs.description:
What you’ll be part of

Garner is on a mission to transform the U.S. healthcare system — and we’re the only proven player doing exactly that. We partner with employers to redesign how healthcare works: applying 550+ proprietary clinical metrics across 80+ specialties to a dataset of 320M+ patients to identify the best-performing doctors, then using compelling incentives to steer members to the care that helps them get healthier, faster.

The result is a rare “win win” — better care and lower costs for both members and employers. In just five years, our work has helped over 2.5 million people access higher-quality care and saved $1B in healthcare costs. We recently raised our Series E and have doubled five years running. If you've ever wanted your work to solve a problem that touches every person in this country, this is the opportunity to do exactly that. You'd be joining a team fundamentally reimagining healthcare in the U.S. — and using AI to scale that impact further and faster than anyone else can.

Who we want

This is a role for someone who wants to work on a hard problem, deliver real impact and be pushed to be the best version of themselves. As a Provider Sales Director, you’ll be embedded in Provider Partnerships and report directly to the SVP of Provider.

You will own a critical component of Garner's provider segment as a quota-carrying seller, selling our solutions into hospitals, health systems, ACOs and clinically integrated networks, physician groups, and digital health companies. You will run the full cycle from prospecting through close, using Garner's own data as the centerpiece of the pitch rather than a supporting slide. This is a builder's seat: the segment playbook is still being written, and the person in this role will help write it.

Where you will work:

Garner is headquartered in NYC, but this position is available for individuals who are comfortable with remote work and occasional travel to HQ.

What you will do

• Own and advance a provider-segment pipeline end to end, from segmentation and prospecting through close, carrying an individual quota against your assigned budget.

• Build and deepen senior relationships across hospitals and health systems, ACOs and clinically integrated networks, physician groups, digital health companies, and healthcare consultants.

• Run a data-driven sales motion: use Garner's own data and insights to shape strategy conversations with sophisticated buyers.

• Partner with Product, Sales leadership, and Account Management, feeding market signal back into the roadmap and handing off closed accounts cleanly.

jobs.title: Field Service Technician (Water Technologies)
jobs.description:
Veolia LabWater Solutions is seeking a highly motivated, customer-focused Field Service Technician to join our North American Field Service team. This position is responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and calibrating laboratory water purification systems at customer facilities throughout an assigned territory.

The ideal candidate possesses strong mechanical and electrical aptitude, excellent troubleshooting skills, and a passion for delivering exceptional customer service. This individual will work independently while collaborating closely with Technical Support, Sales, Customer Service, and internal operations to ensure customers receive timely, professional, and high-quality service.

Key Responsibilities

• Install, commission, configure, and validate laboratory water purification systems in accordance with company procedures and manufacturer specifications.
• Perform preventative maintenance, system inspections, calibrations, software updates, and operational verification to ensure optimal equipment performance.
• Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical and electrical equipment failures at customer sites.
• Replace defective components and perform corrective maintenance to restore equipment to factory operating specifications.
• Complete service reports, calibration documentation, expense reports, and all required administrative paperwork accurately and within established deadlines.
• Generate quotations for billable repairs, preventative maintenance agreements, validation services, consumables, and system upgrades.
• Proactively manage preventative maintenance agreement (PMA) opportunities within the assigned territory by identifying renewal opportunities and working closely with the Sales and Customer Service teams.
• Train customers on proper system operation, preventative maintenance practices, and routine maintenance procedures.
• Respond to emergency service requests in a timely and professional manner while maintaining excellent customer communication.
• Build and maintain strong customer relationships through professionalism, technical expertise, and outstanding service.
• Maintain company-issued tools, test equipment, inventory, and vehicle in a clean, organized, and service-ready condition.
• Ensure compliance with all company, customer, and regulatory safety policies while working in laboratory, pharmaceutical, healthcare, industrial, and research environments.
• Participate in a rotating 24/7 on-call support schedule.
• Collaborate with Technical Support and engineering to resolve complex technical issues and identify product improvement opportunities.
• Maintain a high level of technical knowledge by participating in ongoing product training and professional development.
• Assist other departments within the service organization.

Qualifications

Required

• Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Electronics, Biomedical Technology, Mechanical Technology, or another related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant field service experience.
• Minimum of two years of field service experience installing, maintaining, and repairing technical equipment.
• Strong mechanical, electrical, and electronic troubleshooting skills.
• Excellent diagnostic and problem-solving abilities.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with customers at all organizational levels.
• Outstanding organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize multiple service calls and administrative responsibilities.
• Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
• Willingness to travel extensively throughout the assigned territory, including overnight travel. May be required to travel outside of the assigned territory on occasion.

Preferred Qualifications

• Previous experience servicing laboratory water purification systems is highly preferred.
• Previous experience servicing biomedical, medical diagnostic, analytical laboratory, pharmaceutical, or life science instrumentation is highly desirable.
• Experience with reverse osmosis (RO), deionization (DI), ultraviolet (UV) disinfection systems, water purification technologies, water treatment equipment, or laboratory instrumentation is considered a strong advantage.
• Experience performing equipment validation, calibration, preventative maintenance, and equipment qualification.
• Knowledge of laboratory, pharmaceutical, healthcare, research, or biotechnology environments.
• Experience reading electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical service documentation.
• Proficiency with Google Workspace, and Salesforce

Core Competencies

• Customer-focused mindset
• Technical aptitude
• Critical thinking and analytical troubleshooting
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills
• Professionalism and integrity
• Self-motivated with the ability to work independently
• Excellent planning and organizational skills
• Adaptability in a fast-paced environment
• Commitment to quality and continuous improvement
• Strong attention to detail

Why Join Veolia LabWater Solutions?

At Veolia LabWater Solutions, our Field Service Technicians play a critical role in supporting scientific  research, healthcare, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and industrial laboratories by ensuring our customers receive reliable, high-quality laboratory water systems and exceptional service.

We offer:

jobs.title: Substance Use/Behavioral Health Counselor
jobs.description:
The Substance Use Counselor serves as a member of a multi-disciplinary substance use patient care team.  The Counselor provides direct patient and therapeutic counseling services with a focus on substance use and general mental health to individuals, families, and groups. Work performance is reviewed for conformance to policies, procedures, and practices related to substance use and behavioral health service delivery. The Substance Use Counselor will represent the company professionally and positively to enhance and promote the core values and the mission of NATIVE HEALTH, always exercising the utmost discretion, diplomacy, and tact in customer interactions. The SUD Counselor reports directly to the Recovery Service Coordinator for clinical oversight and supervision.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

• Assesses and provides appropriate therapeutic substance use counseling services for individuals, families, and/or groups presenting with problems related to general mental health and/or substance abuse, that are within the scope of the Counselor’s license, education, and skills.
• Provides Substance use and behavioral health related prevention/education services to the community in a cost effective and efficient manner.
• Provides accurate and timely documentation, billing, and program audit support.
• Actively participates in case staffing meetings and peer review sessions.
• Collaborate with the care team and other internal and external health care providers for shared patients to facilitate patient care and follow-up, while promoting the healthcare home mission in all aspects of service delivery.
• Supports the organization as needed

QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE/REQUIREMENTS:

• An Active and unrestricted AZBBHE licensure as a Licensed Master of Social Work (LMSW), Licensed Associate Counselor (LAC), Licensed Associate Marriage and Family Therapist (LAMFT), Licensed Associate Addiction Counselor (LAAC) is required.
• An Active and unrestricted AZBBHE licensure as a Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Professional Counselor (LPC), or Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or Licensed Independent Addiction Counselor (LIAC) preferred.
• Three years of specialized experience in substance abuse with diverse populations is strongly preferred. Experience working with underserved populations is also highly preferred.
• Bilingual in Spanish is preferred. Fluency evaluation is required.

Standard Employment Requirements

• Must possess a valid and unrestricted Arizona driver’s license (within 30 days of hire if applicant is from out-of-state) with no DUI/DWI or reckless driving convictions in the last five years. No more than two at-fault accidents in the last three years. Must maintain a valid Arizona driver’s license during employment. Must be insurable under NATIVE HEALTH’s liability auto policy.
• Must pass a criminal background check and obtain a Class I Fingerprint Clearance Card within the initial ninety (90) calendar days of employment and retain a valid card while employed with NATIVE HEALTH.
• Must pass substance abuse testing upon employment and submit to random testing during employment.
• Must provide an updated immunization (IZ) record at the time of employment.
• Must have a current (within 12 months) Tuberculosis (TB) skin report upon employment and provide an annual update.
• Must obtain BLS certification within (90) calendar days of employment and maintain certification during employment.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

The following factors are essential to this position, and to minimally qualify, applicants must provide evidence in their resumes that they possess these required factors:

• Knowledge of principles, techniques and trends in counseling, psychotherapy, clinical case management, and various treatment modalities.
• Knowledge of principles and techniques of mental health and substance use education, prevention, and crisis intervention.
• Ability to deliver strong clinical services to individuals, families, and/or groups.
• Model professionalism, integrity, and ethical principles at all times.
• Ability to accomplish the quality and quantity of work expected within set limits of cost and time.
• Ability to plan own work and carry out assignments effectively and completely.
• Must have strong listening, written, and oral communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with patients, providers, and staff.
• Ability to establish rapport and gain the confidence of others (providers, case managers, primary care team, patients and associates).
• Must be able to work with confidential material without betraying the trust of patients, families, or the agency- in accordance with HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 regulations, as well as agency policies.
• Ability to assess quality of patient care and make improvements, as needed.
• Knowledge and competence in supporting the cultural, social, and economic backgrounds of a diverse service population with traditionally underserved needs.
• Knowledge of mental health and substance use issues of the diverse populations served.
• Knowledge of existing social and behavioral health resources available for patient care.
• Knowledge of and skills to provide brief intervention counseling focused on adults and/or children with general mental health and/or substance abuse challenges.
• Remains current and timely completes all assigned Relias trainings and other training related to the health promotion and disease prevention of the persons served in the program.
• Proficient with computer-based applications such as MS Office, Adobe, and electronic health record.

Native Health complies with all state and federal requirements, including EEOC requirements.

This is a high-impact, strategic leadership role critical to driving Twilio's pricing strategy and operationalizing key pricing processes. jobs.title: IT Platforms Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT TIDE

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.

Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.

Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.

Tide facts:

• Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs

• Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing

• Over $300 million raised in funding

• 3,000 Tideans globally

• Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026

• We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg

ABOUT THE TEAM:

The IT team at Tide is a small, high-impact group of around 20 people, combining a responsive service desk with strong project-based engineering capability. The team operates in a cloud-native environment, with Google Workspace at the core, and supports a large, globally distributed workforce. The focus is on enabling the business through reliable, secure access to a wide range of SaaS platforms, while continuously improving how services are delivered as the organisation scales.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Workplace Technology Engineer, you’ll be a hands-on engineer looking after the platforms and devices Tideans use every day. You’ll work closely with the rest of the team to implement, operate, maintain and improve our core IT platforms by focusing on Configuration as a Code framework.

You will:

• Operate and improve our core IT platforms. You’ll handle day-to-day configuration, changes and troubleshooting, and deliver improvements within agreed standards and designs.

• Manage our device fleet end to end. That covers provisioning, compliance, patching and retirement of Mac and Windows devices, with a focus on a smooth experience for employees.

• Apply our security controls. You’ll roll out and maintain device trust, DLP and web security policies in partnership with InfoSec, and help troubleshoot when they affect users.

• Support onboarding and offboarding. You’ll make sure access is granted and removed accurately and on time, and help automate the manual steps.

• Automate repetitive work with scripts and the platforms’ built-in automation.

• Act as L2/L3 escalation for the service desk, resolving complex issues and turning recurring problems into documented fixes.

• Contribute to projects, owning workstreams within larger platform rollouts and upgrades.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:

• 4+ years in IT or workplace engineering, ideally in a cloud-first organisation.

• Hands-on administration experience with Google Workspace and with Jamf and/or Intune across Mac and Windows.

• Exposure to SSE or web security tools (Netskope or similar) and to Zero Trust concepts such as device trust and conditional access.

• Experience administering Jira Service Management or a similar ITSM tool.

Nice to have:

• Experience with SSO and provisioning (SAML, SCIM).

OUR TECH STACK:

• Netskope (SSE/SASE)

• Jamf Pro and Microsoft Intune

• Mac, Windows and ChromeOS endpoints

• Okta

• C1

• Cisco Meraki

• Jira, Confluence and Jira Service Management

Our location-specific employee benefits are designed to cater to the unique needs of Tideans:

• Mental wellbeing platform

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Analytical Sciences
jobs.description:
About Summit:

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

• HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

• HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

• HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

• HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.

Senior Manager, Analytical Sciences

Location: Princeton, New Jersey

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Analytical Sciences will provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical activities supporting biologic products from clinical development through post-approval support. This role is responsible for advancing robust analytical strategies, overseeing method development, validation, and transfer, and contributing to product characterization, comparability assessments, and regulatory submissions. The successful candidate will combine strong technical expertise with effective external partner management, sound judgment, and a flexible, hands-on approach in a dynamic development environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead analytical method development, qualification, validation, and transfer activities for biologic drug substances and drug products.

• Design and oversee extended product characterization studies to establish a comprehensive understanding of product quality attributes.

• Develop analytical strategies and execute comparability assessments supporting process changes, manufacturing changes, formulation changes, technology transfers, and product lifecycle activities.

• Author and critically review analytical sections of regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions.

• Ensure analytical programs align with relevant ICH guidelines and global regulatory expectations across preclinical, clinical, registration, and post-approval stages.

• Provide scientific interpretation of analytical data, identify risks, and recommend practical, phase-appropriate solutions.

• Manage contract laboratories, contract development and manufacturing organizations, and other external partners, including defining scope, monitoring timelines and deliverables, reviewing technical work, and resolving issues.

• Partner cross-functionally with Process Development, Formulation, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and other CMC functions to deliver integrated development plans.

• Contribute to continuous improvement of analytical capabilities, technical standards, workflows, and documentation practices.

• Demonstrate a flexible, collaborative, and can-do attitude while responding effectively to changing priorities and business needs.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, chemical engineering, biology, or a related scientific discipline; an advanced degree is preferred.

• Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in the biotechnology, biopharmaceutical, or pharmaceutical industry.

• Demonstrated experience with analytical method development, validation, and transfer for biologics.

• Experience with extended product characterization and comparability assessments for biologic products.

• Hands-on experience authoring and reviewing analytical content for regulatory submissions.

• Strong knowledge of relevant ICH guidelines and regulatory expectations for biologics from preclinical development through post-approval support.

• Proven experience managing external laboratories, vendors, or development and manufacturing partners.

• Strong scientific writing, data interpretation, problem-solving, project management, and stakeholder communication skills.

Work Expectations

• This position is based at the company’s Princeton, New Jersey site.

• Ability and willingness to work outside standard business hours when needed to support critical activities and global business needs.

• Ability and willingness to travel for business, including visits to external partners and manufacturing or laboratory sites.

This is the pay for this position

Pay Transparency

$148,000—$188,000 USD

Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor. The total compensation package for this position may also include bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable variable compensation.

Summit does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact Summit’s Talent Acquisition team at recruiting@smmttx.com to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to Summit.

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and takes pride in creating and maintaining diverse environment. We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training or promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At JRM Construction, we build more than exceptional spaces - we build talented teams, rewarding careers, and trusted relationships. As a leading employee-owned construction firm, our people take ownership of every project and work collaboratively to deliver outstanding quality and a positive client experience. Guided by integrity, teamwork, continuous improvement, and genuine care for our people, JRM provides an environment where employees can grow and help shape the company’s long-term success.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Cybersecurity Analyst who combines a strong foundation in Windows-based IT administration with hands-on experience designing, implementing, and operating modern information security tools, alongside a governance-focused mindset. This role is critical to the success of our security operations and will play a key part in evaluating, testing, and deploying emerging technologies and new procedures, ensuring JRM remains proactive in an ever-evolving cybersecurity landscape. The ideal candidate is not only technically proficient but also highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain detailed documentation, and uphold structured workflows. The Analyst also shares responsibility for incident response.

Reporting directly to the Manager of Information Security, this position offers an exciting opportunity for a security-minded technologist to thrive within a forward-thinking program that values agility, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Governance & Risk Management:

• Assist in developing, documenting, and enforcing cybersecurity policies, standards, and control procedures.

• Support alignment with frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and CIS Controls.

• Maintain the security risk register and perform technical risk assessments and drive remediation to closure.

Windows IT Administration & Hardening:

• Leverage expertise in Windows Server, Active Directory, DNS, Group Policy, and PowerShell to engineer, automate, and maintain secure system baselines.

• Work with the IT and infrastructure teams to ensure secure configurations and compliance enforcement across the environment.

• Deploy, configure, and tune endpoint management and compliance controls using modern UEM, MDM, and EDR tools.

Identity Security & Access Management:

• Implement identity governance practices, privileged access controls, phishing resistant MFA, and conditional access policy design across Microsoft Entra ID and other third-party IdPs.

• Automate and improve lifecycle management processes, including secure onboarding and offboarding.

Phishing Defense & Awareness:

• Operate a phishing simulation and security awareness platform, run phishing simulations, and report on campaign effectiveness.

• Triage user-reported phishing attempts and maintain IT communication templates and user education content.

Security Engineering & Tooling:

• Design, deploy, and maintain core security platforms, including EDR, SIEM, email security, and vulnerability management.

• Maintain configuration baselines and documentation for deployed security tools.

• Integrate security tools with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and the broader IT environment to improve visibility and reduce manual effort.

• Run vulnerability scanning, prioritize findings by risk, and coordinate remediation with IT and infrastructure teams.

Detection, Incident Response & Automation:

• Monitor SIEM alerts and dashboards, and tune detections to reduce noise.

• Act as a technical responder in security incidents: triage, investigate, contain, and document root cause and lessons learned.

• Support incident response playbooks and tabletop exercises.

• Automate repetitive security tasks and response workflows using PowerShell, Python, and SOAR or automation platforms.

Innovation & Emerging Technology Evaluation:

• Participate in research, testing, and proof-of-concept (PoC) efforts for new cybersecurity tools, technologies, and frameworks.

• Deploy new technologies and procedures that improve detection, prevention, and governance.

• Provide technical input and analysis for tool evaluations, pilots, and strategic initiatives.

Qualifications

Required:

• 3+ years of experience in IT administration, systems engineering, or information security, with a strong focus on Windows environments.

• Familiarity with Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), third-party IDP providers, Intune, and modern endpoint security tools.

• Scripting and automation skills in PowerShell.

• Understanding of cybersecurity frameworks and governance models (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS).

• Analytical, collaborative, and adaptable mindset with strong documentation skills.

Preferred:

• Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and tuning security tools such as EDR, email security, and vulnerability management platforms, or evaluating emerging and cloud security solutions.

• Exposure to SIEM detection engineering and SOAR or automation platforms.

• Experience in risk assessments, audit preparation, or compliance reporting.

• Familiarity with Python, SQL, or Bash/Shell for automation and security analysis.

Salary Information
To the extent this position is performed in New York City, the annual salary range for this role is $90,000 - $110,000.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment at JRM without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

The salary range listed in job postings reflects the Company’s good-faith estimate at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as position tier, geographic location, work experience, market conditions, education/training, and skills.

jobs.title: Senior Incident Response Analyst - InfoSec
jobs.description:

As a Senior Incident Response Analyst at Elastic, you are one of the front-line defenders for ensuring we are delivering safe and secure products and services to our customers, users, and fellow Elasticians. You will be responsible for reviewing and responding to alerts across a wide variety of sources that include multiple cloud providers, CI/CD environments, SaaS services, user workstations, and much more. Elastic is distributed globally by design, and we model our response practice around that same concept; enabling domain experts to respond with oversight from the Incident Response team and relying on you to provide oversight and guidance to these experts. You’ll also dive in and provide support in identifying what happened, who did it, when, and where to ensure we’ve accurately secured our environment during and after security events. If doing all of this with the Elastic Stack excites you, then we’d love to talk with you!

• Review and respond to alerts generated from our Elastic Detection Engine and other monitoring sources

• Provide feedback to the Threat Detection team to improve the quality of detections by identifying false positives, enrichment opportunities, and automated response possibilities

• Conduct analysis on SIEM and/or endpoint logs during complex investigations

• Develop and document innovative approaches to detect, respond to, and eradicate advanced threats and improve overall time to respond

• Identify additional integration points that would aid in event enrichment and enable automated response activities

• Gather additional context for security events

• Identify the root cause of events and collaborate with teams to remediate any identified control gaps or failures

• Oversee and coordinate response activities that span multiple teams and products to ensure comprehensive remediation and sufficient mitigation of any identified gaps in security posture

What You Bring

• At least 3 years of experience related to security operations / incident response in a complex, global environment. SaaS and cloud experience is a plus.

• Demonstrated ability to solve complex IT and security problems through log and system analysis (Incident Response, SRE, System Administration). If you’ve done this with the help of the Elastic Stack, even better!

• Demonstrated ability to think innovatively about solving critical security problems; Experience or a desire to optimize processes via AI/ML would be a plus.

• Experience coordinating response activities to resolve IT and security-related problems with the right people in a timely manner.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to make sound decisions with limited information, and embrace challenging the status quo.

• Are eligible to work in DoD Impact Level 4 or above cloud service environments

jobs.title: Bulk Truck Logistics Coordinator
jobs.description:

This position is responsible for scheduling freight and servicing customers of liquid food and feed ingredients in North America, with a focus on product manufactured in Upper Sandusky, OH. This position would also have responsibility to help with negotiating and managing freight contracts with freight providers. This position would also perform various reporting tasks, communicating documents with customers, and any other customer service needs.

• Generate load numbers for customer orders in a timely and accurate manner
• Schedule orders with carriers and maintain schedule changes
• Prepare and organize paperwork needed for shipments
• Ticket application for multiple products, freight matching, and filing
• Communicate professionally with customers to coordinate deliveries in a timely manner

• Coordinate quality requirements and issues from customers with LDC lab and operations team
• Assist with setting up carriers and maintaining documents and certificates

• Work with sales staff to ensure they have competitive transportation rates to accurately quote business for customers and manage existing business lanes

• Associate Degree in supply chain, industrial management, business, finance, or economics
• Or, 2 years’ experience in oilseeds, or logistics or supply chain management

Preferred qualifications:

Employee Supervision

Job Summary

The General Counsel serves as AMAROK’s senior legal strategist and trusted advisor to executive leadership. This role will be instrumental in providing strategic legal counsel, guiding enterprise risk management, and establishing scalable legal frameworks that safeguard the organization’s interests while advancing business objectives and long-term growth. The General Counsel will be charged with leading commercial transactions, directing litigation and dispute strategies, partnering on employment and labor matters, and ensuring rigorous corporate governance, working collaboratively across the company to protect our assets and support enterprise-wide initiatives.

The ideal candidate will translate complex legal matters into clear, actionable recommendations, balancing legal considerations with commercial priorities. By leading a high-performing legal and compliance function and leveraging data-driven insights, this individual will drive impactful risk mitigation and operational excellence, strengthening AMAROK's market leadership and addressing evolving business requirements. Success involves proactive legal strategies, robust contract governance, optimized outside counsel management, minimized legal exposure, and aligned business growth. This position is based in Columbia, SC.

Your Impact

• Serve as a trusted legal advisor to executive leadership, providing strategic counsel on business operations, corporate initiatives, governance, and enterprise-wide legal matters.

• Lead legal oversight of commercial transactions, including the drafting, review, negotiation, and execution of customer, vendor, real estate, financing, partnership, and other business agreements.

• Direct the company's legal strategy for litigation, disputes, claims, investigations, and administrative proceedings while overseeing external legal counsel and managing legal expenditures.

• Partner with Human Resources and executive leadership on complex employment matters, workforce decisions, labor and employment compliance, and workplace investigations.

• Provide legal oversight and guidance on corporate governance matters, including Board of Directors activities, corporate records, legal entity structures, and statutory obligations.

• Lead enterprise risk management by identifying, evaluating, and mitigating significant legal risks across contractual, operational, financial, and reputational domains.

• Protect company assets including intellectual property, proprietary technology, confidential information, and contractual rights through robust legal strategies.

• Establish scalable contract governance frameworks, review standards, approval authorities, negotiation guidelines, and risk assessment protocols to enhance operational efficiency.

• Drive continuous improvement of legal operations, processes, and policies to support efficient, consistent, and scalable legal services across departments.

• Monitor significant legislative, regulatory, and legal developments, assessing potential business implications and recommending appropriate organizational responses.

• Collaborate with Compliance and functional leadership to evaluate regulatory requirements and strengthen adherence to applicable federal, state, and local laws.

• Champion legal awareness and sound business judgment through leadership consultation, education, and practical guidance across the organization.

• Stay at the forefront of the corporate legal and security industry landscape by proactively identifying emerging legal trends, commercial risks, and strategic opportunities.

What You'll Bring

• Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from an accredited law school.

• Active membership in good standing with at least one state bar (eligibility for admission in South Carolina or ability to obtain admission within a reasonable period preferred).

• 5+ years of legal experience in a law firm, corporate legal department, or combination thereof, with significant experience in commercial contracts, business law, litigation management, employment law, and regulatory compliance.

• Strong professional legal network with the ability to easily tap into external counsel, industry experts, and specialized legal resources as needed.

• Proven experience supporting executive leadership and advising business stakeholders.

• Ability to excel in a fast-paced corporate environment with strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.

jobs.title: Associate Director, CMC Statistics
jobs.description:
About Summit:

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

• HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

• HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

• HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

• HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.

Associate Director, CMC Statistics

Job Title: Associate Director, CMC Statistics
Department: CMC
Location: Princeton, NJ (Onsite; four days per week)
Reports To: Executive Director, Analytical Sciences

Overview of Role

The Associate Director, CMC Statistics, will provide hands-on statistical leadership across Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) activities. This individual will partner with Analytical Sciences, MSAT, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and external CDMOs/CROs to develop scientifically sound, phase-appropriate, and regulatory-defensible statistical strategies for drug substance and drug product development. The role will be accountable for statistical support of specification setting, stability trending and shelf-life assessment, analytical method bridging and transfer, comparability assessments, method validation, process and product monitoring, investigations, and lifecycle management. The successful candidate will translate complex CMC datasets into clear conclusions, risk assessments, and recommendations that support global regulatory submissions, commercial readiness, and ongoing product control.

Role and Responsibilities

• Serve as the CMC statistical subject matter expert for biologic drug substance and drug product development, registration, commercialization, and lifecycle management.

• Develop and execute statistical strategies for specification setting, including establishment and justification of release and stability acceptance criteria, control limits, tolerance intervals, and clinically and process-relevant decision rules.

• Lead statistical evaluation of stability data, including trend analysis, shelf-life and retest-period modeling, protocol design, pooling assessments, extrapolation, and ongoing stability monitoring.

• Design and analyze analytical method bridging, transfer, qualification, and validation studies; define acceptance criteria and assess equivalence, comparability, precision, accuracy, linearity, range, robustness, and intermediate precision.

• Lead statistical planning and analysis for analytical and product comparability assessments associated with process changes, manufacturing-site transfers, scale changes, method changes, and post-approval activities.

• Provide statistical support for analytical control strategies, critical quality attribute assessments, process characterization, process validation, continued process verification, and product quality reviews.

• Apply appropriate methods such as regression, analysis of variance, mixed models, equivalence testing, multivariate analysis, design of experiments, control charts, capability analysis, and risk-based sampling to CMC datasets.

• Support deviations, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, root-cause assessments, CAPAs, and change controls through objective statistical analysis and clear interpretation.

• Author and review statistical analysis plans, protocols, reports, technical memos, procedures, regulatory submission sections, and responses to health authority questions.

• Ensure statistical approaches align with applicable ICH guidance, global regulatory expectations, cGMP requirements, data-integrity principles, and internal quality standards.

• Partner with external CDMOs, CROs, and testing laboratories to align study designs, data standards, analyses, deliverables, and timelines; critically review vendor analyses and resolve technical issues.

• Develop fit-for-purpose statistical tools, templates, standards, and governance approaches that improve consistency, efficiency, traceability, and data-driven decision-making across CMC.

• Communicate complex statistical concepts and conclusions clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, influence cross-functional decisions, and present recommendations to senior leadership.

• Manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, resource-lean environment and perform other duties as assigned.

Experience, Education, and Specialized Knowledge and Skills

Required Qualifications

• Advanced degree (PhD, ScD, or equivalent preferred; master’s degree considered) in Statistics, Biostatistics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related quantitative discipline.

• Minimum of 10 years of industry experience applying statistics to biologics CMC activities in a biopharmaceutical or biotechnology setting.

• Direct, substantial experience with specification setting, stability trending and shelf-life assessment, analytical method bridging, and comparability assessment is required.

• Demonstrated experience supporting biologic drug substance and drug product programs and working with analytical, manufacturing, quality, and regulatory data.

• Strong command of statistical methods relevant to CMC, including regression, ANOVA, mixed models, equivalence and non-inferiority approaches, tolerance intervals, control charts, capability analysis, multivariate methods, and design of experiments.

• Experience applying statistical principles to analytical method qualification, validation, transfer, lifecycle monitoring, and investigations.

• Working knowledge of applicable ICH guidance, FDA and EMA expectations, cGMP requirements, and data-integrity standards for biologics development and commercialization.

• Proficiency with one or more statistical software platforms such as JMP, SAS, R, Python, or Minitab, with the ability to produce reproducible, traceable analyses and effective data visualizations.

• Experience authoring or reviewing technical protocols, statistical analysis plans, reports, regulatory submission content, and health authority responses.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain statistical concepts and business implications to non-statistical audiences.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound scientific judgment, influence cross-functional teams, and manage multiple priorities with high attention to quality and detail.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, or other complex biologics.

• Experience supporting late-stage development, BLA/MAA submissions, commercial readiness, process validation, PPQ, post-approval changes, and product lifecycle management.

• Experience operating in an outsourced or virtual development model with CDMOs, CROs, and external testing laboratories.

• Experience establishing CMC statistical standards, procedures, templates, analysis plans, or governance frameworks.

• Familiarity with data visualization and reporting tools such as Spotfire, Tableau, or comparable platforms.

Key Competencies

• Scientific and statistical rigor with pragmatic, risk-based judgment.

• Clear communication and the ability to translate data into actionable CMC decisions.

• Collaboration, influence, and stakeholder management across internal teams and external partners.

• Proactive problem-solving, agility, and accountability in a dynamic environment.

• Commitment to quality, compliance, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

Work Location and Travel

This position is based onsite in Summit’s Princeton, New Jersey office and requires in-office presence four days per week. Periodic travel may be required to support CDMO/CRO oversight, technical meetings, audits, inspections, regulatory interactions, or cross-functional workshops.

Additional Information

The pay range for this role will vary depending on location. Actual compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. The total compensation package may also include bonus, stock, benefits, and/or other applicable variable compensation.

Summit is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are made without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Vice President, CMC Regulatory Affairs
jobs.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera’s mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.

We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

What You’ll Do:

Vice President of CMC Regulatory will lead all aspects of CMC Regulatory. Reporting into the Senior Vice President of Regulatory, you will provide strategic and operational leadership to ensure the effectiveness of the CMC Regulatory team and the integrated CMC team. With their lead candidate planning to initiate Phase 3, the candidate must plan for and have extensive drug development expertise. The company offers innovative science, competitive compensation, and a patient-focused company culture.

Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week) OR Remote (home-based, onsite at a hub 1 week every other month).

Responsibilities:

• Develop and own the global CMC regulatory strategy for the portfolio, and provide input to corporate and program strategy, including Phase 3 readiness, marketing application planning, and launch

• Serve as the company's lead CMC voice with FDA, EMA, and other global health authorities, including leading CMC-focused meetings (e.g., End-of-Phase 2, pre-submission, Scientific Advice) and responses to information requests

• Responsible for ensuring the appropriate execution of CMC regulatory strategy

• Set standards and expectations for submission quality and cross-functional delivery and hold the team accountable for results

• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing CMC Regulatory team as the company scales toward registration. This includes organizational design, hiring, succession planning, and coaching managers to grow as leaders

• Oversee all CMC-related submission planning and execution, ensuring that high quality and accurate submission documents are completed within target timelines

• Accurately interpret and discuss data within cross-functional teams and with health authorities

• Anticipate evolving global regulatory expectations and industry trends, advise executive leadership on their impact, and adjust CMC regulatory strategy accordingly

• Lead the preparation of risk assessments on CMC regulatory topics. Predict potential regulatory questions and develop robust contingency and mitigation plans with the integrated CMC team

• Establish and lead strategic relationships with CDMO partners, health authorities, and internal executives, and break down silos to enable integrated CMC execution

• Ensure CMC dossiers meet ICH format and content requirements, as well as specific local requirements of individual countries

• Determine resourcing, budget, and use of external consultants and vendors for CMC Regulatory, and influence resource allocation across the integrated CMC organization (Process Development, Manufacturing, Analytical, Quality)

• Partner with Quality and Technical Operations on commercial manufacturing readiness, process validation, comparability, and pre-approval inspection strategy. Define the post-approval change and lifecycle management strategy

Required Qualifications:

• 15+ years of biopharmaceutical industry experience; with 10+ years of relevant Regulatory CMC

• Demonstrated track record of successful submissions to FDA and/or other health authorities, including EMA

• Ability to apply scientific principles to assess regulatory issues, request and collect relevant information, analyze data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions

• Ability to motivate and lead others, both with direct line and within integrated team

• Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills as well as the ability to effectively lead and influence others

• Comfortable in a fast-paced small company environment with minimal direction and able to adjust workload based upon changing priorities

Education:

• BS degree in Biochemistry, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering or related field required; advanced degree preferred

Salary Range

$272,000—$340,000 USD

For Full Time Roles: This range represents the company’s good-faith estimate of the salary at the time of posting. Actual pay may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and internal equity. We also offer comprehensive health coverage, flexible time off, paid holidays, and a year-end shutdown. Enjoy a monthly wellness stipend, generous 401(k) match, tuition reimbursement, commuter benefits, disability and life insurance, plus annual bonus opportunities and equity grants—because your well-being and future matter to us.
