jobs.title: Program Manager, Accounting Operations & Strategy
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a Program Manager to join our Accounting organization and help it run as one global team. Accounting is scaling at an unprecedented pace across multiple hubs, and the goals, rhythms, programs, and people that make up the team need to stay connected as we grow. In this role, you will own that connective tissue: the annual goal-setting cycle, the leadership team’s operating cadence, org-wide events and internal communications, and the programs that make a distributed team feel like one.

You will partner with Accounting leadership, the People team, Finance Systems, and hub leads. This is a hands-on role with a lot of range: part chief of staff, part program manager, part culture builder.

Responsibilities

Goals and operating rhythm

• Run the annual goal setting process and the reporting that tracks progress against those goals.

• Look at how the org actually operates (meetings, handoffs, planning cycles, decision making) and fix what isn't working.

• Maintain one org-wide planning calendar that shows close, audit, and team milestones alongside company-wide and team events, so leaders can see the pressure points and plan around them.

• Build and maintain a simple set of org health metrics (attrition, engagement scores, hiring pipeline, training completion, survey trends) and report on them regularly.

Leadership and org-wide events

• Run our extended leadership team (XLT) program, including agendas, meetings, follow-ups, and action items.

• Own planning and agenda for the annual offsite and run the quarterly team all-hands.

• Write the internal updates: a regular team newsletter, plus talking points when leadership needs to explain a change to the whole org.

People and culture

• Coordinate projects across the org that support employee experience programs.

• Partner with the People team to roll out training and development programs for Accounting.

• Review team survey results, identify the themes, and build action plans to address the feedback. Follow through and report back to the team.

• Run hub programs, including visit and rotation programs, local hub events, and meeting norms that work across time zones, so we feel like one global team.

• Run recognition and team rituals: wins, milestones, anniversaries, and peer recognition, especially across hubs.

Team operations

• Support contractor management, including onboarding, tracking, and coordination with the right partners.

• Keep the team's knowledge base current: wiki, org charts, role descriptions, and key process docs.

• Keep the team calendar accurate so everyone knows what's coming.

Preferred qualifications

• 7+ years in program management, operations, chief of staff, or strategy roles. Experience inside a finance or accounting org is a plus, but not required.

• A track record of running recurring programs end to end and getting people to follow through without formal authority.

• Good judgment about what matters and what doesn't. You can handle a lot of moving pieces without dropping them.

• Clear, direct writing. You can brief a senior leader in a few sentences.

• Comfort with confidential information and sensitive people topics.

• Experience supporting distributed or global teams.

• You're organized, but you also know when a process is getting in the way and should be simplified.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$230,000—$300,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Director of Analytical Services
jobs.description:
Before reading the job post, we encourage you to watch this video about our company. It gives you an inside look at how we started, the team and culture that made us successful, and where we're going. It's easy to read a job post and apply, but people often wonder about the culture and whether they would fit in. If you want to call Harrow your home and genuinely want to be part of a family and something big, then we encourage you to click this link and get to know us.

Who is Harrow?

Harrow (Nasdaq: HROW) is a leading provider of ophthalmic disease management solutions in North America. Harrow is an incredible entrepreneurial company – where we celebrate the ability of every member of the Harrow Family to be the CEO of their job. Harrow’s values have driven interest over the past decade in attracting high-performing professionals in a variety of disciplines. Members of our Harrow Family often express their pride in being a part of our commitment to (1) innovation, (2) patient access to affordable medicines, and (3) our track record of having never turned down an ophthalmologist doing mission work around the world – providing free medicines in support of mission work aimed at giving or maintaining the gift of sight to those most in need.  We encourage you to learn more about Harrow and its unique culture to see if you’re the right person to help contribute as we build a truly exceptional company, one we are all so proud of!

Harrow’s ophthalmic pharmaceutical portfolio is one of the most comprehensive in the industry, including:

• An expanding Retina Portfolio including IHEEZO®, TRIESENCE®, BYOOVIZTM, and OPUVIZTM

• A broad Dry Eye Disease product line, led by VEVYE® and bolstered by well-known adjacent ocular surface disease products such as FLAREX® and FRESHKOTE®

• A peri-operative Surgical product line, led by TRIESENCE®, and BYQLOVITM

• A Rare and Specialty product line, which includes various high-need and utility products such as ILEVRO®, NATACYN®, and VERKAZIA®

• A robust internal development pipeline with multiple late-stage candidates, including MELT-300, MELT-210, H-N08, and CR-01

Job Summary

The Director, Analytical Services is a hands-on leader who runs the analytical laboratory and works at the bench alongside the team. The role is accountable for the quality, compliance, and timeliness of all analytical testing that supports drug product release, stability, and qualification of raw materials and APIs. The Director personally performs complex testing, method development and validation, instrument troubleshooting, data review, and laboratory investigations, while setting the laboratory's scientific and operational direction. The Director partners closely with Quality and Operations to align laboratory capacity with production demand, serves as the analytical subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and audits, and drives the laboratory's modernization, including equipment renewal, LIMS, and paperless data systems.

Core Responsibilities

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for the analytical laboratory, including setting laboratory goals, priorities, and key performance indicators (KPIs) such as on-time release, right-first-time testing, data review cycle time, OOS and investigation closure rates, and equipment uptime.

• Perform and direct routine and non-routine analytical testing, including in-process, finished product release, stability, raw material, and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) testing, in compliance with approved specifications, USP-NF monographs, written procedures, and cGMP requirements (21 CFR Parts 210 and 211).

• Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality to forecast production volume and testing demand, and plan laboratory staffing, instrument capacity, and scheduling to meet release timelines.

• Personally lead and perform analytical method development, transfer, verification, and validation at the bench consistent with ICH Q2(R2), ICH Q14, and USP <1225>, <1226>, and <1224>, including impurity and degradation product methods.

• Lead the stability program, including protocol design, study execution, data trending, and support for beyond-use dating (BUD) assignments.

• Ensure data integrity across paper and electronic systems in accordance with ALCOA+ principles and 21 CFR Part 11; perform second-person data review and audit trail review and oversee electronic system access controls.

• Serve as the laboratory's primary technical troubleshooter for HPLC, UPLC, GC, and other instruments, and resolve chromatographic, method, and instrument issues directly at the bench.

• Step into routine bench testing and data review as needed to meet release timelines and cover peaks in testing volume.

• Own and personally conduct laboratory investigations, including OOS, OOT, and laboratory deviations, with timely, scientifically sound root cause analysis and effective CAPA within the Quality Management System (e.g., Veeva).

• Serve as the analytical subject matter expert and primary laboratory representative during FDA inspections, state board of pharmacy inspections, customer audits, and internal audits, and lead timely responses to observations.

• Lead equipment and instrument lifecycle management, including qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), calibration, preventive maintenance, and capital planning for replacement of aging equipment.

• Drive laboratory modernization initiatives, including the implementation of LIMS, chromatography data systems (e.g., Chromeleon), and paperless laboratory workflows, in partnership with IT and Quality.

• Develop and manage the laboratory operating and capital budgets, and oversee contract testing laboratories, including vendor qualification, technical oversight, and review of outsourced data.

• Recruit, develop, and retain a high-performing team of chemists, data reviewers, and laboratory managers; set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and train and coach analysts at the bench on techniques, methods, and good documentation practices.

• Author, review, and approve SOPs, specifications, test methods, protocols, and reports, and drive continuous improvement in laboratory efficiency, quality, and compliance.

• Hold regular operational reviews with laboratory staff and senior leadership to communicate laboratory performance, risks, and resource needs.

• Maintain a safe laboratory environment in compliance with OSHA regulations, chemical hygiene, and established safety procedures.

• Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications & Requirements

• Minimum BS in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline; MS or PhD preferred

• At least twelve years of analytical laboratory experience in a cGMP pharmaceutical environment, including at least five years in a laboratory leadership role with direct reports

• Current, hands-on bench expertise with HPLC, UPLC, GC, FTIR, UV-Vis, Karl Fischer, and related techniques, including instrument troubleshooting, and with chromatography data systems such as Chromeleon or Empower

• Willingness and ability to work at the bench as a player-coach, performing testing, method work, and data review alongside the team

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with analytical method development and validation, impurity testing, and stability programs

• In-depth knowledge of USP-NF, ICH guidelines, 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 11, and FDA expectations for data integrity

• Proven track record of leading OOS, deviation, and CAPA investigations using root cause analysis tools

• Experience hosting or supporting FDA and other regulatory inspections

• Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (e.g., Veeva) and LIMS; experience leading a LIMS or paperless laboratory implementation is preferred

• Experience managing laboratory budgets, capital equipment planning, and contract laboratory relationships

• Strong leadership, decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present data and recommendations to senior leadership

• Must be computer literate, with working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

• Must be able to maintain a safe working environment and follow safety procedures

Position Type

• On-Site

Travel

• Up to 15%, including travel between company sites and to contract laboratories and vendors

As part of the IT Support team, you will be on the front lines supporting team members across the organization — solving everyday technical problems, building relationships, and delivering excellent service.

Required

jobs.title: Fabrication Supervisor - Houston, TX

Fabrication Supervisor

Crane Structural Fabrication

Location: Houston, Texas

Company: Konecranes

Position Summary

Konecranes is seeking a hands-on Fabrication Supervisor to lead fabrication personnel responsible for the manufacturing of custom-engineered crane structures, including bridge girders, end trucks, trolley frames, platforms, walkways, machinery structures, and other welded assemblies used in overhead and gantry crane systems.

The Fabrication Foreman is responsible for the safe, efficient, and high-quality execution of all fabrication activities, including material preparation, fit-up, welding, dimensional verification, and structural assembly. This position provides direct leadership to fabrication employees and is accountable for safety, productivity, quality, schedule adherence, and workmanship.

Success in this role requires a visible leader who actively engages on the shop floor, promotes accountability, and ensures all fabricated structures meet engineering requirements, dimensional tolerances, and applicable welding standards, including AWS D14.1. The ideal candidate understands that crane manufacturing demands exceptional precision, weld quality, and structural integrity to ensure safe and reliable operation in the field.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

• Lead and direct welders, fitters, fabricators, and production personnel.
• Establish clear performance expectations and hold employees accountable for safety, quality, productivity, and attendance.
• Promote a culture of craftsmanship, ownership, discipline, and continuous improvement.
• Provide coaching, training, and development opportunities for fabrication employees.
• Support employee development and succession planning within the department.
• Foster teamwork and collaboration between Fabrication, Engineering, Quality, Planning, and Assembly teams.
• Maintain a visible presence on the shop floor and actively support daily operations.

Fabrication Operations

• Oversee fabrication, fit-up, welding, grinding, structural assembly, and material handling activities.
• Coordinate manpower, equipment, and resources to meet production schedules and customer delivery commitments.
• Monitor workflow and remove obstacles impacting productivity and throughput.
• Ensure fabrication processes are executed in accordance with approved drawings, work instructions, and welding procedures.
• Manage daily production priorities and communicate progress, risks, and resource needs to management.
• Drive labor efficiency while maintaining quality and safety expectations.
• Coordinate with engineering and quality personnel to resolve fabrication issues and drawing discrepancies.

Welding Quality & Structural Integrity

• Ensure all welding activities are performed in accordance with approved Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS), quality requirements, and AWS D14.1 standards.
• Verify weld quality through proper fit-up, joint preparation, welding practices, and visual inspection standards.
• Ensure welders maintain required qualifications and certifications.
• Drive first-pass weld quality and minimize weld repairs and rework.
• Review weld defects, nonconformances, and repair activities and implement corrective actions.
• Work closely with Quality personnel to ensure compliance with inspection and testing requirements.
• Promote workmanship standards that result in safe, structurally sound crane components.
• Quality & Dimensional Control
• Ensure fabricated structures meet engineering drawings, specifications, and customer requirements.
• Maintain strict control of dimensional tolerances, structural alignment, and fabrication accuracy.
• Verify girder geometry, wheel alignment, rail alignment, span dimensions, camber requirements, and structural squareness.
• Ensure fabricated components transition to assembly operations without quality-related delays.
• Drive first-time quality and reduce fabrication-related rework.
• Support root-cause analysis and implementation of corrective actions for recurring quality issues.
• Ensure all required inspection documentation and production records are completed accurately.
• Safety Leadership
• Lead and promote a strong safety-first culture throughout fabrication operations.
• Ensure compliance with all Konecranes safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
• Conduct routine safety observations, audits, and corrective actions.
• Promote safe welding, cutting, rigging, lifting, and material handling practices.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and efficient work environment utilizing 5S principles.
• Actively investigate incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions and implement corrective measures.

*This position will be located on the factory floor

Desired Qualifications

• Experience leading fabrication, welding, structural steel, heavy equipment, or industrial manufacturing operations.
• Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop hourly production personnel.
• Thorough understanding of welding processes, fabrication methods, and structural assembly techniques.
• Working knowledge of AWS D14.1 welding requirements and quality standards.
• Ability to read and interpret fabrication drawings, weld symbols, inspection reports, and engineering documentation.
• Experience with dimensional inspection, alignment verification, and structural tolerance control.
• Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Crane manufacturing, structural steel fabrication, bridge construction, heavy equipment, or similar experience preferred.

What Success Looks Like

• Consistent achievement of fabrication schedules and production targets.
• High first-pass weld acceptance rates.
• Reduced weld repairs, rework, and quality escapes.
• Compliance with AWS D14.1 and Konecranes workmanship standards.
• Improved labor productivity and fabrication efficiency.
• Strong employee accountability, engagement, and development.
• Safe, organized, and disciplined fabrication operations.
• Delivery of structurally sound, dimensionally accurate crane components ready for assembly.

What we offer:

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

Konecranes moves what matters. Konecranes is a global leader in material handling solutions, serving a broad range of customers across multiple industries. We consistently set the industry benchmark, from everyday improvements to the breakthroughs at moments that matter most, because we know we can always find a safer, more productive and sustainable way. That's why, with 16 000+ professionals in over 50 countries, we are trusted every day to lift, handle and move what the world needs.

• Monitor productivity and remove obstacles impacting performance.
• Ensure assembly activities are completed according to engineering requirements.

• Verify proper alignment of hoists, gearboxes, motors, wheel assemblies, drive systems, and other rotating equipment utilizing precision measurement tools and alignment techniques.

• Ensure assemblies meet engineering drawings and specifications.
• Maintain compliance with Konecranes workmanship standards.
• Verify completion of inspection checkpoints and quality documentation.
• Drive first-pass quality and reduce rework.
• Ensure completed assemblies are prepared for electrical installation and testing.

Safety Leadership

• Lead and promote a strong safety culture.
• Ensure compliance with company safety policies and procedures.
• Conduct routine safety observations and corrective actions.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and efficient work environment.

* This position will be located on the factory floor.

Desired Qualifications

• Demonstrated experience installing and precision aligning industrial machinery, including motors, gearboxes, hoists, couplings, bearings, and related power transmission equipment.
• Knowledge of machinery alignment principles, mechanical tolerances, precision measurement tools, and industrial assembly best practices.
• Experience leading mechanical assembly operations in manufacturing, industrial equipment, heavy machinery, or construction-related industries.
• Strong leadership and communication skills.
• Ability to interpret mechanical drawings and assembly documentation.
• Experience managing production schedules and workforce performance.
• Knowledge of overhead cranes, material handling equipment, or heavy industrial equipment preferred.

What Success Looks Like

• Safe execution of all assembly activities.
• Consistent achievement of production schedules.
• High first-pass assembly quality.
• Reduced rework and production delays.
• Strong employee engagement and accountability.
• Effective coordination with fabrication, electrical assembly, testing, and planning teams.

jobs.title: Manager, Service Delivery
jobs.description:
At Jamf, we believe in an open, flexible culture based on respect and trust. Our track record and thriving work environment all stem from the freedom we grant ourselves to get the job done right. We take pride in helping tens of thousands of customers around the globe succeed with Apple.

The secret to our success lies in our connectivity, while operating with a high degree of flexibility. Work-life balance remains our priority while feeling connected is important to maintain our strong culture, achieve our goals, and thrive as #OneJamf.

What You'll Do at Jamf:

The Manager, Service Delivery leads a team of Professional Services engineers serving education customers and is accountable for delivery quality, utilization, and margin across the team's services engagements. The role owns project management for those engagements, balances team capacity between project and consulting work, and builds repeatable practices that let the team scale. The Manager partners with Customer Onboarding, Sales, and Customer Success to scope and forecast work so customers reach successful implementations on time and within budget.

What you can expect to do in this role:

• Leads and develops a team of Professional Services engineers serving education customers by coaching technical and consulting skills, managing performance, supporting career growth, and owning hiring and onboarding so the team can deliver high-quality customer outcomes.

• Manages delivery of services engagements from kickoff through close, owning planning, scheduling, scope and budget control, change requests, status tracking, risk management, and customer communication so projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to quality commitments.

• Manages team capacity and utilization across project delivery and consulting work, forecasting demand with Sales and Customer Success, planning for seasonal peaks tied to education renewal cycles, and giving leadership early visibility into staffing gaps.

• Reviews engagement scopes and estimates with Architects and Sales to confirm work is well scoped, properly staffed, and aligned to margin targets.

• Makes day-to-day staffing, prioritization, and engagement-scoping decisions independently within agreed delivery and margin targets, escalating contract exceptions, headcount changes, and cross-team priority conflicts to Services senior leadership.

• Defines, in partnership with Customer Onboarding, the team's consulting role on customer implementations, including when Services is engaged, what Services provides, and who owns each part of the work.

• Establishes lightweight, repeatable project management practices, such as intake, templates, shared trackers, status reporting, and post-project reviews, so engineers can take on more project ownership and the team can scale.

• Serves as the escalation point for customer and delivery issues on Services engagements, resolving problems quickly and applying lessons learned to prevent recurrence.

• Tracks and reports team performance metrics, including utilization, project health, backlog, margin, and customer satisfaction, and uses the results to improve delivery quality and customer outcomes.

• Partners with Customer Onboarding, Architects, Sales, Customer Success, and other teams to align priorities and solve problems, influencing teams outside the direct reporting line.

• Other duties and special projects as assigned.

What we are looking for:

• 5+ years in professional services, customer implementation, or technical project delivery in a SaaS or technology environment (required)

• 3+ years leading others, through formal people management or through functional or end-to-end project leadership, including coaching, directing work, and accountability for team or project outcomes (required)

• 3+ years managing delivery of multiple concurrent customer projects, including scoping, scheduling, scope and budget control, risk and dependency management, change requests, status reporting, and customer communication (required)

• Experience managing capacity, utilization, or resource forecasting for a delivery or services team (required)

• Ability to influence and align cross-functional partners, such as Sales, Customer Success, and implementation teams, without direct authority (required)

• Strong written and verbal communication, including translating complex technical concepts into plain language for customers and executives and handling difficult conversations and escalations (required)

• Formal people management experience, including hiring and performance management (preferred)

• Experience building lightweight project management practices, such as intake, templates, shared trackers, and status reporting, for a delivery team (preferred)

• Familiarity with Apple device management or the Jamf platform (preferred)

• Familiarity with CRM, project-tracking, and customer success platforms, and with financial and margin reporting for a services team (preferred)

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in business, information technology, or a related field (required)

• A combination of relevant experience and education may be considered (required)

• Project management certification, such as PMP (preferred)

#LIRemote

• We know that big ideas can come from anyone, so we empower everyone to make an impact. Our 90% employee retention rate agrees!

• You will have the opportunity to make a real and meaningful impact for more than 60,000 global customers with the best Apple device management solution in the world.

• Our volunteer time off allows employees to support and give back to our communities.

$95,000—$147,000 USD

We are a team of free-thinkers, can-doers, and problem-crushers. We value humility and the relentless pursuit of knowledge. Our culture flows from a spirit of selflessness and relentless self-improvement - driving both personal growth and collective progress throughout our company. We unite around common goals while respecting personal approaches, believing that fulfilled individuals create a thriving, vibrant workplace.

Our aim is simple: hire exceptionally good people who are incredibly good at what they do and let them do it. We provide the support and resources to let everyone be their authentic, best selves at work, at rest, and at play. Above it all, waves our banner of #OneJamf – and the knowledge that when we stand together, we accomplish so much more than we could alone. We seek individuals who share this unwavering journey toward growth to join us in our quest for constant improvement.

Jamf extends the legendary Apple experience people enjoy in their personal lives to the workplace. jobs.title: Delivery Driver (Non CDL)
jobs.description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Heavy Equipment Delivery Driver (Non CDL)

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We’re hiring a Delivery Driver (Non CDL) at our rental facility in Sherman, TX, and we’re looking for someone who’s ready to grow with us, bring energy and drive to their work, and help us build the future of construction.

Schedule: Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and offers overtime pay after working 40 hours. (This role is subject to on-call scheduling with additional compensation provided)

Primary Responsibilities

We don’t just deliver equipment - we deliver innovation. At EquipmentShare, our technology ensures that our drivers work efficiently and effectively by providing real-time access to fleet locations, work orders, and delivery details.

• Operates vehicle according to applicable state and federal transportation laws

• Transports loads safely and in a timely manner over required route, obeying all traffic laws and observing all safety regulations

• Deftly maneuvers truck and trailer into loading and unloading areas; follows loading crew signals

• Assists with loading of or loads and unloads goods and materials, using specialized equipment when warranted; unloads empty skids and returns all equipment to designated area

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive compensation

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• 401(k) + company match

• Tool and boot reimbursements (role dependent)

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events, food truck nights, and monthly dinner nights

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

• Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

Required Skills/Abilities:

• Strong interpersonal and customer service skills with the ability to speak professionally and courteously with customers and staff at delivery points

• Ability to remain focused in a busy environment

Education and Experience:

• Must hold either a commercial drivers license (Class A CDL) or chauffeur’s license depending on state, appropriate for weight of vehicle to be operated

• Must pass background and drug testing as required by federal and/or state department(s) of transportation regulations

• Must pass DOT physical, as trucks driven are over 10k lbs

• Must be at least 21 years old to operate company vehicle.

Physical Requirements:

• Prolonged periods sitting in a trailer cab for long periods of time

• Must be able to lift and move up to 40 pounds at a time

• Must be able to travel frequently

• CDL drivers may be required to be clean shaven in order to deliver to EquipmentShare customers who have this requirement

• This is a safety sensitive position and any offer of employment will be contingent on passing a 10 panel drug screen

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager (AI Agents)
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRABA



Traba is building the AI operating layer for the industrial supply chain.



We started in the workforce space because contingent labor is the biggest operational pain point our manufacturing and logistics customers face. We used it to embed ourselves inside their daily operations and create a far better customer experience through technology. Now those same customers are pulling us beyond staffing into the broader operational workflows that run their facilities. That foundation gave us proprietary data from millions of shifts and deep enterprise relationships.



But our edge is more than data. By connecting to the systems running across every facility and activating the workers already on our platform to execute against them, we are building applied AI that drives real productivity gains and transforms how the global supply chain operates at scale.



We are backed by Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst.




THE ROLE



We are looking for an entrepreneurial and experienced Product Manager to join as a founding member of the Agents team and help us build the next layer of Traba's product, an agentic platform that synthesizes the data flowing through our marketplace and operates autonomously inside our customers' supply chain workflows. Think Claude, but for Light Industrial businesses.

You'll embed deeply in our customers' operations, design and ship production agents that understand context, reason through ambiguity, make decisions, and execute work on behalf of users. This is a true 0-to-1 product role operating at the frontier of applied AI.

You will work directly with founders, product engineers, ML teams, and early design partners to define workflows, shape product strategy, and build products while the underlying model ecosystem continues changing beneath us. The assumptions, capabilities, and constraints will evolve rapidly and the product will evolve with them.

This role reports directly to our VP of Product.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

jobs.title: Associate Director, Statistical Programming
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Tango Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to discovering novel drug targets and delivering the next generation of precision medicine for the treatment of cancer.

Using an approach that starts and ends with patients, Tango leverages the genetic principle of synthetic lethality to discover and develop therapies that take aim at critical targets in cancer.

This includes expanding the universe of precision oncology targets into novel areas such as tumor suppressor gene loss and their contribution to the ability of cancer cells to evade immune cell killing.

Tango's labs and offices are located at 201 Brookline Avenue, in the Fenway area of Boston, Massachusetts.

Summary

Tango has an exciting opportunity to join our growing Biostatistics team as an Associate Director, Statistical Programming, reporting to the Senior Director of Statistical Programming. In this role, you will be responsible for study-specific statistical programming activities, maintaining programming infrastructure, and ensuring compliance with SOPs to deliver high-quality, timely outputs.

Your Role

• Lead and manage the statistical programming activities for clinical trials and studies, ensuring high-quality and timely deliverables for CSR, publications, presentations, various reports for health authority submissions, clinical data review, and ad hoc analysis either internally or through CRO partners

• Develop, validate, and maintain analysis datasets (SDTM, ADaM), tables, listings, and figures, TLFs) in accordance with regulatory guidelines and internal standards

• Review key clinical study or program documents

• Perform complex statistical analyses and simulations using SAS to support clinical trial design and data interpretation; manage macro library and templates for efficiently preparing, processing, analyzing clinical data and validating analysis results

• Provide expertise in statistical programming for regulatory submissions (e.g., FDA, EMA), including electronic submission standards (eCTD)

• Participate in Tango’s Data Governance Team to build and maintain secure statistical computing and programming infrastructure

• Collaborate with biostatisticians, data managers, and cross-functional team members to define programming strategies and requirements, establish project timelines, and perform statistical analyses

• Manage and provide oversight of CROs to ensure high-quality statistical analysis deliverables (datasets, TLFs, etc.) within timeline and budget

• Author or Review SDTM and ADaM specifications to ensure compliance to CDISC standards

• Review key clinical study or program documents

• Develop SAS code, manage macro library and templates for efficiently preparing, processing, analyzing clinical data, and validating analysis results

• Author and/or review statistical analysis related SOPs

• Stay current with industry trends, best practices, and emerging technologies in statistical programming and data analysis

• Additional duties and responsibilities as required

What You Bring

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in statistics, life sciences, computer science, or related field with at least 8 years’ statistical programming experience

• Solid understanding of industry standards applicable to clinical study data and regulatory reporting requirements including eCTD and CDISC implementation

• Expert level expertise in SAS programming (Base, Macro, STAT, GRAPH, SQL) is essential; with experience delivering complex programming assignments, macros, and analyses

• Experience with R and Python

• Extensive experience in early-phase clinical studies including programming and validation of SDTM and ADaM data sets, tables, listings and figures

• Experience managing CROs for outsourced statistical programming activities

• Expertise in the requirements and technology to support electronic submissions

• Experience in oncology preferred

• Experience with BLA or NDA/sNDA submissions to FDA/EMA required

• Strong analytical and communication skills

jobs.description:
Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures.

Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard.

We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good.

Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Role Summary

This position is part of the Life & Annuity Solutions team, which is responsible for designing, implementing, and managing our life and annuity products. The team is at the forefront of delivering innovative solutions that enhance customer experience and drive business growth.

This role performs actuarial and business analyst functions within the company’s illustration, policy administration and ancillary systems for life and annuity products and riders, resolving diverse issues creatively using analytical and problem-solving techniques to assess and identify causes.

A successful candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, ensuring accuracy through rigorous testing while balancing multiple priorities with adaptability, exceptional attention to detail, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. More than just a business analyst position, this role offers the opportunity to shape the future of life and annuity solutions. It involves cross-functional collaboration and meaningful contributions to the company’s mission of delivering on its promises.  If you're driven by innovation and impact, this could be the perfect fit.

This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you will be in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days.  Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.  The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Responsible for assigned aspects of the setup and maintenance of Life and Annuity products, ensuring accuracy across administration, illustration, and ancillary systems. This role defines products in systems, validates values, and loads rates while also performing systems analysis and building testing tools to ensure all life and annuity product calculations are complete and accurate. Working collaboratively with Agile scrum teams, the illustration team, and product development actuaries, this role optimizes product implementation and ensures accurate system integration.

To accomplish this, the role involves the following responsibilities:

Responsibilities include:

• Analyze assigned product changes to identify potential system modifications, collaborating with Senior Actuarial Systems Analyst, Principal Actuarial Systems Analyst, or manager to confirm the required changes, and develop business requirements for assigned system changes, as applicable.

• Continue developing knowledge of NLG’s life and annuity products, benefit structures, calculations, and systems, applying product and business context when making implementation and testing decisions appropriate to the scope of assigned work.

• Develop and refine test strategies, validation approaches, and test tools used to validate product rates, calculations, values, and system behavior, following established protocols, and raising potential improvements or alternative approaches for review with a Senior or Principal Actuarial Systems Analyst.

• Create and maintain tools and applications that support accurate implementation, administration, validation, and ongoing support of life and annuity products that can be understood and maintained by others.

• Develop and maintain system-based rule configurations to accurately reflect product features in administrative and illustration environments.

• Provide product and policy analysis and work collaboratively with other business areas to support accurate contract administration, considering downstream impacts of implementation and systems decisions.

• Provide guidance and training to Associate Actuarial Systems Analysts as appropriate, sharing product, systems, testing, and technical knowledge.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 3-5 years experience in systems or systems support, product implementation or related role in financial services industry.

• Basic understanding of life and annuity product mechanics.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively, build effective relationships, and manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

• Strong mathematical, analytical, problem-solving, verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong proficiency in MS Office suite of applications including very strong Excel skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Computer Science, Finance or related field.

• Experience with life insurance and/or annuity products with a demonstrated understanding of relevant product mechanics and calculations, such as UL, IUL, whole life cash value and death benefit calculations, definition of life insurance and modified endowment calculations, interest theory, and other related actuarial product benefit calculations.

• Familiarity with administration or illustration systems for life insurance and/or annuity products.

At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength.

• Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work.

• Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working.

• Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content and results.

• Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products, including work created or supported through AI.

• Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies and guiding principles related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property.

Core Competencies

Service Focus - Demonstrates a client centric focus for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect.

Decision Making - Makes sense of complex information, critically evaluates, and creates solutions.

Results Oriented - Sets performance and personal goals; Driven to meet or exceed goals and objectives.

Plans and Aligns - Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals; Aligns people and skills to tasks and assignments; Evaluates results of work.

Demonstrates Learning Agility - Enhances skills and knowledge through continuous learning; Focuses on personal results by establishing stretch goals; Seeks feedback and changes accordingly.

Establishes Relationships - Builds partnerships with others to instill trust, collaborate, and meet shared objectives.

Communicates Effectively - Actively listens, conveys messages to meet different audience needs, and remains open to new ideas and opinions.

Fosters Diversity - Values diversity and difference in thought, experience, and perspective; Promotes an environment that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion; Supports equal and fair treatment for all.

Benefits

The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in National Life’s discretionary annual incentive programs, subject to the rules governing such programs. Electrical Assembly Supervisor

Crane Electrical Assembly, Wiring & Testing

Location: Houston, Texas

Company: Konecranes

Position Summary

Konecranes is seeking a results-oriented Electrical Assembly Supervisors to lead electrical installation, wiring, troubleshooting, testing, and commissioning activities associated with custom Engineered-to-Order overhead cranes.

This position is responsible for ensuring electrical systems are installed and tested safely, correctly, and efficiently while maintaining the highest standards of quality and workmanship. The Electrical Assembly Foreman provides direct leadership to electrical assembly personnel and drives accountability for safety, quality, productivity, and schedule adherence.

This role is critical in ensuring cranes are fully functional, tested, and prepared for shipment and field installation.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

• Lead and direct electrical assemblers, technicians, and wiring personnel.
• Establish a culture of accountability, urgency, and execution.
• Coach employees to achieve performance and quality objectives.
• Address performance issues promptly and constructively.
• Foster strong teamwork across assembly, engineering, quality, and project management groups.

Production Management

• Oversee electrical installation and wiring operations.
• Coordinate manpower and resources to support production schedules.
• Monitor progress and resolve technical and operational issues.
• Ensure equipment is wired and configured according to engineering requirements.
• Coordinate testing and commissioning activities.

Quality & Technical Standards

• Ensure all electrical installations, wiring methods, control panels, and equipment assemblies comply with applicable NEC, UL, customer, and project-specific code requirements.
• Support equipment designs and assembly processes that meet CSA requirements for cranes destined for Canadian service.
• Ensure electrical installations comply with engineering drawings, schematics, and customer specifications.
• Maintain compliance with Konecranes workmanship standards.
• Verify testing, inspection, and documentation requirements are completed.
• Drive first-pass quality and reduce troubleshooting and rework.
• Ensure equipment is fully functional before shipment.

Testing & Commissioning

• Oversee functional testing of completed crane systems.
• Support troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of electrical issues.
• Coordinate resolution of deficiencies identified during testing.
• Verify readiness for shipment and field installation.

Safety Leadership

• Lead and promote a strong safety culture.
• Ensure compliance with electrical safety requirements and company procedures.
• Conduct regular safety reviews and corrective actions.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and efficient work environment.

*This position will be located on the factory floor

Desired Qualifications

• Thorough knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and its application to industrial control panels, motor controls, crane systems, and manufacturing equipment.
• Familiarity with Canadian Standards Association (CSA) electrical requirements, C22.1 Canadian Electrical Code, and customer-specific Canadian compliance requirements preferred.
• Experience interpreting electrical schematics, control drawings, and code requirements to ensure compliant installations.
• Knowledge of UL, NEC, CSA, and industrial electrical safety standards applicable to overhead crane manufacturing and testing.
• Experience leading electrical assembly, industrial controls, wiring, commissioning, or manufacturing operations.
• Strong leadership and communication skills.
• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
• Experience managing production schedules and workforce performance.
• Knowledge of motor controls, VFDs, PLCs, industrial wiring, and crane systems preferred.
• Demonstrated commitment to safety and quality.

What Success Looks Like

• Safe execution of electrical installation and testing activities.
• Consistent achievement of production schedules.
• High first-pass test completion rates.
• Reduced troubleshooting and rework.
• Strong employee engagement and accountability.
• Reliable delivery of fully tested crane systems ready for shipment.

What we offer:

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

We consistently set the industry benchmark, from everyday improvements to the breakthroughs at moments that matter most, because we know we can always find a safer, more productive and sustainable way. That's why, with 16 000+ professionals in over 50 countries, we are trusted every day to lift, handle and move what the world needs.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (AI Agents)
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRABA

 

Traba is building the AI operating layer for the industrial supply chain.

 

We started in the workforce space because contingent labor is the biggest operational pain point our manufacturing and logistics customers face. We used it to embed ourselves inside their daily operations and create a far better customer experience through technology. Now those same customers are pulling us beyond staffing into the broader operational workflows that run their facilities. That foundation gave us proprietary data from millions of shifts and deep enterprise relationships.

 

But our edge is more than data. By connecting to the systems running across every facility and activating the workers already on our platform to execute against them, we are building applied AI that drives real productivity gains and transforms how the global supply chain operates at scale.

 

We are backed by Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst.

 


THE ROLE

 

We are looking for an entrepreneurial and experienced Product Manager to join as a founding member of the Agents team and help us build the next layer of Traba's product, an agentic platform that synthesizes the data flowing through our marketplace and operates autonomously inside our customers' supply chain workflows. Think Claude, but for Light Industrial businesses.

 

You'll embed deeply in our customers' operations, design and ship production agents that understand context, reason through ambiguity, make decisions, and execute work on behalf of users. This is a true 0-to-1 product role operating at the frontier of applied AI.

 

You will work directly with founders, product engineers, ML teams, and early design partners to define workflows, shape product strategy, and build products while the underlying model ecosystem continues changing beneath us. The assumptions, capabilities, and constraints will evolve rapidly and the product will evolve with them.

 

This role reports directly to our VP of Product.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Architect and steward product strategy for Traba’s AI agent platform

 - Solve complex customer problems by balancing user needs, technical constraints, and evolving AI capabilities

 - Write detailed product requirements and partner deeply with product engineers and ML teams

 - Rapidly validate and prototype ideas alongside customers and design partners

 - Design agent systems that reason through workflows, orchestrate tools, maintain context, and execute meaningful work

 - Define product behavior, evaluation systems, and quality frameworks that improve reliability and performance

 - Use data to uncover patterns and answer key product and system questions

 - Evolve our AI product portfolio with a deep understanding of model capabilities and system architecture

 - Visualize and communicate complex concepts from system behavior and evaluations to user experiences and business impact

 - Socialize your work across all levels and departments while synthesizing diverse stakeholder feedback

 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

Real agent builder. You have launched customer-facing AI products where the system took meaningful actions on behalf of users. We are intentionally setting a high bar here. Shipping AI features, copilots, chat interfaces, wrappers, or lightweight LLM integrations alone is not enough. You understand agents that execute workflows, orchestrate systems, use tools, maintain context, and perform work autonomously.

0-to-1 operator. You have built products from scratch with real customers and understand the realities of finding product market fit. You have launched, rebuilt, changed direction, killed ideas, and iterated toward signals. You are comfortable creating structures where no playbook exists.

AI-native problem solver. You move quickly in environments where models evolve constantly and assumptions regularly break. You understand that building AI products often means navigating prompt rewrites, model shifts, reliability tradeoffs, and capability cliffs.

First-principles thinker. You spend equal time thinking about why, how, and what. You understand that strong product judgment often comes from deeply understanding systems and constraints rather than applying generic playbooks.

Customer-embedded builder. You believe the best products are built shoulder-to-shoulder with customers. You have experience deeply embedding with early customers, understanding workflows firsthand, and rapidly shipping based on direct feedback loops. Experience with forward deployed environments or customer-embedded product development models is highly valued.

Technical depth. You are comfortable operating alongside ML engineers and highly technical teams as peers. You can understand evaluations, reason through system tradeoffs, prototype ideas, and participate deeply in technical conversations. You do not need to be an ex-engineer, but you should have strong technical instincts and enjoy getting into the details.

Builder mentality. Inventive and scrappy problem solver. You move quickly, embrace ambiguity, and know how to create meaningful outcomes without relying on giant teams or excessive process.

Deeply collaborative. You work seamlessly across engineering, ML, operations, design, leadership, and customers to bring new products to life.

 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 

 - 5 – 7 years of experience as a Product Manager

 - Evidence of launching products from scratch and driving meaningful customer outcomes

 - Experience building AI-native products or customer-facing agent systems

 - Strong technical abilities with the ability to work deeply with engineering and ML teams

 - Ability to read evaluations, reason through system performance, and prototype ideas

 - Experience operating in highly ambiguous startup environments with fast iteration cycles

 - Deep familiarity with AI tools and hands-on experience building with modern AI systems

 - Desire to work at a startup and cover an exceptionally wide surface area

 - A strong work ethic and desire to build a category-defining company

 


BENEFITS

 

 - 📈 Start-up equity

 - 💰 Competitive Salary

 - 🩺 100% Paid health, dental & vision coverage

 - 🍽️ Dinner Provided via Grubhub & stocked kitchen for NY employees

 - 🚍 Commuter benefit

 - 🎤 Team building events

 - 🏋🏽 Gympass Benefit

 - 🌴 Flexible PTO

 - ✚✚ Additional: One Medical Membership, Gympass, HSA via Optum, Talkspace, Health Advocate, Teledoc Health

 


SALARY RANGE DETAILS

 

The compensation range for this position is set between $180,000 and $210,000, reflecting our market analysis and other relevant considerations. However, exceptions may be made for candidates with qualifications that significantly differ from those outlined in the job description.We also offer a highly competitive equity package designed to ensure you share meaningfully in the long-term success and upside of the business.

The position is based onsite in New York City or San Francisco, five days per week, giving you the opportunity to collaborate closely with a high-performing team in a fast-paced, energetic environment. Being in person supports real-time decision-making, stronger teamwork, and the kind of creative problem-solving that drives meaningful impact.

 


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

 

Traba is dedicated to promoting Equal Opportunity employment practices. We evaluate all applicants without discrimination based on race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, gender, marital status, sexual orientation and identity, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other characteristics that are legally protected by local, state, or federal regulations. We encourage applicants from a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skill sets.

 


OUR VALUES

 

Dream Big - We are on a path to change the world for the better. We create and communicate a bold direction that inspires a life-changing vision. We don’t sacrifice long-term value for short-term results.

Olympian’s Work Ethic - Changing the world never comes easy. We work harder, longer, and smarter, not just two out of three. We put everything we have on the field.

Growth Mindset - We confront the toughest challenges head-on and persevere. Sometimes we fail, but we brush ourselves off, adapt, learn, and push forward with resilience.

Customer Obsession - We go the extra mile for our workers and businesses. We remain focused on delivering high-quality products and services that solve this massive and overlooked industries’ problems

jobs.title: ESI Director, Suitability
jobs.description:
Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures.

Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard.

We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good.

Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Role Summary

This position is responsible for the suitability review and approval of broker-dealer and investment adviser accounts and transactions. The role analyzes complex securities transactions and handles discussions with the field on escalated transactions.

Working closely with the Registered Representatives of Equity Services, Inc. (ESI), this position reviews new business and subsequent transactions across annuities, mutual funds, 529s, and advisory business. The role also delivers suitability training, drafts field communications, and drives process improvements through to implementation.

The ideal candidate brings agility, strong knowledge of securities product features and regulatory requirements, business acumen, and courage, along with excellent communication skills and a commitment to lifelong learning.

This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you will be in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days.  Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.  The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Provide superior service to the Registered Representatives of ESI and their clients.

• Review new business cases and subsequent transactions promptly and accurately, including annuities, mutual funds, 529s, and advisory business.

• Conduct in-depth case reviews and documentation within established time constraints.

• Analyze complex securities transactions and handle discussions with the field on escalated transactions.

• Deliver effective solutions when handling sensitive situations related to case review.

• Systematically review and approve the daily Trade Blotter and similar reports.

• Conduct post-transaction follow-up to help resolve outstanding items.

• Provide quality internal and external support to make it easier to do business.

• Deliver presentations and suitability training internally and externally as needed.

• Identify process improvements and see them through to implementation.

• Draft field communications.

• All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree.

• 10 years of financial services experience.

• 8 or more years of experience conducting suitability reviews of broker-dealer and advisory business.

• FINRA Series 7 and 24 licenses.

• Strong knowledge of annuity products.

• Strong background in customer service, with the ability to handle difficult conversations.

• Complex problem solver who can thrive amid ambiguity.

• Ability to think independently and tactfully challenge the opinions of others.

• Demonstrated ability to perform quality work in a fast-paced environment and to work well as a team player with individuals at all levels of the organization.

• Superb interpersonal, time management, communication, and organizational skills.

• Ability to pass a background and fingerprint check.

Preferred Qualifications

• FINRA Series 53

AI Proficiency Expectations:

At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength.

All applicants are expected to:

• Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work.

• Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working.

• Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content.

• Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles.

• Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property.

Core Competencies

Cultivates Innovation - Fosters innovation by taking calculated risks; Work cooperatively with others to produce innovative solutions.

Ensures Accountability - Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments and performance goals.

Directs Work - Provides direction, delegates, and removes obstacles to get work done.

Demonstrates Emotional Intelligence - Exhibits the ability to recognize, understand, and manage emotions and how emotions can influence others; Uses a combination of feedback and reflection to gain productive insight into personal strengths and opportunities.

Exhibits Critical and Creative Thinking - Engaging thinking skills that focus on logic and reasoning to make decisions (critical) and innovative solutions to solve problems (creative).

Leads Change - Facilitates change and transition at the individual and team level; Develops strategic goals for aligning with change.

Develops Talent - Builds team(s) equipped for the future by applying coaching techniques for developing team members to meet their professional/personal goals and the organizational goals; Listens and responds with empathy; Asks thought provoking questions.

Inspires Others - Motivates and influences others by creating an environment where teams can do their best work; Partners across the organization to achieve results.

Benefits

• Your benefits start day one and are flexible and customizable to your and your family’s specific needs. Check out the BENEFITS of a Career at National Life!

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist-Inpatient Oncology Operations, Full-time Rotating
jobs.description:
The Clinical Pharmacist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADCs) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Licensure:

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)

Preferred:

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

Artificial Intelligence Disclosure

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all employment decisions will be made by a person.

We offer a wide range of benefits that provide employees with tools and resources to improve their physical, emotional, and financial well-being while providing protection for unexpected life events.
