Primary Function of Position

At Intuitive, the needs of our customers are a key driver in our approach to service innovation. Within Global Services Product Management, we build deep understanding of customer needs by working closely with them to assess strengths and opportunities. We incorporate these insights into our Global Service offerings, capabilities, and digital service solutions.

The Product Manager, Global Service Offerings will play a role in Global Services innovation by defining and executing Global Service offering strategy, pricing, portfolio alignment, market research, performance analytics, and commercialization. This role will focus on the day-to-day execution and evolution of our global service offering strategy, ensuring offerings deliver measurable value for customers while supporting company growth objectives. This role will partner across regions and functions—working with Service Operations, Sales, Marketing, Contracts, Finance, and Product—to design, launch, and optimize service offerings that align with customer needs, improve outcomes, and complement our medical device portfolio.

This is a high-visibility role and directly influences recurring revenue, customer satisfaction, and the long-term success of our service business. The Product Manager will develop solution roadmaps and continuously iterate on those roadmaps based on user feedback, emerging customer and service team needs, and business objectives.

Responsibilities for this role include both upstream and downstream activities. Upstream, the Product Manager will create proposals to enhance or develop new service capabilities, draft business cases to support those proposals, and define requirements for delivery. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Architect the robot operating system. Design the core abstractions: how robots, cameras, tools and jobs are modelled, how work is planned and dispatched, how state is shared and how failures are handled. Decide what belongs in Python and what needs Rust.

 - Bring in new vision. Integrate novel computer vision algorithms into the control loop, from finding and centring parts to checking every pick and placement, and make them fast and reliable enough for production.

 - Build agentic robotics. Put large models to work in the robots themselves: programming a new part from its datasheet, judging a pick from a camera image, diagnosing a fault and recovering from it, with evals that prove it works before it runs alone.

 - Move a fleet. Route dozens of movers at once without collisions or deadlocks, and coordinate gantries, printers and ovens around them.

 - Bridge to real time. Design clean interfaces between high-level planning and the real-time controllers driving the motors.

 - Make it observable. Simulation, tracing and replay, so every change is proven before it reaches the factory and every failure can be explained.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've worked on, and ideally architected, a large-scale robot code base that ran on real hardware in production.

 - Strong software engineering in Python and Rust (or C++ and a willingness to move to Rust). You care about types, testing, concurrency and clear architecture.

 - Experience with some of: motion or path planning, multi-robot coordination, controls, perception, scheduling.

 - Hands-on experience applying large models (LLMs or vision-language models) to robotics, or a strong drive to.

 - You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

 - You're happy to visit our factories in the US and UK to see your code run.


STACK

 - Robot software: Python and Rust

 - Vision and models: OpenCV, PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, Claude and OpenAI APIs

 - Planning: multi-agent path-finding, OR-Tools

 - Data and observability: PostgreSQL, OpenTelemetry, ClickHouse

 - Agents: Claude Code and Codex throughout


PAY

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

jobs.title: Senior HRIS Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.



THE ROLE

This role is at the heart of building and running the HR platform that powers Legora's global People operations. You'll join at a pivotal moment for the company, bringing hands-on expertise to help us get the foundations right as we scale. You'll work closely with external partners and internal teams to design, configure, test and release a platform that supports our growing global workforce. You'll make sure it stays reliable, secure and continuously improving as the business grows.

This is a hands-on role for someone who has built and run an enterprise HRIS and knows what it takes to make a platform work in practice, not just on paper. You'll combine technical expertise with an understanding of People processes, working closely with stakeholders to turn business requirements into effective system solutions.


What you'll own

 - Platform design and build. Work with our external partners on solution design, configuration, testing and release. Bring practical experience to challenge design decisions and ensure we're building a platform that will work for Legora long term.

 - Workstream delivery. Own defined sub-streams of our HRIS implementation from requirements to release. Run discovery with stakeholders, document requirements and design decisions, and manage your own plan, risks and dependencies

 - Platform configuration & administration. Configure, maintain and optimize our HRIS, including business processes, organisational structures, security, approvals and employee lifecycle transactions.

 - Requirements gathering. Run workshops with People, Finance, IT and business stakeholders to understand how processes work today and how they need to work at scale.

 - Translate People requirements into effective system configurations and workflows. Partner with functional experts to simplify processes, standardise where possible and build solutions that scale across our global footprint.

 - Data integrity. Support data mapping, validation and reconciliation across our People systems. Establish system controls and quality checks, working with People Operations and other data owners to maintain accurate, reliable employee data.

 - Testing & release management. Own functional testing for system changes, coordinate user acceptance testing and support ongoing releases. Assess downstream impacts, maintain documentation and ensure changes are deployed safely.

 - Platform support & optimisation. Troubleshoot issues, investigate root causes and support users. Identify opportunities to improve workflows, increase self-service adoption and reduce manual intervention.


What you'll bring

 - 4+ years of hands-on experience with an enterprise HRIS, including platform support, configuration, testing, data work and releases.

 - Experience gathering and documenting requirements for HR system changes, and turning them into configuration and test plans.

 - Strong Core HCM knowledge, including business processes, organisational structures, security and reporting.

 - A strong understanding of employee lifecycle processes and how they operate across a global organisation. Experience translating HR requirements into system configurations and workflows.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a high bar for data accuracy, system reliability and documentation.

 - The ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, explaining complex system concepts clearly. Track record of owning a workstream within a larger project or change programme.

 - A proactive, hands-on mindset. You're comfortable getting into the details, challenging assumptions and taking ownership of problems through to resolution.

 - Nice to have*:* experience with integrations between an HRIS and other systems, such as payroll, ATS, IT provisioning or finance. This could be defining requirements, mapping data, testing, or troubleshooting failed syncs.

 - Fluency in English, which is our working language.


Why this role

People technology is foundational to how Legora scales. We're building the infrastructure that will support thousands of employees across an increasingly complex global footprint, and this role will shape how that infrastructure works for years to come.

You'll help us make the right design decisions, build a strong technical foundation and establish how we manage and improve our People systems over time. This is an opportunity to take ownership of a global platform in a fast-growing AI company, where your work will directly improve how employees, managers and the People team get things done.

What’s In It For You

 - Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America.

 - Meaningful work: Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily.

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Strategic Connectivity Manager (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

STRATEGIC CONNECTIVITY MANAGER (STARLINK)

Starlink, our revolutionary satellite constellation, is delivering low-latency broadband internet around the world. In addition to the current use cases Starlink is serving in masse – such as residential, maritime, aviation, fixed site enterprise – there are many other uses cases and applications for Starlink that help social and economic development that require development or modification of existing capabilities and thinking. Examples include serving anchor institutions (schools, clinics, libraries, community centers, etc.), refugee camps, securing development bank funding, and supporting unique philanthropic efforts.

The Strategic Connectivity Projects team is charged with identifying and enabling these projects by assessing the potential positive impact of projects, thinking creatively, applying excellent business judgement, and having a bias for action.

We are searching for someone to apply additional focus to these projects in the APAC, Middle East, and Central Asia region =, to increase the pace of progress and scale the impact by orders of magnitude. Our ideal candidate is a self-starter that has a passion for expanding connectivity access, building excellent teams, sharing the stories of how Starlink can positively impact social and economic development, and managing complex cross-functional projects.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Scale the use of Starlink in projects that have significant positive social and economic impact around the world

• Develop and execute strategies that align with Starlink business goals as well as team-specific goals

• Manage and grow capabilities to enable embracing projects of all sizes

• Select, establish, and maintain key relationships that align with the strategy and mission, such as influential individuals, philanthropic entities, non-governmental organizations, and development banks

• Measure and report progress towards goals, establishing new tracking methods if required

• Maintain a strong grasp of standard Starlink product offerings and business processes

• Apply excellent business judgement on if, when, and how to deviate

• Ensure Starlink products, processes and capabilities develop with social and economic development project use cases in mind by identifying and justifying necessary changes or deviations

• Identify and work collaboratively with key internal partners such as market access, global operations, growth, sales, legal, finance, account management, and communications

• Work with communications team to collect and share compelling messaging and stories about Starlink’s positive impact around the world

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or business fields

• 7+ years of experience in engineering or operations

• 2+ years of project management experience

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Ability to champion and lead significant cross-functional projects and business initiatives, including ability to manage in an environment with competing priorities and limited resources

• Exceptional external interface and public speaking skills, including excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Successful internal communicator within SpaceX that possesses the ability to tailor communications appropriately to level (working-level to executive-level)

• Excellent negotiation and conflict resolution skills

• Strong ability to determine what projects to pursue that have positive social and economic development potential as well as are smart business decisions

• Ability to navigate risk and ambiguity successfully

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be available to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to support critical milestones or operations shifts

• Must be willing to travel to other SpaceX offices and customer locations as needed (estimated need is 25% on average through the year, but there may be surges/concentrated periods)

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Level 3: $125,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Computer Vision
jobs.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Inspect boards. Improve automated optical inspection that finds missing, rotated and wrongly placed parts and bad solder, working alongside our AI agents.

 - Pick reliably. Train and deploy the models that find parts in bins and trays, centre them on the nozzle and catch a clumped or dropped pick.

 - Align precisely. Fiducial detection, calibration and image alignment for placements measured in fractions of a millimetre.

 - Build the data loop. Decide what to capture, build labelling tools, and turn operator verdicts into training data.

 - Go fast. Work with our high-speed cameras and GPU capture pipeline to move vision closer to real time.

 - Measure it. Track accuracy in production, find where errors come from, and prove every change against past results.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've shipped computer vision into production, beyond a notebook.

 - Strong software engineering in Python, C++ or a comparable language.

 - A mix of classical vision (geometry, calibration, template matching) and deep learning; you know when each is the right tool.

 - Experience with industrial or machine-vision cameras is a bonus.

 - You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

 - You like the physical world: lighting, lenses and parts rotated by 90°.


STACK

 - Vision: OpenCV, PyTorch and Lightning, ONNX Runtime on GPU, libtorch from Haskell

 - Cameras: Basler GigE cameras via pylon, high-speed cameras with GPUDirect capture

 - Services: Python and Haskell, PostgreSQL, Nix and NixOS


PAY

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

jobs.title: Head of Wholesale Underwriting
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO

Commercial insurance still runs on processes built decades ago. Underwriting is slow, and pricing leans on broad averages instead of the specifics of each risk. Technology can change how commercial risk is priced and managed, as long as it's paired with real underwriting expertise. The companies that get this right will shape the next era of the industry, and Shepherd intends to lead it.

Shepherd is a Managing General Underwriter (MGU) building the fastest and smartest AI-native commercial risk platform in the industry, where underwriters, data, and automation work together. The result is faster decisions for our broker partners and pricing that reflects the actual risk.

We started where the gap is widest: construction and energy, two of the most complex and highest-hazard segments in commercial insurance. Today we write Primary and Excess Casualty, Builder’s Risk, and Workers' Compensation distributed through a nationwide network of retail brokers. Our mission is to make risk frictionless for the builders and operators shaping the physical world, from concept through construction and into decades of operation.

 


🚀 OUR INVESTORS

Shepherd has raised over $67M, including a $42M Series B led by Intact Private Capital. Intact also partners with Shepherd to provide capacity across its insurance products. Shepherd is also backed by leading institutional investors, including Costanoa Ventures, Spark Capital, Susa Ventures, and Y Combinator.

 


🏗️ HEAD OF WHOLESALE UNDERWRITING

Shepherd is expanding its distribution and is launching a dedicated wholesale brand targeting E&S Property, Casualty and Financial Lines. The Head of Wholesale Underwriting will report to the Chief Insurance Officer and lead the development and execution of a newly-established, wholesale-exclusive insurance brand across multiple products and verticals.You http://verticals.You will set the wholesale distribution strategy, define the products and appetite, hire the product line leaders and help secure the Excess & Surplus (E&S) capacity behind the program. This is a unique opportunity to help define the underwriting, brand and distribution strategies for a newly-established business unit. We're looking for someone with 12+ years of wholesale E&S experience, a proven track record of leadership, deep broker relationships, and an entrepreneurial mindset who is excited to build something new with modern technology and a forward-thinking team.


🎯 ABOUT YOU

You are a builder who wants to shape the future of commercial insurance and do the best work of your career. You have deep wholesale expertise, a loyal broker network, and the drive to turn a blank page into a profitable book.

You'd be a great fit if you have:

 - 12+ years in the wholesale and E&S commercial P&C market, with leadership roles at a carrier, MGA/MGU, or wholesale specialty underwriting organization.

 - A proven record of building or significantly scaling a wholesale business, product line, or channel, with P&L ownership for premium, profit, and loss-ratio results.

 - Deep relationships with national and regional wholesale brokerage teams that can drive submission flow from day one.

 - Strong command of how E&S business and the wholesale channel dynamics work, including surplus lines regulation and compliance, wholesale producer agreements, BOR protections, commission structures, and open brokerage and binding authority models.

 - Experience leading, mentoring, or managing underwriters, including setting authority and running underwriting audits.

 - Executive presence to present strategy and results to leadership, capacity partners, and reinsurers.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound decisions with incomplete information and adapt quickly as the business evolves.

 - Willingness to travel about 25% to meet brokers, partners, and the team.

 - A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. A background in construction accounting, finance, or law is a plus.


💼 ABOUT THE ROLE

Shepherd's underwriting approach is broker and client-centric with a heavy emphasis on an efficient process. Our goal is to leverage our technology and data to make quick, informed underwriting decisions tailored to our brokers' specific needs.

In this role, you will:

 - Launch Shepherd's new wholesale business and brand.

 - Define the wholesale strategy, including target products and classes, E&S appetite, broker partners, and growth and loss-ratio targets by line of business.

 - Work with Underwriting leadership to establish wholesale-exclusive classes and design new E&S products where the opportunity is greatest.

 - Hire product underwriting leaders and support the development of the underwriting guidelines, authority frameworks, referral rules, rating approach, and forms for the respective wholesale / E&S lines of business.

 - Structure a focused distribution strategy with our wholesale broker partners by product line, helping to onboard wholesale broker partners, setting producer and market partner agreements, and building Shepherd's reputation as a go-to market for wholesale brokers.

 - Work with capacity and reinsurance partners to secure and structure the E&S paper behind the program, and keep those partners informed on results.

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data to design a wholesale submission-to-bind workflow to create a frictionless experience for our wholesale partners for each product.

 - Own premium, profit, loss-ratio, retention, and expense results for the wholesale business.

 - Hire, coach, and grow a team of wholesale product line leaders, underwriters, distribution leaders, and support staff as the business scales.

 - Work with Corporate Underwriting to help set letters of authority, run underwriting audits, and coach from the results.

 - Work with Claims, Actuarial, Customer Experience and Finance so the business is underwritten, serviced, and reported well.

This is a position based in New York City, San Francisco, Chicago, Atlanta, Boston, Los Angeles, or Dallas–Fort Worth.


💰 COMPENSATION

The base salary range for this role is $350,000 – $425,000, plus an annual performance bonus and equity in Shepherd. Offers within the range depend on experience and the relationships and market following you bring.


⚡ HOW WE WORK

Shepherd runs on four values. Here's what each one means in this seat.

 - 🚀 Think big, build big. We exist to protect progress and the industries that rely on it. You're building a wholesale business meant to scale nationally, so the products, partnerships, team, and tools get designed for where the channel is going, not just where it starts.

 - 🤝 Win together. We rise as one. We support each other, raise the bar, and celebrate collective success. As the first leader of our wholesale arm, you set the standard for every wholesale underwriter and broker partner who follows, and you build it hand in hand with our retail team.

 - 🔄 Cross the aisle. Collaboration wins. We listen deeply, work across boundaries, and prioritize shared success over individual lanes. The best underwriting tools here come from underwriters who sit with engineers and data scientists, and much of this job is making that partnership work.

 - 🔥 Go get it. We act with urgency, move with confidence, take smart risks, and push forward with intention. Nobody hands you the broker list, the appetite, or the first submission. You build the plan, open the doors, and bind the first deal.

jobs.title: Head of Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
Steer offers a suite of software tools for today's automotive repair shop. We combine a mix of software tools that a repair shop needs to run a highly profitable shop, in one user-friendly, cost-effective platform. Through the Steer suite, we allow the shop owner to get back to focusing on what matters, and to stop worrying about marketing and customer retention.

Steer began as an online directory for drivers to find a local mechanic. Fast forward to today, Steer has launched a complete Customer Relationship Management (CRM) marketing suite, complete with text messaging, email automation, direct mail integration, reputation management, appointment reminders, declined/recommended services, and many other features. We are always innovating and we are proud to be a leader in the automotive repair industry.  In August 2024 Steer acquired AutoOps - the leader in modern, intelligent, and fully integrated scheduling software for auto repair shops. AutoOps allows customers to smoothly schedule through a shop's website and Google Business Profile.

About the Role

As Head of Revenue Operations, you will build, optimize, and scale the operational, data, and technology foundation across our entire go-to-market organization—including Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, and Partnerships. Reporting directly to executive leadership, your mission is to transform our systems, billing infrastructure, reporting, and GTM strategy into a clear, high-performing growth engine.

You will lead a small but high-impact RevOps team (2 direct reports) while personally owning the architecture and execution of our RevTech stack (including HubSpot and Chargebee), lead management, funnel optimization, enablement and ramp, and AI deployment. This is not a traditional admin role—we are looking for a builder, strategic systems architect, and AI-forward operator who rationalizes existing tools before adding new ones, replaces manual reporting with automated signal, and shortens new-hire time-to-productivity as a core business metric.

This role is 100% remote and available to US-based candidates.

You Are

• An Operational Builder & AI-Forward Architect: Highly organized and system-minded, you thrive on taking complex, disconnected processes and building simple, scalable workflows. You actively identify, test, and deploy AI tools and automated knowledge systems to eliminate manual work and boost team productivity.

• A Strategic Systems Thinker: You look beyond basic CRM administration to understand broader business goals, connecting executive priorities to billing infrastructure, tech stack rationalization, and RevOps strategy.

• A Hands-On Problem Solver: You balance executive strategy with technical execution—equally comfortable presenting to leadership or personally building automations, forecasting models, and CRM workflows.

• A Growth & Ramp Driver: You view new-hire time-to-productivity as a business metric, using automated measurement, early success signals, and modern systems to ramp revenue teams faster.

• A Collaborative Leader: You manage, mentor, and elevate a team of RevOps professionals while bridging the gap between technical data systems and business leadership to align GTM operations.

You Will

• Own Revenue Systems, Billing Infrastructure & AI Innovation: Lead full ownership and architecture of core revenue systems (HubSpot, Chargebee, and broader RevTech). Continuously inspect, consolidate, and optimize current platforms before evaluating new spend. Build advanced automation workflows across Marketing, Sales, CS, Finance, and Partnerships, and deploy AI tools (such as living AI knowledge bases/Claude skills libraries) to streamline operations.

• Drive Enablement, Ramp & Team Productivity: Own new-hire ramp time with a clear, measurable path to reduction. Design onboarding, coaching, and exception-based reporting workflows that run through systems rather than headcount. Partner with Sales leadership on structural changes (comp design, team placement) that raise pipeline productivity per rep.

• Optimize Funnel Performance & Revenue Intelligence: Diagnose pipeline leaks and conversion bottlenecks across all channels. Build executive dashboards, forecasting models, and predictive analytics to improve speed-to-lead, decision-maker contact rates, expansion efficiency, and retention outcomes. Ground all recommendations in data first.

• Lead Data Strategy & Governance: Define how data is captured, structured, and managed across the customer lifecycle, improving CRM hygiene, billing accuracy, reporting integrity, and system interoperability.

• Manage & Develop the RevOps Team: Lead, hire, and mentor 2 direct reports. Build a culture of innovation, systems thinking, accountability, and technical excellence, raising team competency across AI, automation, and systems architecture.

• Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate closely with Sales, Marketing, CS, Finance, Product, and Executive Leadership to support product-led growth (PLG) motions, upgrade paths, monetization strategies, and long-term GTM infrastructure.

You Have

Must Have

• RevOps Leadership Experience: 5–8+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, GTM Systems, or Revenue Enablement, with proven experience leading teams or major strategic initiatives.

• Systems & Tech Stack Mastery: Deep expertise configuring and managing HubSpot, along with strong experience in billing/subscription management platforms (Chargebee or similar) and operational architecture.

• AI & Automation Curiosity: Hands-on track record implementing modern automation tools and proactive experience deploying AI solutions (including AI-powered knowledge or enablement systems).

• Enablement & Ramp Ownership: Experience owning, measuring, or influencing new-hire ramp time and onboarding outcomes as core operational metrics.

• Data & Analytics Proficiency: Strong analytical background with direct experience querying raw data, building forecasting models, and designing board-level/executive dashboards (SQL, BI tools, or advanced analytics platforms).

• Stack Rationalization Skills: Proven track record evaluating, consolidating, or replacing major GTM and business software platforms.

Nice to Have

• Billing Operations: Direct experience with Chargebee, subscription management, and revenue recognition workflows.

• Product-Led Growth (PLG): Experience supporting PLG motions, automated upgrade paths, and expansion loops.

• Early-Stage / High-Growth Scaling: Experience scaling a RevOps function in a fast-growing SaaS tech company.

• Multi-Segment GTM: Background supporting multi-segment environments (SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise).

• Marketing Attribution & Demand Gen: Deep understanding of marketing attribution models and demand generation tech stacks.

Interview Process

• Initial Screen: 30 min with the Lead Recruiter

• Hiring Manager Interview: 45 min with the CRO

• Problem Solving Interview & Executive interview : 60 min with the Director of People & 45 min with the CEO

• Case Study Presentation: 60 min with the CRO & CFO

We Offer

• 100% remote work environment

• Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance within 30 days (100% employer-paid medical)

• Equity package

• Flexible PTO with a 15-day minimum

• Generous Parental Leave

• FSA and HSA options

• 401(k)

• Growth & Wellness Stipend

• WFH Equipment stipend

• Chance to work with the latest technology and AI tools

• A collaborative, high-ownership culture with clear opportunities for career growth

Why Join Steer?

At Steer, we align our mission of transforming the auto repair experience for shop owners and their customers with your passion for growth, innovation, and excellence.

Here, you’ll find opportunities to expand your skills, take on career-shaping challenges, and contribute to the future of the auto repair industry, all while enjoying comprehensive benefits and flexible work arrangements to support your well-being.

Join Steer to be part of a forward-thinking, flexible, and collaborative culture where you are empowered to do meaningful and impactful work.

We value diversity and believe that forming teams in which everyone can be their authentic self is key to our success. We welcome applications from those with diverse backgrounds and industries.

Our hiring process looks beyond just credentials. The school you went to at 18 doesn't define your potential to thrive and enrich our culture. Even if you don't meet every requirement, we invite you to apply.

jobs.title: Data Mining Sr. Analyst
jobs.description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

Machinify is seeking a Senior Analyst to lead the development and refinement of new reimbursement and payment integrity concepts. This is a hands-on healthcare domain role, not a technical or engineering position. The ideal candidate understands reimbursement logic, payment policies, and provider contracts in depth — and can translate that expertise into clear, structured concepts that inform analytics and automation efforts.

You will be focused on discovering where and why payment errors occur, designing methods to detect and prevent them, and partnering with technical teams to operationalize your findings. This role is ideal for someone who loves digging into claims data, identifying systemic payment issues, and shaping how technology solutions capture real-world reimbursement logic.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead pre and post-pay claim reviews to identify inaccurate payments using reimbursement and contract expertise.

• Analyze and interpret provider contracts to ensure payments align with negotiated terms, methodologies, and payer rules.

• Collaborate closely with engineering and data science teams to translate business and reimbursement logic into analytical and automation frameworks.

• Research and document emerging reimbursement and contract patterns, coverage rules, and billing practices to inform concept development.

• Translate complex reimbursement and contract scenarios into structured rules and business logic for implementation.

• Analyze claim-level data to pinpoint root causes of overpayments or incorrect denials and recommend corrective approaches.

• Maintain expertise on CMS and commercial payer reimbursement guidelines.

jobs.description:
Company Description

About Walden University Walden University, a Covista institution, supports a diverse community of adult learners from across the U.S. and other countries, who seek to achieve their academic goals and make positive, lasting social impact in their professions and communities. Walden offers more than 100 online degree and certificate programs, for students pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, doctoral or certificate. Walden University has graduated more than 174,000 students and is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

Visit WaldenU.edu for more information, and follow on Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn.

Walden University is a pioneer in student-centered distance education. An accredited graduate institution with a mission for social change, Walden is dedicated to high academic standards and helping students make a difference in their professions, organizations, and communities. Walden University offers advanced degrees online to professionals whose work impacts others.

Walden's Ph.D. in Management, DBA, MBA, and BSBA degree programs are accredited by the Accreditation Council for Business Schools and Programs (ACBSP), a leading specialized accreditation association that identifies and supports excellence in business education.

Job Description

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) Adjunct faculty members’ primary responsibility will be teaching and mentoring capstone students. Faculty must demonstrate a commitment to actively support the learning and development needs of students earning their degrees in a distance learning environment.

Walden faculty must have a commitment to fostering Walden’s Community of Care.

• Student-centered engagement and support — Faculty are expected to communicate regularly, provide timely guidance, support students individually, and connect them with appropriate resources.
• Academic expertise and quality feedback — Faculty should demonstrate strong knowledge of university systems, policies, research processes, rubrics, and program expectations while giving constructive, detailed feedback.
• Empathy balanced with accountability — Faculty should meet students where they are, show flexibility when appropriate, and still uphold academic standards that support timely, high-quality doctoral completion.

Based on student enrollment, Adjunct Faculty may be invited to instruct content courses or research methodology courses, which they are credentialed to teach. Participation in Mentor Training will be provided and required.

Key performance indicators of faculty include:

• · Embracing diverse, process-learning approaches resulting in outcomes of academic quality and integrity.
• · Knowledge of an inquiry-action model of education fostering applied research, discovery, and critical thinking that results in curiosity, lifelong learning, and positive contributions to societal wellbeing.
• · Prioritizing student engagement through weekly substantive, content-based and motivational discussion posts to the classroom.
• · Building collaborative, collegial, and positive relationships and communications with other faculty members.
• · Supporting students where they are and as individuals who are balancing challenges at home and work.

Availability

Adjunct faculty should be reasonably accessible to their students. Faculty members are expected to be available to students outside of the online asynchronous course discussion board. In addition to providing substantive feedback on student submissions, faculty members will publish their availability to students through course syllabi, instructor information in the classroom, or other appropriate documents.

Course Capstone Research Mentoring and Teaching

Discussion Boards for classrooms are open 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Although postings to the classroom may be done at any time of day, postings and responses must be completed in a timely manner in accordance with the Faculty Handbook or other criteria established by Walden University and the program to which they are assigned. As such,

Adjunct Faculty members are expected to be in classrooms for a minimum of 4 days per week and post responses to students’ questions within 48 hours. Faculty Members are required to verify the quality of student submissions, and to provide feedback and grades to students through the online classroom.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:

• Terminal degree in Business Administration (PhD, DBA) or a related field from an accredited institution is required.
• Proof of teaching and mentoring business doctoral students in an online instructional setting at the graduate level for at least 1 year.
• Demonstrate ongoing engagement in scholarly and professional business activities within the past 5 years and exhibits proficiency in APA 7th edition formatting and citation standards.
• Strong research methodology background in quantitative and qualitative methods in research (preference given to quantitative). Excellent leadership, communication, team, and human relation skills.

Technology Requirements:

• Adjunct faculty provide their own laptops and are expected to use the Walden University Learning Management System and the Microsoft 365 tools with their assigned Walden email addresses in their Walden activities. Walden University provides a Walden e-mail account and access to the learning platform, password-protected faculty sections of the website, university and college cloud services, and other faculty communications tools.
• The Faculty Member must be able to use Microsoft Office products (MS Word, MS Excel, and MS PowerPoint), zip software, and Adobe Acrobat and must have reliable Internet access as well as alternate access in cases where primary access becomes unavailable.

In support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected compensation rate for this position is as follows:

• Graduate Course Instruction: $1,560 - $4,080 per Quarter or Semester, depending on type of course taught and length of course
• Undergraduate Course Instruction: $700 - $2,200 per quarter, depending on type of course taught and length of course Actual pay may be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as type of course taught; experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. Walden also offers other opportunities for its contributing faculty members, such as dissertation/doctoral study committee chair positions, research reviewing, and dissertation and doctoral study mentoring. Our Talent Acquisition Team will be happy to answer any questions you may have, and we look forward to learning more about your salary requirements.

jobs.title: Financial Systems Admin
jobs.description:
KAYAK, part of Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), is a leading travel search engine. With billions of queries across our platforms, we help people find their perfect flight, stay, rental car and vacation package. We're also transforming business travel with a new corporate travel solution, KAYAK for Business.

As an employee of KAYAK, you will be part of a travel company that operates a portfolio of global metasearch brands including Momondo, Cheapflights and HotelsCombined, among others. From start-up to industry leader, innovation is in our DNA and every employee has an opportunity to make their mark. Our focus is on building the best travel search engine to make it easier for everyone to experience the world.

KAYAK is looking for a NetSuite / Salesforce / FloQast Administrator to join our Enterprise Applications team within Finance. You'll be the day-to-day owner of configuration, user administration, and integration health across our core finance and revenue systems — the person who actually knows why a saved search broke, why a workflow stalled, or why a sync between NetSuite and Salesforce didn't fire. This role rewards curiosity and precision: you don't need to arrive as a NetSuite expert, but you do need to want to become one, and you need to be the kind of person who double-checks a config change before it touches production. You'll work closely with Finance, Accounting, Sales Ops, and Engineering, and partner with senior systems analysts and architects on the bigger roadmap items — but the daily craft of keeping these systems accurate, well-documented, and running smoothly is yours.

This role will be required to work from our Concord, MA or Cambridge, MA office at least 3 days per week.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Administer day-to-day configuration of NetSuite, Salesforce, FloQast and Blackline: user setup/deactivation, roles and permissions, saved searches, SuiteAnalytics workbooks/dashboards, Salesforce flows and validation rules, troubleshooting issues within Salesforce.

 - Serve as backup administrator for Expensify, supporting user provisioning, system configuration, synchronization issues, and end-user troubleshooting

 - Build and maintain NetSuite SuiteFlow workflows and troubleshoot existing SuiteScript customizations — you don't need to write scripts from scratch on day one, but you should be comfortable reading one, tracing what it does, and knowing when to escalate to a developer.

 - Triage and resolve support tickets from Finance and general employees related to expense reports, financial records, and account access, digging into root cause rather than just closing the ticket.

 - Monitor and troubleshoot integrations between NetSuite and Salesforce — including iPaaS/middleware tools and direct API/SFTP data feeds — escalating to engineering when needed.

 - Support month-end and quarter-end close by ensuring system data accuracy, running reports, and resolving reconciliation discrepancies.

 - Support the month-end close by managing file-based data transfers to the external reporting platform, validating successful loads, and troubleshooting exceptions with the Reporting team

 - Perform sandbox testing and validate NetSuite's release upgrades against existing customizations and integrations before anything touches production.

 - Maintain user access lists and perform basic access reviews to support audit, SOX, and compliance needs.

 - Create and maintain clear documentation, quick-reference guides, and training materials — you take pride in writing something a new teammate could actually follow without asking you a follow-up question.

 - Partner with senior systems analysts/architects to implement approved process changes and provide hands-on support during testing and hypercare for larger rollouts, without owning roadmap prioritization.




PLEASE APPLY IF YOU HAVE:

 - 2-4 years of hands-on administration experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and/or Expensify (or similar ERP/CRM/expense platforms) — OR strong ERP/CRM administration fundamentals elsewhere plus genuine enthusiasm for going deep on NetSuite specifically. We'd rather hire for curiosity and a learning mindset than a perfect checklist of prior tools.

 - Familiarity with (or eagerness to quickly learn) NetSuite's configuration layer: saved searches, SuiteFlow, roles/permissions, custom fields and records, and at least reading-level comfort with SuiteScript.

 - Working knowledge of basic system integrations (API/SFTP, or iPaaS tools like Celigo/Workato/Boomi) and comfort troubleshooting data sync issues.

 - Real attention to detail — the kind that notices a saved search is returning one extra row before it becomes a finance reporting problem.

 - Solid Excel/Google Sheets skills; comfort building reports and saved searches.

 - Clear communicator who can support non-technical end users and explain system issues in plain language.

 - Familiarity with basic finance/accounting workflows (AP, expense management, order-to-cash) is a plus but not required.

 - Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience; NetSuite/Salesforce admin certifications (e.g. NetSuite SuiteFoundation, Salesforce Administrator) are a plus and a good signal of the self-directed learning this role rewards.




BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year.

 - Company-wide week off a year – the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

 - No meeting Fridays

 - Paid parental leave

 - Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday

 - Paid volunteer time

 - Focus on your career growth:

 - Development Dollars

 - Leadership development

 - Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

 - Travel Discounts

 - Employee Resource Groups

 - Competitive retirement and health plans

 - Free lunch 2 days per week

 - Focus on mental health and well-being:

 - Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth

 - Company-paid subscription to HeadSpace

There are a variety of factors that go into determining a salary range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought/required. The range for this Massachusetts-based role is $85,000-$100,000.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus.

 


INCLUSION

At KAYAK, we want everyone to have the space to grow, share ideas and do great work. That's why we're focused on hiring the best talent from all walks of life and experiences, supporting them well and making sure no one feels like they have to fit a mold to belong here.

Need any adjustments for the interview, application or on the job? No problem – just give us a heads-up. We've got you.

#LI-AS1

jobs.title: Senior Analyst, Compensation & Analytics
jobs.description:
About the role

We are looking for a sharp, analytically-driven Sr. Analyst to join Forter's Total Rewards team as a compensation professional. You will own our compensation operations, including job architecture, market pricing of new roles, and end-to-end delivery of recurring programs like our comp cycles.

You will also partner with HR, Finance, and functional stakeholders to support hiring, retention, and career growth through clear compensation guidance. This role reports to the Sr. Director of Total Rewards.

What you'll be doing

• Compensation Operations & Cycles: Own our global compensation operations and recurring programs end-to-end, including the main and secondary comp cycles, promotions, and bonus payouts: timelines, budgets, Aeqium configuration, manager guidance, and post-cycle reporting.

• Job Architecture: Manage and evolve our job architecture, including job profiles, leveling criteria, and grade structures, so it scales with the business and supports consistent pay decisions.

• Market Pricing: Price new and evolving roles using Radford and other survey data, maintain job matches, support the annual range refresh, and turn findings into clear recommendations.

• Business Partnering: Advise People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and functional leaders on offers, promotions, retention, and leveling, with defensible guidance grounded in Forter's compensation philosophy.

• Analytics & Reporting: Build and maintain recurring compensation and headcount reporting, and help Finance track compensation budgets.

• Education & Continuous Improvement: Develop training materials and comp education for managers and People Partners, and keep improving our processes and documentation to make programs more scalable.

• AI-Enabled Ways of Working: We expect you to use AI tools (e.g., Claude, Glean, Gemini) in your day-to-day work to automate analysis, reporting, and documentation, and to continually find new ways to scale the team's impact with AI.

What you'll need

• 3–5 years of progressive compensation experience, ideally in a tech or high-growth environment.

• Background supporting multiple functions and global populations, with hands-on job architecture and leveling experience.

• Experience owning compensation programs such as salary reviews, promotion cycles, and bonus plans, with strong process ownership and attention to data integrity.

• Hands-on market pricing experience using Radford (or similar) and the ability to translate findings into clear narratives.

• Strong analytical skills: advanced Excel, compensation modeling, and workforce analytics. Experience with HRIS and comp planning tools (e.g., HiBob, Aeqium) is a plus.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to partner with and influence People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, Glean, Gemini) to automate analysis, reporting, and documentation, and genuine curiosity about applying them to compensation work.

• Collaborative, solutions-oriented approach, with the ability to bring structure to ambiguity and make programs better over time.

About us:

Commerce is evolving faster than the systems built to support it. Agentic AI is redrawing how people buy. Customer expectations have a new ceiling. And bad actors are evolving alongside every advancement.

Forter was built to meet this moment — and stay ahead of it.

We are a human-first, AI-built company. Our technology analyzes patterns across a network of over 2 billion shoppers, delivering identity intelligence across the entire commerce journey — from sign-up to checkout to returns — that protects revenue and unlocks great customer experiences simultaneously. With Forter, businesses know who to trust, whether it’s humans or the agents shopping for them. The result: zero friction for the customers who matter. No revenue left behind.

The world's most trusted brands — Nordstrom, Instacart, Priceline, Adobe, ASOS, and eBay among them — rely on Forter to get this right. Since 2013, we've raised $525M from investors including Tiger Global, Bessemer, Sequoia Capital, and Salesforce Ventures, and today we power commerce decisions for nearly 1 million businesses globally. We're more than fraud, payments and orchestration – we make trust a competitive advantage.

Trust is backed by data –  Forter is a recipient of over 10 workplace and innovation awards, including:

Life as a Forterian:

Forterians are, genuinely, some of the best people you'll work with. Smart, curious, and deeply good humans who care about the work and each other. That's not an accident — it's something we've been intentional about since day one, and it's the thing people mention most when they talk about why they stay. When you're surrounded by people like this, doing work that actually matters, it changes what a job can feel like.

Forter was built on a simple but powerful conviction: when AI does its job, humans can do theirs better. That philosophy shapes our products and shapes how we work. AI is core to our workflows — not as a shortcut, but as a force multiplier that gives Forterians the space to focus their energy where human judgment is irreplaceable.

We're a global team of 500+ people, with regional headquarters in New York, Tel Aviv, London, and Singapore, and employee presence across the US, Canada, Germany, France, Japan, China, and Australia. Our teams are cross-functional by design, and the work you do here is visible, consequential, and connected to the outcomes that matter.

You'll have real ownership here and proximity to decisions. And we back that with investment in your growth — RSU offerings, L&D programs built around AI tools, and a culture of recognition rooted in our 4.5 day weeks (aka Forter’s Appreciation Fridays and Sundays). From team outings to local cultural celebrations, we mark the moments that matter — wherever you are in the world. We don't want Forter to be just another job. We want it to be the place you build.

If you're ready to work on a problem that sits at the intersection of AI, commerce, and human trust, this is it.

jobs.title: C++ Developer – ETF Technology & Infrastructure
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Director of Performance Marketing
jobs.description:
Role Summary

Empower Brands is seeking a Director of Performance Marketing to help build and lead a centralized franchisee growth capability across our portfolio of brands.

This role will oversee paid media strategy, platform and partner management, franchisee performance reporting, and the ongoing evolution of services that support local lead generation and conversion. The leader will work across brand teams, digital marketing, finance, operations, and franchisee stakeholders to create a more consistent and scalable approach to local marketing execution.

The ideal candidate brings strong performance marketing experience, an agency or multi-location background, and the ability to translate strategy into practical, measurable programs. This person should be comfortable operating in a growing environment, working cross-functionally, and remaining close to execution as the capability develops.

The role reports to the Chief Marketing Officer and partners closely with the Senior Director of Digital and Marketing Operations.

Location: Richmond, VA

What This Role Will Build

The initial portfolio of growth products and services is expected to include:

• In-house paid-media execution, including: Google Search, Local Services Ads, Display, YouTube, and other Google advertising capabilities Meta advertising

• Localized campaign landing pages

• Franchisee-facing dashboards and reporting

• Call-tracking integration

• Speed-to-lead tools and workflows

• AI-enabled SMS, voice, and email follow-up

• Lead-management and CRM integrations

• Standardized direct-mail capabilities

• Future franchisee demand-generation and conversion products

The initial priority will be launching and scaling the in-house performance marketing capability. The broader scope will expand as the operating model, technology, and franchisee adoption mature.

Key Responsibilities

Build and Launch the Capability

• Lead the design, implementation, and launch of Empower’s in-house performance marketing capability.

• Translate the strategic vision into a practical operating model, service offering, implementation roadmap, and franchisee experience.

• Lead platform implementation, configuration, and ongoing optimization.

• Establish the workflows, standards, service levels, governance, and processes required to scale across multiple franchise brands.

• Partner with Brand Presidents, Marketing, Finance, Legal, IT, Operations, and franchisee leadership groups to prepare for launch.

• Support the onboarding of the franchise brands and franchisee accounts.

• Build the capability in parallel with broader organizational hiring and platform implementation timelines.

Lead Paid-Media Strategy and Initial Execution

• Lead the set up of campaign architecture, account setup, migration, launch, and optimization during the initial build.

• Lead execution across Google Search, Local Services Ads, Display, YouTube, Meta, and other relevant paid channels.

• Establish scalable campaign structures, naming conventions, budget-management practices, tracking standards, and quality controls.

• Evaluate performance by franchisee, territory, market, service line, and channel.

• Ensure that account transitions preserve access, historical data, tracking integrity, and continuity of lead flow wherever possible.

• Develop standards that can later be executed by campaign managers, account managers, platforms, and agency partners.

Own Product and Service Evolution

• Serve as the product owner for Empower’s franchisee growth-products and services ecosystem.

• Develop and maintain a roadmap for MaaS, landing pages, dashboards, speed-to-lead, AI follow-up, and related capabilities.

• Translate franchisee, brand, and business needs into platform requirements and product enhancements.

• Determine which capabilities should be built internally, delivered by vendors, or managed through hybrid operating models.

• Identify opportunities to improve service quality, automation, scalability, and franchisee outcomes.

• Build the playbooks and operating standards that allow the capability to scale across brands.

Manage Platforms, Vendors, and Integrations

• Manage onboarding, service levels, issue resolution, and performance reviews.

• Partner with IT and internal stakeholders on CRM, data, tracking, security, and user-access requirements.

• Ensure that Empower maintains appropriate ownership and administrative access across advertising accounts, landing pages, tracking assets, and performance data.

• Lead the integration of media, CRM, call-tracking, dashboard, billing, and reporting workflows.

Create the Franchisee Service Experience

• Define how franchisees are onboarded, supported, trained, and engaged throughout the MaaS relationship.

• Establish onboarding, stabilization, monthly review, escalation, and performance-management processes.

• Partner with existing Digital Marketing Managers and brand marketing teams on franchisee communications and recurring performance reviews.

Drive Adoption and Change Management

• Develop the adoption and migration strategy for new and existing franchisees.

• Lead account and agency-transition planning in partnership with internal teams.

• Create communications, training, documentation, and escalation paths that support a successful rollout.

• Help establish the participation, exception, and transition framework in partnership with the CMO, Brand Presidents, Legal, and Operations.

Own Commercial and Operating Performance

• Monitor platform fees, internal costs, media funding, billing workflows, and account-level economics.

• Establish adoption, revenue, capacity, service-quality, and performance targets.

• Evaluate MaaS performance based on both service economics and its contribution to franchisee sales and royalty growth.

• Partner with FP&A on forecasting and financial analysis.

Build and Lead the Future Team

• Begin as an individual leader without immediate direct reports.

• Recommend the future team structure based on account volume, complexity, service expectations, and platform capabilities.

• Develop hiring triggers and role definitions for account managers, campaign managers, channel specialists, and related support.

• Hire, train, and lead the future team as the capability scales.

• Create clear accountability between product ownership, account management, campaign execution, brand teams, and external vendors.

Required Experience

• 5+ years experience leading paid-media strategy and execution across Google and Meta.

• Bachelors degree in marketing, advertising, communications, business or a related discipline

• Deep knowledge of Google Search, Local Services Ads, Display, YouTube, Meta, campaign architecture, attribution, and optimization.

• Experience implementing or operating marketing technology, advertising platforms, dashboards, or multi-location marketing systems.

• Experience integrating paid-media execution with CRM, call tracking, landing pages, lead routing, and reporting.

• Demonstrated experience building a new service, capability, operating model, or internal agency function from the ground up.

• Strong change-management experience across complex stakeholder groups.

• Experience selecting, negotiating with, and managing agencies, technology vendors, and platform partners.

• Ability to personally execute campaigns and platform work during the initial build.

• Ability to move between strategy, product design, operations, technology, campaign execution, and stakeholder management.

• Experience building business cases and contributing to pricing, packaging, budget, and service-economics decisions.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate data into actions and business recommendations.

• Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in an entrepreneurial, evolving, and highly visible environment.

Preferred Experience

• Franchise marketing experience.

• Multi-location or distributed marketing experience.

• Agency leadership or agency operations experience.

• Experience supporting multiple brands through a shared platform or centralized operating model.

• Product-management or product-ownership experience.

• Experience in home services or another locally driven service category.

• Experience in a private-equity-backed organization.

• Experience scaling capabilities through periods of rapid growth and organizational change.

• Familiarity with franchise agreements, required marketing programs, local advertising requirements, and franchisee advisory structures.

• Experience with speed-to-lead, conversational AI, automated follow-up, or lead-conversion platforms.

The estimated compensation range for this position is $150,000 to $175,000 annually. Actual compensation for the position is based on a variety of factors, including, but not limited to years of experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.

WHO WE ARE:

Empower Brands is a leading franchise organization encompassing ten industry-leading brands across residential and commercial services: Archadeck Outdoor Living, Bumble Roofing, Canopy Lawn Care, Conserva Irrigation, FRSTeam, JAN-PRO, Koala Insulation, Outdoor Lighting Perspectives (OLP), Superior Fence and Rail, and Wallaby Windows. Empower is dedicated to providing its customers with the highest quality products and services in the home and commercial services industries while simultaneously delivering its franchise owners committed personal support, tools and empowerment to pursue their own success. Empower Brands is a portfolio company of MidOcean Partners, a leading private equity firm with an excellent track record investing in successful, growth-focused franchise businesses. For more about Empower Brands, visit EmpowerFranchising.com.

Note:

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) incumbent in this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. The requirements listed in this document are the minimum levels of knowledge, skills, or abilities. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an “at will” relationship.

Empower Brands is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. jobs.title: Product & Collections Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

ELOVA is a fast-growing, direct-to-consumer jewelry brand with 100K+ customers and 1,000+ reviews with a strong rating. We are a small team of about 12 people, led by three founders, and we build the brand in a serious, premium way.

We sell online, launch new products at a high pace, and learn quickly from what our customers buy and love. Now we are building our product & design department from the ground up.




THE ROLE

You will be one of the first people on our product side and shape what ELOVA sells. You decide which products we launch, create variations of what works, and build our collections, hands-on from first idea to live product.

There is no large team to hand parts of the work to, and that is the point: you see the whole process, take real responsibility, and learn fast what works and what doesn't. Supply chain and production are handled by the founders, so you can focus on product and collections. Together with you, we will build the full role and the product & design department around it.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Choose which products we sell, from supplier proposals and our own ideas, based on trends, your feeling for fashion and what our customers buy.

 - Create variations of our best sellers: new colours, materials, shapes and combinations that keep the range fresh.

 - Build our collections: decide what belongs together, how a collection tells a story and when it goes live.

 - Follow trends and other brands closely, and bring new ideas to the team.

 - List new products in Shopify, so you see your work go live from start to finish.

 - Help shape the product & design department as it grows.


WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You are very creative and have a strong feeling for fashion and jewelry.

 - You want to build a career in fashion and are excited to grow with a fast-growing, high-volume brand.

 - You have a fashion-related education or are close to finishing one, for example, fashion design, fashion management, or product development.

 - You like to work hands-on and enjoy doing the whole process yourself, including practical tasks like listing products.

 - You work independently, take ownership, and are not afraid to share your ideas.

 - You speak and write English fluently.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with jewelry or accessories, through studies, an internship, a job, or your own projects.

 - A portfolio or social media account where you share your creative work.

 - Experience with Shopify or another e-commerce platform.

 - Experience in a product, buying, or design role at a fashion or lifestyle brand.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - A real job, not an internship: full-time (40 hours), with part-time possible from 24 hours per week.

 - €3,000 gross per month for a full-time position, as a starting salary.

 - 25 days of paid leave, plus 8% holiday pay (vakantiegeld) for positions in the Netherlands.

 - An employment contract, starting with a temporary contract.

 - Fully remote work.

 - The chance to build ELOVA's product & design department from day one, with real responsibility, real impact, and plenty of room to grow in role and salary.

 - Your designs and collections going live for 100K+ customers.

 - Start as soon as possible.

jobs.title: Windows System Administrator (Senior-Level)
jobs.description:
Link Solutions is seeking a Windows System Administrator (Senior-Level) to join our team at Adelphi, MD.

• U.S. Citizen
• Active Top Secret Clearance required
• IAT Level II Certification equivalent or higher
• Non-remote (relocation assistance available)

The Windows System Administrator will support mission-critical information systems at the Army Research Laboratory (ARL). In this role, you will be responsible for the administration, security, maintenance, and optimization of Windows-based infrastructure supporting a globally distributed enterprise environment. You will work closely with IT, Cybersecurity, and operational teams to ensure the availability, performance, and security of systems supporting research and national defense initiatives.

This position offers the opportunity to work with advanced Microsoft technologies, enterprise-scale infrastructure, cybersecurity frameworks, and Department of Defense systems while directly contributing to innovative research and critical national security missions.

Job Responsibilities:

• Administer, maintain, and optimize Windows Server operating systems in enterprise and classified environments.
• Manage and support Microsoft Active Directory, Group Policy Objects (GPOs), DNS, DHCP, and enterprise authentication services.
• Administer Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM/SCCM) and endpoint management solutions.
• Install, configure, maintain, and secure Windows operating systems, server platforms, and enterprise applications.
• Develop and maintain PowerShell scripts to automate system administration tasks and improve operational efficiency.
• Perform patch management, system updates, and software deployments in accordance with DoD and cybersecurity requirements.
• Implement and maintain Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and security hardening standards.
• Monitor system performance, analyze trends, and troubleshoot hardware, software, and operating system issues.
• Plan, implement, and test backup and recovery procedures to ensure system resiliency and data integrity.
• Conduct routine security audits, vulnerability remediation, and compliance assessments.
• Collaborate with Cybersecurity teams to support vulnerability scanning, risk mitigation, and accreditation efforts.
• Support incident response activities and assist with troubleshooting complex system and network issues.
• Maintain detailed technical documentation, system configurations, standard operating procedures, and architecture diagrams.
• Participate in infrastructure modernization initiatives and technology refresh projects.
• Work with government stakeholders to identify requirements, improve services, and implement innovative IT solutions.
• Provide Tier III escalation support and technical leadership for systems administration activities.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job.

Compensation Range:

• $120,000 - $140,000
• Full-Time (Monday-Friday)

Several factors influence final compensation, including relevant experience, technical expertise, certifications, and education.

• U.S. Citizen.
• Active Top Secret Clearance.
• IAT Level II certification or higher in accordance with DoD 8570/8140 requirements (Security+ CE, SSCP, GSEC, CCNA Security, or equivalent).
• Bachelor's degree with seven (7) years of relevant experience; OR ten (10) years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
• Extensive experience administering Windows Server environments in enterprise settings.
• Experience supporting Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, and enterprise Windows infrastructure.
• Experience implementing and maintaining STIG compliance and security hardening standards.
• Experience performing system patching, vulnerability remediation, and configuration management.
• Experience utilizing PowerShell for automation and administration.
• Knowledge of DoD cybersecurity policies and RMF.
• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred:

• Experience with Nutanix administration and virtualization platforms.
• Experience configuring and administering IIS (Internet Information Services).
• Experience retrieving, applying, and validating STIGs.
• Experience using STIG Viewer, SCAP Compliance Checker, and EvaluateSTIG.
• Experience implementing and supporting Windows Server solutions through deployment and sustainment phases.
• Experience installing, configuring, and supporting COTS/GOTS applications.
• Experience supporting Linux-to-Windows migration projects.
• Working knowledge of Linux administration and command-line operations.
• Experience troubleshooting custom-developed applications.
• Experience with MECM/SCCM administration.

Link Solutions Inc. offers a competitive compensation and benefits package to include paid holidays, paid time off, medical, dental, vision, company-paid long and short-term disability, life insurance, referral bonuses, relocation incentive program, certification reimbursement program, retirement, and more.

Link Solutions, Inc. is an EOE. AA/M/F/D/V. We participate in the E-Verify Employment Verification Program. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
